能建立 perpendicular line 求 foot of perpendicular
能求 two-plane intersection、skew-line distance 和 common perpendicular

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Equations of a plane
过点 \(A\)，位置向量为 \(\mathbf a\)，并包含两个不平行方向 \(\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) 的平面可写成
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b+\mu\mathbf c}.
\]
若 \(\mathbf n\) 是平面的 normal vector，则
\[
(\mathbf r-\mathbf a)\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=0,
\]
即
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p},\;
p=\mathbf a\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n.
\]
若 \(\mathbf n=(a,b,c)\)，Cartesian form 为
\[
\boxed{ax+by+cz=d}.
\]
从 parametric form 转换时，可用 \(\mathbf b\times\mathbf c\) 求 normal；也可消去 \(\lambda,\mu\)。


1.2 A line and a plane
设直线
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf d
\]
和平面 \(\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\)。

若 \(\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n\ne0\)，直线与平面有唯一交点；
若 \(\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=0\)，直线平行于平面；
在平行情形下，若 \(\mathbf a\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\)，则整条直线位于平面内。

求交点时，把直线的 \(x,y,z\) 参数式代入平面方程，先求参数，再代回直线。


1.3 Foot of a perpendicular and distance to a plane
从点 \(P\) 到平面 \(\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=p\) 的垂线方向为 \(\mathbf n\)。先写
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf p_0+t\mathbf n,
\]
再与平面联立，所得交点 \(M\) 是 foot of the perpendicular，距离为 \(|PM|\)。
对于平面 \(ax+by+cz=d\) 和点 \((x_0,y_0,z_0)\)，距离公式为
\[
\boxed{
D=\frac{|ax_0+by_0+cz_0-d|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}
}.
\]


1.4 Angle between a line and a plane
若直线方向为 \(\mathbf d\)，平面 normal 为 \(\mathbf n\)，直线与平面的锐角为 \(\alpha\)，则
\[
\boxed{
\sin\alpha=\frac{|\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n|}{|\mathbf d|\,|\mathbf n|}
}.
\]
这里使用 \(\sin\alpha\)，因为直线与平面的角与 \(\mathbf d\)、\(\mathbf n\) 之间的角互余。


1.5 Intersection and angle of two planes
两个不平行平面的交集是一条直线。可用两种方法求交线：

令一个坐标为参数，联立两个 Cartesian equations；
取两平面的 normals \(\mathbf n_1,\mathbf n_2\)，则交线方向平行于 \[\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2,\] 再求交线上的一个点。

两平面的锐角等于其 normals 的锐角：
\[
\boxed{
\cos\theta=\frac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}
{|\mathbf n_1|\,|\mathbf n_2|}
}.
\]
所有包含平面 \(\pi_1:f_1=0\) 与 \(\pi_2:f_2=0\) 的公共交线的平面可写成
\[
pf_1+qf_2=0,
\]
其中 \(p,q\) 不同时为零。


1.6 Vector product
对于
\[
\mathbf a=(a_1,a_2,a_3),\;
\mathbf b=(b_1,b_2,b_3),
\]
\[
\boxed{
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=
\begin{pmatrix}
a_2b_3-a_3b_2\\
a_3b_1-a_1b_3\\
a_1b_2-a_2b_1
\end{pmatrix}
}.
\]
\(\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\) 同时垂直于 \(\mathbf a\) 和 \(\mathbf b\)，方向由 right-hand rule 决定，且
\[
|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|=|\mathbf a|\,|\mathbf b|\sin\theta.
\]
因此平行四边形面积为 \(|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|\)，三角形面积为其一半。向量积满足
\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=-(\mathbf b\times\mathbf a).
\]


1.7 Distances involving lines
点 \(P\) 到直线 \(\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf d\) 的距离可写成
\[
\boxed{
D=\frac{|(\mathbf p-\mathbf a)\times\mathbf d|}{|\mathbf d|}
}.
\]
两条 skew lines
\[
\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b,\;
\mathbf r=\mathbf c+\mu\mathbf d
\]
的共同垂直方向为 \(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d\)。最短距离为
\[
\boxed{
D=\frac{|(\mathbf c-\mathbf a)\boldsymbol\cdot(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d)|}
{|\mathbf b\times\mathbf d|}
}.
\]
若要求 common perpendicular 的方程，可分别取两线上一般点 \(P,Q\)，令 \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) 同时垂直于 \(\mathbf b\) 和 \(\mathbf d\)，解出两个参数后用 \(P\) 或 \(Q\) 与方向 \(\mathbf b\times\mathbf d\) 写直线。

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
2. Textbook Examples
本节保留教材 Chapter 7 的全部编号 Example。题意与符号按教材重写，步骤展开到可直接复习的方法层级。

Find the equation of the plane through \(A(4,2,0)\), \(B(3,1,1)\) and \(C(4,-1,1)\).






提示Solution





Two independent directions in the plane are
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix},\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence a parametric equation is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-1\\1\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}0\\-3\\1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Thus \(x=4-\lambda\), \(y=2-\lambda-3\mu\) and \(z=\lambda+\mu\). Eliminating \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\) gives
\[
\boxed{2x+y+3z=10}.
\]





Write down the equation of the plane through \((2,1,3)\) whose normal is \(4\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+6\mathbf k\).






提示Solution





With \(\mathbf a=(2,1,3)\) and \(\mathbf n=(4,5,6)\),
\[
(\mathbf r-\mathbf a)\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=0.
\]
Therefore \(4(x-2)+5(y-1)+6(z-3)=0\), so
\[
\boxed{4x+5y+6z=31}.
\]





Find the point where
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-1\end{pmatrix}
\]
meets the plane \(5x+y-z=1\).






提示Solution





A point of the line has coordinates \((2+\lambda,3+2\lambda,4-\lambda)\). Substitution gives
\[
5(2+\lambda)+(3+2\lambda)-(4-\lambda)=1,
\]
so \(9+8\lambda=1\) and \(\lambda=-1\). The point of intersection is
\[
\boxed{(1,1,5)}.
\]





Show that the line
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\\-2\end{pmatrix}
\]
is parallel to the plane \(2x+4y+5z=8\).






提示Solution





The direction of the line is \(\mathbf d=(3,1,-2)\) and a normal to the plane is \(\mathbf n=(2,4,5)\). Since
\[
\mathbf d\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n=3(2)+1(4)-2(5)=0,
\]
the line direction is perpendicular to the normal. Hence the line is parallel to the plane.





Determine whether the line in Example 7.4 lies in the plane \(2x+4y+5z=8\).






提示Solution





Example 7.4 shows that the line is parallel to the plane. For \(t=1\), the point on the line is \((5,2,-2)\), and
\[
2(5)+4(2)+5(-2)=8.
\]
This point belongs to the plane. Therefore the whole line lies in the plane.





\(A\) is \((7,5,3)\) and \(\pi\) is \(3x+2y+z=6\).

Find the line through \(A\) perpendicular to \(\pi\).
Find its intersection \(P\) with \(\pi\).
Find \(AP\).







提示Solution






A normal to \(\pi\) is \((3,2,1)\), so

\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}7\\5\\3\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\\1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

Substitution of \((7+3\lambda,5+2\lambda,3+\lambda)\) into the plane gives

\[
3(7+3\lambda)+2(5+2\lambda)+(3+\lambda)=6.
\]
Thus \(14\lambda=-28\), so \(\lambda=-2\) and
\[
\boxed{P=(1,1,1)}.
\]



\[
\overrightarrow{AP}=\begin{pmatrix}-6\\-4\\-2\end{pmatrix},
\;
AP=\sqrt{36+16+4}=\boxed{\sqrt{56}}.
\]





Find the angle between
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}-1\\2\\5\end{pmatrix}
\]
and the plane \(2x+3y+z=4\).






提示Solution





Take \(\mathbf n=(2,3,1)\) and \(\mathbf d=(-1,2,5)\). If \(A\) is the angle between \(\mathbf n\) and \(\mathbf d\), then
\[
\cos A=\frac{\mathbf n\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf d}{|\mathbf n||\mathbf d|}
=\frac{-2+6+5}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{30}}.
\]
Hence \(A=63.95^\circ\). The angle between the line and the plane is
\[
90^\circ-A=26.05^\circ,
\]
or \(\boxed{26^\circ}\) to the nearest degree.





Find the line of intersection of
\[
3x+2y-3z=-18
\;\text{and}\;
x-2y+z=12.
\]






提示Solution





Putting \(y=0\) gives \(x=3\), \(z=9\), so \(P=(3,0,9)\). Putting \(z=1\) gives \(x=-1\), \(y=-6\), so \(Q=(-1,-6,1)\). Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\-6\\-8\end{pmatrix}
=-2\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore one equation of the common line is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-6\\1\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Equivalent base points and non-zero scalar multiples of the direction vector give the same line.





Find the acute angle between \(\pi_1:2x+3y+5z=8\) and \(\pi_2:5x+y-4z=12\).






提示Solution





The normals are \(\mathbf n_1=(2,3,5)\) and \(\mathbf n_2=(5,1,-4)\). Hence
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{-7}{\sqrt{38}\sqrt{42}}.
\]
This gives \(\theta=100.1^\circ\) between the chosen normals. The acute angle between the planes is therefore
\[
\boxed{180^\circ-100.1^\circ=79.9^\circ}.
\]





Find the plane through \((1,2,3)\) that contains the common line of
\[
\pi_1:2x+2y+z+3=0,
\;
\pi_2:2x+3y+z+13=0.
\]






提示Solution





Every plane in the sheaf through the common line has equation
\[
p(2x+2y+z+3)+q(2x+3y+z+13)=0,
\]
where \(p\) and \(q\) are not both zero. Substitution of \((1,2,3)\) gives
\[
12p+24q=0,
\]
so \(p=-2q\). Therefore
\[
-2(2x+2y+z+3)+(2x+3y+z+13)=0,
\]
and the required plane is
\[
\boxed{2x+y+z=7}.
\]





Find the equation of the common perpendicular to
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+\alpha\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix},
\;
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\1\\4\end{pmatrix}
+\beta\begin{pmatrix}-3\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]






提示Solution





Let
\[
P=(1+\alpha,\alpha,-1),
\;
Q=(-2-3\beta,1,4+\beta).
\]
Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-3-\alpha-3\beta,1-\alpha,5+\beta).
\]
For \(PQ\) to be perpendicular to both given lines,
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(1,1,0)=0,
\;
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(-3,0,1)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
-2\alpha-3\beta-2=0,
\;
3\alpha+10\beta+14=0.
\]
Solving gives \(\alpha=2\), \(\beta=-2\). Hence \(P=(3,2,-1)\), \(Q=(4,1,2)\) and \(\overrightarrow{PQ}=(1,-1,3)\). The common perpendicular is
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]





Let \(\mathbf a=3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+5\mathbf k\) and \(\mathbf b=\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+2\mathbf k\).

Calculate \(\mathbf a\times\mathbf b\).
Hence find a unit vector perpendicular to both \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\).







提示Solution








\[
\mathbf a\times\mathbf b=
\begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\
3&2&5\\
1&-4&2
\end{vmatrix}
=24\mathbf i-\mathbf j-14\mathbf k.
\]

Since \(|\mathbf a\times\mathbf b|=\sqrt{24^2+(-1)^2+(-14)^2}=\sqrt{773}\), one required unit vector is

\[
\boxed{\widehat{\mathbf n}=\frac1{\sqrt{773}}
\begin{pmatrix}24\\-1\\-14\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Its negative is also perpendicular to both vectors.





Find the Cartesian equation of the plane through \(A(3,4,2)\), \(B(2,0,5)\) and \(C(6,7,8)\).






提示Solution





\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-1,-4,3),
\;
\overrightarrow{BC}=(4,7,3).
\]
A normal is
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{BC}
=(-33,15,9)=-3(11,-5,-3).
\]
Use \(\mathbf n=(11,-5,-3)\). The equation is \(11x-5y-3z=d\). Substitution of \(A\) gives \(d=33-20-6=7\). Hence
\[
\boxed{11x-5y-3z=7}.
\]





A plane is
\[
\mathbf r=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+5\mathbf k
+\lambda(5\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k)
+\mu(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k).
\]
Find its Cartesian equation.






提示Solution





A normal is the vector product of the two directions:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}5\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix}
\times
\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\-3\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}5\\17\\9\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathbf r\boldsymbol\cdot(5,17,9)
=(3,-1,5)\boldsymbol\cdot(5,17,9)=43,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{5x+17y+9z=43}.
\]





The line \(l\) is
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}-10\\20\\2\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}5\\4\\3\end{pmatrix}
\]
and \(P=(70,30,22)\). The point \(M\) on \(l\) is closest to \(P\).

Express \(\mathbf m\) and \(\overrightarrow{PM}\) in terms of \(\lambda\).
Show that \(\lambda=10\) and find \(M\).
Verify the value of \(PM\).







提示Solution








\[
\mathbf m=\begin{pmatrix}-10+5\lambda\\20+4\lambda\\2+3\lambda\end{pmatrix},
\;
\overrightarrow{PM}=\begin{pmatrix}-80+5\lambda\\-10+4\lambda\\-20+3\lambda\end{pmatrix}.
\]

At the nearest point, \(PM\) is perpendicular to the line direction \(\mathbf d=(5,4,3)\):

\[
5(-80+5\lambda)+4(-10+4\lambda)+3(-20+3\lambda)=0.
\]
Thus \(50\lambda=500\), so \(\lambda=10\) and
\[
\boxed{M=(40,60,32)}.
\]

\(\overrightarrow{PM}=(-30,30,10)\), hence

\[
PM=\sqrt{900+900+100}=\boxed{10\sqrt{19}}.
\]





Find the shortest distance from \(P(3,5)\) to \(5x-3y+4=0\).






提示Solution





Using the two-dimensional distance formula,
\[
D=\frac{|5(3)-3(5)+4|}{\sqrt{5^2+(-3)^2}}
=\boxed{\frac4{\sqrt{34}}}.
\]
This example is retained because it is a numbered textbook example; the main Further Mathematics vector work uses the corresponding three-dimensional methods.





Find the shortest distance from \((2,4,-2)\) to \(6x-y-3z+1=0\).






提示Solution





\[
D=\frac{|6(2)-4-3(-2)+1|}{\sqrt{6^2+(-1)^2+(-3)^2}}
=\frac{15}{\sqrt{46}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{D=\frac{15}{\sqrt{46}}\approx2.21}.
\]





The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\2\end{pmatrix},
\;
l_2:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\\1\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}-2\\6\\-4\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Show that they are parallel.
Find the shortest distance between them.







提示Solution






The second direction is \(-2\) times the first, so the lines are parallel.
Take \(A=(2,-3,0)\) on \(l_1\) and \(P=(4,2,1)\) on \(l_2\). Then

\[
\overrightarrow{AP}=(2,5,1),
\;
\overrightarrow{AP}\times(1,-3,2)=(13,-3,-11).
\]
Therefore
\[
D=\frac{\sqrt{13^2+(-3)^2+(-11)^2}}{\sqrt{1^2+(-3)^2+2^2}}
=\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{299}{14}}\approx4.62}.
\]





Find the shortest distance between
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}8\\9\\-2\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix},
\;
l_2:\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}6\\0\\-2\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]






提示Solution





Let \(\mathbf a_1=(8,9,-2)\), \(\mathbf a_2=(6,0,-2)\), \(\mathbf d_1=(1,2,-3)\) and \(\mathbf d_2=(1,-1,-2)\). Then
\[
\mathbf a_1-\mathbf a_2=(2,9,0),
\;
\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(-7,-1,-3).
\]
Also
\[
(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)\boldsymbol\cdot(\mathbf a_1-\mathbf a_2)=-23,
\;
|\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2|=\sqrt{59}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{D=\frac{23}{\sqrt{59}}\approx2.99}.
\]

title: 1.6 Vectors
section: 3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
text:
3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
这里只收录教材 Exercise 中明确标注 Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics 9231 来源的题目；标注为 Mathematics 9709 的题目不在本节重复收录。

The lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) have equations
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=8\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k
+\lambda(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j)
\]
and
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-14\mathbf k
+\mu(-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k).
\]
The point \(P\) on \(l_1\) and the point \(Q\) on \(l_2\) are such that \(PQ\) is perpendicular to both lines. Find the position vectors of \(P\) and \(Q\).
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 11 (part question), May/June 2015. The sign of the \(\mathbf k\) term is given here in the form consistent with the original mark scheme and the textbook answer.






提示Answer





Write
\[
P=(8+\lambda,2-2\lambda,3),
\;
Q=(5,3-2\mu,-14+3\mu).
\]
Then
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-3-\lambda,1-2\mu+2\lambda,-17+3\mu).
\]
The two perpendicularity conditions give
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(1,-2,0)=0
\Longrightarrow -5-5\lambda+4\mu=0,
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(0,-2,3)=0
\Longrightarrow -53-4\lambda+13\mu=0.
\]
Solving gives \(\lambda=3\) and \(\mu=5\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\overrightarrow{OP}=11\mathbf i-4\mathbf j+3\mathbf k},
\;
\boxed{\overrightarrow{OQ}=5\mathbf i-7\mathbf j+\mathbf k}.
\]





The plane \(\Pi_1\) has equation
\[
\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\-1\end{pmatrix}
+s\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Find a Cartesian equation of \(\Pi_1\).

The plane \(\Pi_2\) has equation \(2x-y+z=10\).

Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\).
Find an equation of their line of intersection in the form \(\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 8, October/November 2013.






提示Answer






A normal to \(\Pi_1\) is

\[
\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}
\times
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\\-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
x+3y-z=(2)+3(3)-(-1)=12,
\]
so \(\boxed{\Pi_1:x+3y-z=12}\).

Use normals \(\mathbf n_1=(1,3,-1)\) and \(\mathbf n_2=(2,-1,1)\):

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{|2-3-1|}{\sqrt{11}\sqrt6}
=\frac2{\sqrt{66}}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\theta=75.7^\circ}\).

A direction of the common line is

\[
\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2
=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\-7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The point \((6,2,0)\) satisfies both plane equations. Therefore
\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}6\\2\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\\-7\end{pmatrix}}.
\]





The line \(l_1\) passes through \(A(2,3,-5)\) and \(B(8,7,-13)\). The line \(l_2\) passes through \(C(-2,1,8)\) and \(D(3,-1,4)\).

Find the shortest distance between \(l_1\) and \(l_2\).
The plane \(\Pi_1\) passes through \(A,B,D\), and \(\Pi_2\) passes through \(A,C,D\). Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 11, May/June 2014.






提示Answer






Direction vectors are

\[
\mathbf d_1=\overrightarrow{AB}=(6,4,-8),
\;
\mathbf d_2=\overrightarrow{CD}=(5,-2,-4).
\]
Also
\[
\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(-32,-16,-32),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-4,-2,13).
\]
Therefore
\[
D=\frac{|\overrightarrow{AC}\boldsymbol\cdot(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)|}
{|\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2|}
=\frac{256}{48}
=\boxed{\frac{16}{3}}.
\]

Suitable normals are

\[
\mathbf n_1=\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AD}
=(4,-62,-28)=2(2,-31,-14),
\]
\[
\mathbf n_2=\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD}
=(34,49,18).
\]
Thus
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(2,-31,-14)\boldsymbol\cdot(34,49,18)|}
{\sqrt{1161}\sqrt{3881}}
=\frac{1703}{\sqrt{1161\cdot3881}}.
\]
Hence the acute angle is \(\boxed{36.7^\circ}\).





The position vectors of \(A,B,C,D\) are
\[
2\mathbf i+4\mathbf j-3\mathbf k,
\;
-2\mathbf i+5\mathbf j-4\mathbf k,
\;
\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+\mathbf k,
\;
\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+m\mathbf k,
\]
respectively, where \(m\) is an integer. The shortest distance between \(AB\) and \(CD\) is \(3\).

Show that the only possible value of \(m\) is \(2\).
Find the shortest distance of \(D\) from \(AC\).
Show that the acute angle between planes \(ACD\) and \(BCD\) is \(\cos^{-1}(1/3)\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 11, May/June 2012.






提示Answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-4,1,-1),
\;
\overrightarrow{CD}=(0,1,m-1),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,0,4).
\]
Now
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}
=(m,4m-4,-4).
\]
Using the skew-line distance formula,
\[
\frac{|\overrightarrow{AC}\boldsymbol\cdot
(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD})|}
{|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}|}=3.
\]
After squaring,
\[
(m+16)^2=9\{m^2+16(m-1)^2+16\},
\]
which reduces to
\[
19m^2-40m+4=0.
\]
Hence \(m=2\) or \(m=2/19\). Since \(m\) is an integer,
\[
\boxed{m=2}.
\]

With \(m=2\), \(D=(1,5,2)\) and

\[
\overrightarrow{AD}=(-1,1,5),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,0,4).
\]
Therefore
\[
D_{D,AC}=\frac{|\overrightarrow{AD}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|}{|\overrightarrow{AC}|}
=\frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{17}}
=\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{18}{17}}}.
\]

Normals to \(ACD\) and \(BCD\) may be taken as

\[
\mathbf n_1=\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD}=(-4,1,-1),
\]
\[
\mathbf n_2=\overrightarrow{BC}\times\overrightarrow{BD}=(-6,-3,3).
\]
Then
\[
\frac{|\mathbf n_1\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf n_2|}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}
=\frac{18}{\sqrt{18}\sqrt{54}}=\frac13.
\]
Thus the acute angle is
\[
\boxed{\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac13\right)}.
\]

title: 1.6 Vectors
text:
4. Past-paper question bank
完全相同的地区版本合并为一题，并在题目下列出全部来源。答案按 published mark scheme 的得分点展开。

2019

The lines are
\[
l_1:\mathbf r=6\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+7\mathbf k+\lambda(\mathbf i+\mathbf j),
\]
\[
l_2:\mathbf r=4\mathbf i+4\mathbf j+\mu(-6\mathbf j+\mathbf k).
\]
Points \(P\) on \(l_1\) and \(Q\) on \(l_2\) are such that \(PQ\) is perpendicular to both lines. Find their position vectors. [8]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/19 Q3; 9231/12/M/J/19 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





\[
P=(6+\lambda,2+\lambda,7),
\;Q=(4,4-6\mu,\mu),
\]
so
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}=(-2-\lambda,2-\lambda-6\mu,-7+\mu).
\]
The perpendicularity conditions give
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(1,1,0)=0
\Longrightarrow -2\lambda-6\mu=0,
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{PQ}\boldsymbol\cdot(0,-6,1)=0
\Longrightarrow 6\lambda+37\mu=19.
\]
Thus \(\lambda=-3\), \(\mu=1\), and
\[
\boxed{\overrightarrow{OP}=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j+7\mathbf k},
\;\boxed{\overrightarrow{OQ}=4\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k}.
\]





Line \(l_1\) passes through \(A(-3,1,4)\) and \(B(-1,5,9)\). Line \(l_2\) passes through \(C(-2,6,5)\) and \(D(-1,7,5)\).

Find the shortest distance between \(l_1\) and \(l_2\). [5]
Find the acute angle between \(l_2\) and plane \(ABD\). [5]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/19 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,4,5),
\;\overrightarrow{CD}=(1,1,0),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}=(-5,5,-2).
\]
Using \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(1,5,1)\),
\[
D=\frac{|(1,5,1)\boldsymbol\cdot(-5,5,-2)|}{\sqrt{54}}
=\boxed{\frac{18}{\sqrt{54}}=\sqrt6}.
\]

Since \(\overrightarrow{AD}=(2,6,1)\), a normal to \(ABD\) is

\[
(2,4,5)\times(2,6,1)=(-26,8,4)=2(-13,4,2).
\]
For the line direction \((1,1,0)\),
\[
\sin\alpha=\frac{|(1,1,0)\boldsymbol\cdot(-13,4,2)|}{\sqrt2\sqrt{189}}
=\frac9{\sqrt{378}}.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{\alpha=27.6^\circ}\).





With \(O\) as origin, \(A,B,C\) have position vectors \(\mathbf i-\mathbf j\), \(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+7\mathbf k\) and \(\mathbf i-\mathbf j+\mathbf k\).

Find the shortest distance between lines \(OC\) and \(AB\). [5]
Find the Cartesian equation of the plane containing \(OC\) and the common perpendicular of \(OC\) and \(AB\). [4]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/19 Q6; 9231/12/O/N/19 Q6; 9231/13/O/N/19 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






Directions are \(\overrightarrow{OC}=(1,-1,1)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(1,2,7)\). Thus

\[
\overrightarrow{OC}\times\overrightarrow{AB}=(-9,-6,3)=-3(3,2,-1).
\]
Using \(\overrightarrow{OA}=(1,-1,0)\),
\[
D=\frac{|(1,-1,0)\boldsymbol\cdot(3,2,-1)|}{\sqrt{14}}
=\boxed{\frac1{\sqrt{14}}}.
\]

The required plane contains directions \((1,-1,1)\) and \((3,2,-1)\). Its normal is

\[
(1,-1,1)\times(3,2,-1)=(-1,4,5).
\]
It passes through \(O\), so
\[
\boxed{-x+4y+5z=0}.
\]






2020

\(l_1:\mathbf r=(3,0,3)+m(1,4,4)\) and \(l_2:\mathbf r=(3,-5,-6)+n(0,5,6)\).

Find their shortest distance. [5]
A plane \(\Pi\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \((1,0,1)\). Find its Cartesian equation. [4]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/20 Q5; 9231/12/M/J/20 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
(1,4,4)\times(0,5,6)=(4,-6,5),
\]
\[
D=\frac{|(0,-5,-9)\boldsymbol\cdot(4,-6,5)|}{\sqrt{77}}
=\boxed{\frac{15}{\sqrt{77}}}.
\]

A normal is \((1,4,4)\times(1,0,1)=(4,3,-4)\). Hence

\[
\boxed{4x+3y-4z=0}.
\]





\(l_1:\mathbf r=-5\mathbf j+m(5\mathbf i+2\mathbf k)\) and \(l_2:\mathbf r=4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-2\mathbf k+n(\mathbf j+\mathbf k)\). A plane \(\Pi\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \(l_2\).

Find the Cartesian equation of \(\Pi\). [4]
Find the distance between \(l_2\) and \(\Pi\). [3]
Points \(P\) on \(l_1\) and \(Q\) on \(l_2\) make \(PQ\) perpendicular to both lines. Show that \(\overrightarrow{OP}=\frac{55}{27}\mathbf i-5\mathbf j+\frac{22}{27}\mathbf k\) and state an equation of \(PQ\). [8]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/20 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






A normal is \((5,0,2)\times(0,1,1)=(-2,-5,5)\). Thus

\[
\boxed{-2x-5y+5z=25}.
\]

Using \((4,2,-2)\) on \(l_2\),

\[
\boxed{D=\frac{53}{\sqrt{54}}}.
\]

Let \(P=(5m,-5,2m)\) and \(Q=(4,2+n,-2+n)\). From \(PQ\boldsymbol\cdot(5,0,2)=0\) and \(PQ\boldsymbol\cdot(0,1,1)=0\), solving gives \(m=11/27\). Hence the stated \(P\) follows. Since the common perpendicular direction is \((-2,-5,5)\),

\[
\boxed{\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}55/27\\-5\\22/27\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}-2\\-5\\5\end{pmatrix}}.
\]





\(A,B,C\) have position vectors \((-1,1,2)\), \((-2,-1,0)\) and \((2,0,2)\).

Find plane \(ABC\). [5] (b) Find its distance from \(O\). [2] (c) Find the acute angle between planes \(OAB\) and \(ABC\). [4]

Sources: 9231/11/O/N/20 Q4; 9231/13/O/N/20 Q4.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






\(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(-2,-6,7)\), so

\[
\boxed{-2x-6y+7z=10}.
\]

\(\boxed{10/\sqrt{89}}\).
A normal to \(OAB\) is \((2,-4,3)\). Thus

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{41}{\sqrt{29}\sqrt{89}},
\]
so \(\boxed{\theta=36.2^\circ}\).





\(A,B,C\) have position vectors \((-2,2,-1)\), \((-2,1,2)\) and \((0,-2,1)\).

Find plane \(ABC\). [5] (b) Find the acute angle between planes \(OBC\) and \(ABC\). [4]

The point \(D\) has position vector \(t\mathbf i-\mathbf j\). (c) Given that the shortest distance between \(AB\) and \(CD\) is \(\sqrt{10}\), find \(t\). [6]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/20 Q7.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






\(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=2(5,3,1)\), hence

\[
\boxed{5x+3y+z=-5}.
\]

A normal to \(OBC\) is \((5,2,4)\). Therefore

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{35}{\sqrt{35}\sqrt{45}},
\]
giving \(\boxed{\theta=28.1^\circ}\).

\(\overrightarrow{AB}=(0,-1,3)\), \(\overrightarrow{CD}=(t,1,-1)\) and their vector product is \((-2,3t,t)\). Thus

\[
\frac{|(2,-4,2)\boldsymbol\cdot(-2,3t,t)|}{\sqrt{4+10t^2}}=\sqrt{10}.
\]
Squaring reduces to \(80t=24\), so \(\boxed{t=3/10}\).






2021

Let \(t>0\). The line \(l_1\) passes through \(t\mathbf i+\mathbf j\) and is parallel to \(-2\mathbf i-\mathbf j\). The line \(l_2\) passes through \(\mathbf j+t\mathbf k\) and is parallel to \(-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k\). The shortest distance between the lines is \(\sqrt{21}\).

Find \(t\). [5]
The plane \(\Pi_1\) contains \(l_1\) and is parallel to \(l_2\). Write a parametric equation of \(\Pi_1\). [1]
The plane \(\Pi_2\) is \(5x-6y+7z=0\). Find the acute angle between \(l_2\) and \(\Pi_2\). [3]
Find the acute angle between \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\). [3]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/21 Q6; 9231/12/M/J/21 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






A vector joining the base points is \(t(-1,0,1)\), while

The plane \(\Pi\) is \(x+3y+2z=1\).

Find the perpendicular distance from \(O\) to \(\Pi\). [2]

Relative to \(O\), the points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
-\mathbf j+2\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i-\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i-\mathbf j-\mathbf k.
\]

Find the acute angle between planes \(OAB\) and \(\Pi\). [4]

Source: 9231/12/O/N/25 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\boxed{D=\frac1{\sqrt{1^2+3^2+2^2}}=\frac1{\sqrt{14}}}.
\]

A normal to \(OAB\) is

\[
\overrightarrow{OA}\times\overrightarrow{OB}
=(0,-1,2)\times(2,0,-1)=(1,4,2).
\]
The normal to \(\Pi\) is \((1,3,2)\). Therefore
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{|(1,4,2)\boldsymbol\cdot(1,3,2)|}{\sqrt{21}\sqrt{14}}
=\frac{17}{\sqrt{294}}.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{\theta=7.49^\circ}\).





The points \(A,B,C\) have position vectors
\[
3\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+5\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j+2\mathbf k,
\;2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-\mathbf k.
\]

Find the equation of plane \(ABC\). [5]

The point \(D\) has position vector \(\mathbf i-\mathbf j+3\mathbf k\).

Find the shortest distance between lines \(AB\) and \(CD\). [5]

Source: 9231/14/O/N/25 Q4.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer








\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=(-1,-3,-3),
\;
\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,-4,-6),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=(6,-3,1).
\]
Using \(A=(3,5,5)\) gives
\[
\boxed{6x-3y+z=8}.
\]

\(\overrightarrow{CD}=(-1,-2,4)\) and

\[
\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{CD}=(-18,7,-1).
\]
Also \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1,-4,-6)\). Thus
\[
D=\frac{|(-1,-4,-6)\boldsymbol\cdot(-18,7,-1)|}{\sqrt{(-18)^2+7^2+(-1)^2}}
=\boxed{\frac4{\sqrt{374}}\approx0.207}.
\]

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

对不超过 \(3\times3\) 的矩阵进行加、减、乘运算，并识别零矩阵与单位矩阵；
判断方阵是 singular 还是 non-singular，计算 \(2\times2\)、\(3\times3\) 行列式和非奇异矩阵的逆；
使用 \((AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}\)，并推广到多个矩阵的乘积；
用 \(2\times2\) 矩阵表示旋转、反射、放大、伸缩、剪切等平面变换；
理解复合变换的顺序：\(AB\) 表示先作 \(B\)，再作 \(A\)；
使用 \(|\det M|\) 求面积伸缩因子；
求矩阵变换下的不动点与不变直线。

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
学习路线


先检查矩阵阶数，再决定加减或乘法是否有定义
能区分 \(AB\) 与 \(BA\)，并准确解释复合变换顺序
能计算 \(2\times2\)、\(3\times3\) 行列式及逆矩阵
能由单位向量的像写出变换矩阵
能从矩阵识别旋转、反射、伸缩、放大和剪切
能用矩阵方程求不动点，并用直线映射条件求不变直线

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Matrix operations
只有阶数相同的矩阵可以相加或相减。若 \(A\) 为 \(m\times n\)，\(B\) 为 \(n\times p\)，则 \(AB\) 有定义且为 \(m\times p\)。
矩阵乘法一般不满足交换律：
\[
AB\ne BA,
\]
但满足结合律与分配律。单位矩阵 \(I\) 满足 \(AI=IA=A\)，零矩阵记作 \(O\)。


1.2 Determinants and inverses
对于
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
\det A=ad-bc.
\]
若 \(\det A=0\)，则 \(A\) singular，不存在逆矩阵；若 \(\det A\ne0\)，则
\[
A^{-1}=\frac1{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
对 \(3\times3\) 矩阵可按任意一行或一列展开行列式；逆矩阵可由余子式、代数余子式和伴随矩阵求得：
\[
A^{-1}=\frac1{\det A}\operatorname{adj}A.
\]


1.3 Products and inverse order
若 \(A,B\) 均非奇异，
\[
(AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}.
\]
右侧顺序必须反转。对三个矩阵，
\[
(ABC)^{-1}=C^{-1}B^{-1}A^{-1}.
\]


1.4 Matrices as transformations
若
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},
\]
则
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x'\\y'\end{pmatrix}
=M\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
矩阵第一列是 \(\binom10\) 的像，第二列是 \(\binom01\) 的像。常用矩阵包括
\[
R_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix},
\]
以及
\[
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&k\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}1&h\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\k&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]


1.5 Successive transformations and area
若先作 \(B\)、再作 \(A\)，复合矩阵为 \(AB\)。矩阵 \(M\) 所表示变换的面积伸缩因子为
\[
|\det M|.
\]
行列式的符号还反映方向是否翻转。


1.6 Invariant points and lines
不动点 \(\mathbf{x}\) 满足
\[
M\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x},
\]
即 \((M-I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf0\)。
若过原点的直线 \(y=mx\) 在变换后仍映到自身，则方向向量 \(\binom1m\) 的像必须仍与 \(\binom1m\) 平行。对于一般直线 \(y=mx+c\)，应把像点代回同一条直线并比较系数。

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
2. Textbook Examples

Example 1.1 · Page 8
Find
\[
\begin{pmatrix}10&3\\-2&7\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Taking each row against the column gives
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}56\\4\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.2 · Page 9
Find
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\-2&5\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}4&3&0\\-2&-3&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

The product has order \(2\times3\):
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}-2&-6&3\\-18&-21&5\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.3 · Page 9
Multiply
\[
\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\-1&4\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
and state what you notice.


Show solution

\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\-1&4\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Multiplication by the identity matrix has no effect.

 Completed


Example 1.4 · Page 16
Describe the transformations represented by
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

The first matrix interchanges the coordinates, so it is reflection in \(y=x\). The second multiplies both coordinates by \(2\), so it is an enlargement of scale factor \(2\) about the origin.

 Completed


Example 1.5 · Pages 16–18
Find the matrices representing:

reflection in the \(x\)-axis;
enlargement of scale factor \(3\) about the origin.



Show solution

Use the images of \(\binom10\) and \(\binom01\) as the columns:
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}},
\qquad
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]


      xy O    ST(S) reflection in x-axis, then enlargement ×3


Example 1.5: the reflected image lies below the x-axis and every distance from the origin is tripled.



 Completed


Example 1.6 · Pages 19–20
(i) Find the matrix for anticlockwise rotation through \(\theta\) about the origin.
(ii) Hence give the matrix for an anticlockwise rotation through \(60^\circ\).


Show solution

\[
\boxed{R_\theta=
\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{R_{60^\circ}=
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.7 · Pages 21–22
The rectangle has vertices \(A(-1,2)\), \(B(1,2)\), \(C(1,-1)\) and \(D(-1,-1)\). Find its image under
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Multiplying the coordinate matrix gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&1&-1\\2&2&-1&-1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}5&7&-2&-4\\2&2&-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{A'(5,2),\ B'(7,2),\ C'(-2,-1),\ D'(-4,-1)}.
\]


      xy O   originalimage   x-axis fixed; horizontal displacement is proportional to y


Example 1.7: a shear preserves height and area while slanting the vertical sides.



 Completed


Example 1.8 · Pages 23–24
In a shear \(S\), the \(y\)-axis is fixed and \((1,0)\) maps to \((1,5)\). Find the matrix of \(S\).


Show solution

The images of the basis vectors are \(\binom15\) and \(\binom01\), so
\[
\boxed{S=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\5&1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.9 · Pages 29–30
Let \(A,B,C\) represent anticlockwise rotations through \(135^\circ\), \(45^\circ\), \(90^\circ\), respectively.

Write down the matrices.
Verify \(A=BC\).
Calculate \(B^3\) and comment.



Show solution

Using \(R_\theta\) gives the three matrices. Since successive anticlockwise rotations add their angles,
\[
\boxed{BC=R_{45^\circ}R_{90^\circ}=R_{135^\circ}=A},
\]
and similarly
\[
\boxed{B^3=R_{135^\circ}=A}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.10 · Page 33
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(i) Show that \((5,5)\) is invariant. (ii) Find all invariant points.


Show solution

Direct multiplication maps \(\binom55\) to itself. In general,
\[
M\binom{x}{y}=\binom{x}{y}
\]
gives \(2x-y=x\) and \(x=y\). Hence every invariant point lies on
\[
\boxed{y=x}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.11 · Pages 34–35
Find the invariant lines of
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}5&1\\2&4\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Put \(y=mx+c\) and require the image point to satisfy the same equation. Comparing coefficients gives
\[
m^2+m-2=0,
\qquad
(m-3)c=0.
\]
Therefore \(c=0\) and
\[
\boxed{y=x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-2x}.
\]


      xy O    y = x y = −2x points may move, but each whole line maps onto itself


Example 1.11: an invariant line need not be a line of invariant points.



 Completed


Example 6.1 · Page 137
A shape of area \(8\text{ cm}^2\) is transformed by
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\3&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Find the image area.


Show solution

\(\det M=6\), so the area scale factor is \(6\). The image area is
\[
\boxed{48\text{ cm}^2}.
\]

 Completed


Example 6.2 · Pages 137–138
The unit square is transformed by
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\4&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Find its image vertices, \(\det M\), and the image area.


Show solution

The four vertices map to \((0,0),(2,4),(5,5),(3,1)\). Also
\[
\det M=2-12=-10.
\]
Hence the image area is \(\boxed{10}\) square units.


      xy O   SM(S) area image = |det M| × area original


Example 6.2: the determinant gives the signed area factor; its absolute value gives the area scale factor.



 Completed


Example 6.3 · Page 138
Given
\[
P=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Q=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\]
find \(\det P\), \(\det Q\), and \(\det(PQ)\).


Show solution

\[
\det P=2,\qquad \det Q=3,
\]
and
\[
PQ=\begin{pmatrix}5&4\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\det(PQ)=6.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\det(PQ)=\det P\det Q}\).

 Completed


Example 6.4 · Page 142
Write down matrices \(A,B\) for rotations through \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise and clockwise, and find \(AB\).


Show solution

\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{AB=I},
\]
so the two matrices represent inverse transformations.

 Completed


Example 6.5 · Page 144
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}11&3\\6&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(i) Find \(A^{-1}\). (ii) If \(A\) maps \(P\) to \(Q(5,2)\), find \(P\).


Show solution

Since \(\det A=4\),
\[
\boxed{A^{-1}=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-6&11\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Then
\[
A^{-1}\binom52=\binom1{-2},
\]
so \(\boxed{P=(1,-2)}\).

 Completed


Example 6.6 · Page 148
Find the determinant of
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&-4\\7&2&-1\\-2&1&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Expanding along the top row,
\[
\det M
=3\begin{vmatrix}2&-1\\1&3\end{vmatrix}
-4\begin{vmatrix}7&2\\-2&1\end{vmatrix}
=21-44.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{\det M=-23}\).

 Completed


Example 6.7 · Pages 150–151
Find the inverse of
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}2&3&4\\2&-5&2\\-3&6&-3\end{pmatrix}
\]
without a calculator.


Show solution

The determinant is \(-6\). The cofactor matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}3&0&-3\\33&6&-21\\26&4&-16\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Transpose and divide by \(-6\):
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac16
\begin{pmatrix}-3&-33&-26\\0&-6&-4\\3&21&16\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Multiplication verifies \(MM^{-1}=I\).

 Completed

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
4. Past-paper question bank






注记



2019 Paper 1 中检出的矩阵题属于旧考纲的 eigenvalues、diagonalisation 或四维变换，因此不收入本节。以下题目按完全相同的地区版本合并，答案依据对应的 Cambridge mark scheme 整理。



2020



2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 6 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) The transformation represented by \(A^{-1}\) maps a triangle of area \(30\text{ cm}^2\) to a triangle of area \(d\text{ cm}^2\). Find \(d\). [3]
(b) Prove by induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[5]
Let \(B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\33&0\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) The line \(y=2x\) is invariant under the transformation represented by \(A^nB\). Find \(n\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since
\[
\det A=2,\qquad \det(A^{-1})=(\det A)^{-1}=\frac12,
\]
the area scale factor is \(\left|\det(A^{-1})\right|=\frac12\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{d=30\times\frac12=15}.
\]
(b) For \(n=1\),
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^1&0\\2^1-1&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so the statement is true initially. Assume that it is true for \(n=k\), where \(k\) is a positive integer:
\[
A^k=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
A^{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^{k+1}&0\\2^{k+1}-1&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
Thus the statement is true for \(k+1\) whenever it is true for \(k\). Hence, by mathematical induction,
\[
\boxed{A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}}
\]
for every positive integer \(n\).
(c) Using part (b),
\[
A^nB=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n+32&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a general point \((x,y)\),
\[
A^nB\binom xy
=\binom{2^nx}{(2^n+32)x}.
\]
The image has gradient \((2^n+32)/2^n\). Since the invariant line has gradient \(2\),
\[
\frac{2^n+32}{2^n}=2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2^n=32
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{n=5}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2020, Q6; 9231/12/M/J/2020, Q6.





2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}k&0&2\\0&-1&-1\\1&1&-k\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-3&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Show that \(A\) is non-singular. [3]
It is given that
\[
CAB=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Find \(k\). [3]
(c) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(CAB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Expanding along the first row,
\[
\det A
=k\begin{vmatrix}-1&-1\\1&-k\end{vmatrix}
+2\begin{vmatrix}0&-1\\1&1\end{vmatrix}
=k(k+1)+2
=k^2+k+2.
\]
The discriminant of \(k^2+k+2\) is
\[
1^2-4(1)(2)=-7<0.
\]
Since its leading coefficient is positive, \(k^2+k+2>0\) for every real \(k\). Thus \(\det A\ne0\) and \(A\) is non-singular.
(b) First,
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3k\\1&-3\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
and hence
\[
CAB
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&9k+3\\-1&-3k-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Comparing, for example, the top-right entry with the given matrix,
\[
9k+3=-\frac32
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{k=-\frac12}.
\]
(c) The given \(CAB\) maps a point \((x,y)\) to
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}
\binom xy
=\binom{-2x-\frac32y}{-x-\frac32y}.
\]
For the line \(y=mx\), substitute \(y=mx\) and require \(Y=mX\):
\[
-1-\frac32m=m\left(-2-\frac32m\right),
\]
Thus
\[
3m^2+m-2=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(3m-2)(m+1)=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=\frac23x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2020, Q4.





2020 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 1 · 9 marks
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(a,b>0\).
(a) State the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [2]
The unit square is mapped by \(M\) onto parallelogram \(OPQR\).
(b) Find the matrix mapping \(OPQR\) back onto the unit square. [2]
(c) Given that the area of \(OPQR\) is \(2\text{ cm}^2\) and \(x+3y=0\) is invariant, find \(a\) and \(b\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Reading the product from right to left, first apply a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(a\), then a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed, taking \((0,1)\) to \((b,1)\).
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Since \(\det M=a\),
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1a\begin{pmatrix}1&-b\\0&a\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(c) The unit square has area \(1\), so its image has area
\[
|\det M|=a.
\]
As \(a>0\) and the given area is \(2\), \(\boxed{a=2}\). A general point on \(x+3y=0\) can be written as \((x,-x/3)\). Its image is
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{-x/3}
=\binom{ax-\frac13bx}{-\frac13x}.
\]
The image must again satisfy \(X+3Y=0\):
\[
ax-\frac13bx-x=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
1=a-\frac b3.
\]
Using \(a=2\) gives \(\boxed{b=3}\), so \(\boxed{a=2, b=3}\).

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2020, Q1; 9231/13/O/N/2020, Q1.





2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Identify the transformation represented by \(A\). [1]
(b) Identify the transformation represented by \(B\). [2]
Triangle \(DEF\) is transformed by \(AB\) onto triangle \(PQR\).
(c) Show that the two triangles have the same area. [3]
(d) Find the matrix mapping \(PQR\) onto \(DEF\). [2]
(e) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(AB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) \(A\) represents reflection in the line \(y=x\).
(b) Comparing \(B\) with the standard rotation matrix shows that it represents a rotation through \(60^\circ\) anticlockwise about the origin.
(c) Multiplying in the stated order,
\[

\[
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}1&k\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The product in the stated order is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&k\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}k&k\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) A point on the line of invariant points satisfies
\[
M\binom xy=\binom xy.
\]
Thus
\[
kx+ky=x,
\]
while the second coordinate is already unchanged. Since \(k\ne0\),
\[
\boxed{y=\frac{1-k}{k}x}.
\]
(c) The required reverse transformation is represented by
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1k\begin{pmatrix}1&-k\\0&k\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) Since the unit square has area \(1\), the area of \(P\) is
\[
|\det M|=|k|.
\]
Hence
\[
|k|=3k^2.
\]
As \(k\ne0\), division by \(|k|\) gives \(1=3|k|\), so
\[
\boxed{k=\pm\frac13}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2024, Q1; 9231/13/O/N/2024, Q1.





2024 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&1&3\\3&2&5\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Show that \(CAB=\begin{pmatrix}3&-7\\-9&3\end{pmatrix}\). [3]
(b) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(CAB\). [5]
Let \(M=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) Describe the transformation represented by \(M\). [2]
(d) Find \(N\) such that \(NM=CAB\). [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) First,
\[
AB
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&1&3\\3&2&5\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&4\\-1&-1\\-2&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
CAB
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}-2&4\\-1&-1\\-2&0\end{pmatrix}
=\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}3&-7\\-9&3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(b) For \(y=mx\),
\[
\binom XY
=\binom{(3-7m)x}{(-9+3m)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
-9+3m=m(3-7m)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
7m^2=9.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{y=\frac3{\sqrt7}x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-\frac3{\sqrt7}x}.
\]
(c) \(M\) is a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(3\).
(d) Since \(NM=CAB\),
\[
N=(CAB)M^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}3&-7\\-9&3\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1/3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{N=\begin{pmatrix}1&-7\\-3&3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2024, Q4.




2025



2025 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 9 marks
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix},
\qquad 0<\theta<2\pi.
\]
(a) State the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [2]
(b) Find the value of \(\theta\) for which the transformation has a line of invariant points. [7]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Reading the product from right to left, first rotate anticlockwise through \(\theta\) about the origin, then apply a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed and \((0,1)\) mapped to \((2,1)\).
(b) Multiplying gives
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta+2\sin\theta&2\cos\theta-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a line of invariant points there must be a non-zero solution of
\[
M\binom xy=\binom xy.
\]
Equating coordinates gives
\[
(\cos\theta+2\sin\theta-1)x
+(2\cos\theta-\sin\theta)y=0,
\]
\[
\sin\theta\,x+(\cos\theta-1)y=0.
\]
These homogeneous equations have a non-zero solution only when the determinant of their coefficient matrix is zero:
\[
(\cos\theta+2\sin\theta-1)(\cos\theta-1)
-(2\cos\theta-\sin\theta)\sin\theta=0.
\]
Using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) simplifies this to
\[
\sin\theta+\cos\theta=1.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\sqrt2\sin\left(\theta+\frac\pi4\right)=1.
\]
In \(0<\theta<2\pi\), the solutions of \(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=1\) are \(\theta=\pi/2\) and the excluded endpoint \(\theta=0\) (equivalently \(2\pi\)). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\theta=\frac\pi2}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2025, Q4; 9231/12/M/J/2025, Q4.





2025 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 1 · 11 marks
A one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(14\) is followed by a rotation anticlockwise about the origin through \(\pi/3\). Let the combined matrix be \(M\).
(a) Show that
\[
2M=\begin{pmatrix}14&-\sqrt3\\14\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[4]
(b) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(M\). [5]
(c) Find \(M^{-1}\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The stretch and rotation matrices are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since the stretch is performed first,
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}7&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]7\sqrt3&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
\]
and multiplying by \(2\) proves the stated result.
(b) For a point \((x,mx)\),
\[
X=7x-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}mx,
\qquad
Y=7\sqrt3x+\frac12mx.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
\sqrt3m^2-13m+14\sqrt3=0.
\]
The discriminant is \(169-168=1\), so
\[
m=\frac{13\pm1}{2\sqrt3}
=2\sqrt3\quad\text{or}\quad\frac7{\sqrt3}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{y=2\sqrt3x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac7{\sqrt3}x}.
\]
(c) Since \(\det M=14\),
\[
M^{-1}
=\frac1{14}\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]-7\sqrt3&7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1/14&\sqrt3/14\\-\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2025, Q1.





2025 May/June · 9231/14 · Question 5 · 14 marks
A one-way stretch in the \(x\)-direction with scale factor \(3\) is followed by reflection in \(y=x\).
(a) Find the combined matrix \(M\). [3]
(b) Give full details of the transformation represented by \(M^{-1}\). [3]
Let \(N\) satisfy \(MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) Find \(N\). [3]
(d) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(MN\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The stretch and reflection matrices are
\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
F=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The stretch is followed by the reflection, so
\[
\boxed{M=FS
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\3&0\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(b)
\[
M^{-1}=S^{-1}F^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}1/3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/3\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus \(M^{-1}\) represents reflection in \(y=x\), followed by a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(1/3\).
(c) Since \(MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}\),
\[
N=M^{-1}(MN)
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/3\\1&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{N=M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2/3\\1&2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) For \(y=mx\),
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{mx}
=\binom{(1+2m)x}{(3+2m)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
3+2m=m(1+2m)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2m^2-m-3=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(2m-3)(m+1)=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=\frac32x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/M/J/2025, Q5.





2025 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 2 · 11 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\frac32\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\frac32&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Describe the transformation represented by \(A\). [2]
(b) Describe the transformation represented by \(B\). [2]
Triangle \(DEF\) is transformed by \(AB\) onto triangle \(PQR\).
(c) Show that the two triangles have the same area. [2]
(d) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(AB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) \(A\) is a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed and \((0,1)\) mapped to \((3/2,1)\).
(b) \(B\) is a shear with the \(y\)-axis fixed and \((1,0)\) mapped to \((1,3/2)\).
(c) Multiplication gives
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}13/4&3/2\\3/2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det(AB)=1,
\]
Therefore the area scale factor is \(|\det(AB)|=1\), so the two triangles have the same area.
(d) For \(y=mx\),
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}13/4&3/2\\3/2&1\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{mx}
=\binom{(13/4+3m/2)x}{(3/2+m)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
\frac32+m=m\left(\frac{13}{4}+\frac32m\right).
\]
After simplification,
\[
m^2+\frac32m-1=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(m+2)\left(m-\frac12\right)=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{y=-2x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac12x}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2025, Q2; 9231/13/O/N/2025, Q2.





2025 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 10 marks
Let \(k,m\) be non-zero constants and
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&m\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Describe the transformation represented by \(B\) when (i) \(m=1\), and (ii) \(m=k\). [4]
(b) Show that \(ABC\) is singular. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a)(i) When \(m=1\),
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so \(B\) represents a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(k\).
(a)(ii) When \(m=k\),
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&k\end{pmatrix}=kI,
\]
so \(B\) represents an enlargement with centre the origin and scale factor \(k\).
(b) First,
\[
AB
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&m\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}0&m\\-k&m\\k&m\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
ABC=\begin{pmatrix}
m&m&2m\\
-2k+m&k+m&-k+2m\\
2k+m&-k+m&k+2m
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Expanding its determinant and collecting terms gives
\[
m(k+m)(k+2m)-m(-k+m)(-k+2m)-m(-2k+m)(k+2m)
\]
\[
{}+m(2k+m)(-k+2m)+2m(-2k+m)(-k+m)-2m(2k+m)(k+m)=0.
\]
The six expanded terms simplify to
\[
6m^2k+6m^2k-12m^2k=0.
\]
Hence \(\det(ABC)=0\), so \(ABC\) is singular.

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2025, Q4.





2025 October/November · 9231/14 · Question 5 · 14 marks
(a) Show that
\[
\cos\frac\pi{12}=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4},\qquad
\sin\frac\pi{12}=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
[2]
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&-\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Give full details of the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [4]
(c) Write \(M^{-1}\) as the product of two matrices, neither equal to \(I\). [2]
(d) Given that \(y=mx\) is invariant, show that
\[
m^2\sin\frac\pi{12}+2m\cos\frac\pi{12}-\sin\frac\pi{12}=0,
\]
and find \(m\) in the requested cotangent/cosecant form. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(\pi/12=\pi/4-\pi/6\),
\[
\cos\frac\pi{12}
=\cos\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6
+\sin\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6
=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4},
\]
and
\[
\sin\frac\pi{12}
=\sin\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6
-\cos\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6
=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
(b) The matrix factorises as
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&-\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Reading from right to left, first reflect in the \(x\)-axis, then rotate anticlockwise through \(\pi/12\) about the origin.
(c) Reversing the order and inverting each factor gives
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\-\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) Write \(s=\sin(\pi/12)\) and \(c=\cos(\pi/12)\). A point \((x,mx)\) maps to
\[
\binom XY=\binom{(c+ms)x}{(s-mc)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
s-mc=m(c+ms),
\]
so
\[
m^2s+2mc-s=0,
\]
as required. By the quadratic formula,
\[
m=\frac{-2c\pm\sqrt{4c^2+4s^2}}{2s}
=\frac{-c\pm1}{s}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{m=-\cot\frac\pi{12}\pm\operatorname{cosec}\frac\pi{12}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/O/N/2025, Q5.

text:
学习路线

title: 1.2 Rational functions and graphs
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Rational functions
有理函数写成
\[
y=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)},
\]
其中 \(f(x)\) 与 \(g(x)\) 是多项式，且 \(g(x)\ne0\)。本章只讨论分子与分母次数不超过 2 的情形。


1.2 Intercepts and asymptotes
作图时依次确定以下信息。

与坐标轴的交点：令 \(x=0\) 求 \(y\) 轴交点；令分子等于零求 \(x\) 轴交点。
竖直渐近线：函数在 \(g(x)=0\) 处无定义时，检查该点两侧的符号与趋向。
水平渐近线：比较 \(x\to\pm\infty\) 时分子与分母的最高次项。
斜渐近线：当分子的次数比分母高 1 时，作多项式除法，将函数写成

\[
y=ax+b+\frac{r}{g(x)}.
\]
当 \(x\to\pm\infty\) 时，余项趋于零，所以斜渐近线为 \(y=ax+b\)。


1.3 A five-step sketching method
教材使用以下五步作图法：

求图像与坐标轴的交点；
求竖直渐近线，并判断曲线在渐近线两侧趋向 \(+\infty\) 还是 \(-\infty\)；
求水平或斜渐近线，并判断曲线从哪一侧接近；
求驻点；
综合所有信息完成草图。



1.4 Range by the discriminant method
把有理函数方程重新整理为关于 \(x\) 的二次方程。对于给定的 \(y\)，图像上存在实点的条件是
\[
\Delta\ge0.
\]
因此，令 \(\Delta<0\) 可以找出函数不能取得的 \(y\) 值；再结合渐近线是否能够取到端点，即可写出值域。


1.5 Symmetry

若 \(f(x)=f(-x)\)，则 \(f\) 是偶函数，图像关于 \(y\) 轴对称。
若 \(f(x)=-f(-x)\)，则 \(f\) 是奇函数，图像关于原点具有二阶旋转对称性。



1.6 The curve \(y=|f(x)|\)
先画 \(y=f(x)\)，再把其中位于 \(x\) 轴下方的部分关于 \(x\) 轴反射。原图上的根保持不变，但通常在根处形成尖点。


1.7 The curve \(y=f(|x|)\)
保留 \(y=f(x)\) 在 \(x\ge0\) 的部分，再把这一部分关于 \(y\) 轴反射。所得图像一定关于 \(y\) 轴对称。


1.8 The reciprocal curve \(y=1/f(x)\)
由 \(y=f(x)\) 作 \(y=1/f(x)\) 时：

两图在 \(y=1\) 与 \(y=-1\) 处相交；
两图在同一 \(x\) 处符号相同；
\(f(x)=0\) 的根通常变成 \(1/f(x)\) 的竖直渐近线；
\(f(x)\) 的竖直渐近线变成 \(1/f(x)\) 在 \(x\) 轴上的间断点；
若 \(f(x)\to L\ne0\)，则 \(1/f(x)\to1/L\)；
\(f\) 增加时 \(1/f\) 减少，\(f\) 减少时 \(1/f\) 增加。



1.9 The curve \(y^2=f(x)\)
方程等价于
\[
y=\pm\sqrt{f(x)}.
\]
因此：

图像关于 \(x\) 轴对称；
当 \(f(x)<0\) 时没有实点；
与 \(y=f(x)\) 在 \(y=0\) 和 \(y=1\) 处相交；
若 \(f(x)\) 的根不是驻点，\(y^2=f(x)\) 通常竖直穿过 \(x\) 轴；
对应驻点的 \(x\) 坐标不变，而 \(y\) 坐标变为 \(\pm\sqrt{f(x)}\)。

title: 1.2 Rational functions and graphs
text:
2. Textbook examples and examination questions

Textbook Examples


Example 4.1 · Pages 96–97
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{x^2+1}{x^2+2}.
\]
(i) Sketch the graph of \(y=f(x)\).
(ii) State the range of \(f(x)\).
(iii) The equation \(f(x)=k\) has no real solutions. Find the values of \(k\).


Show solution

There are no real zeros of either \(x^2+1\) or \(x^2+2\). Hence the curve has no \(x\)-intercepts and no vertical asymptotes. It passes through
\[
\left(0,\frac12\right).
\]
As \(x\to\pm\infty\),
\[
\frac{x^2+1}{x^2+2}\to1,
\]
so \(y=1\) is a horizontal asymptote, approached from below. Also
\[
f'(x)=\frac{2x}{(x^2+2)^2},
\]
so the only stationary point is the minimum \(\left(0,\frac12\right)\). The graph is symmetrical about the \(y\)-axis.
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac12\le f(x)<1}.
\]
The equation \(f(x)=k\) has no real solutions when
\[
\boxed{k<\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad k\ge1}.
\]



Example 4.1: y = (x² + 1)/(x² + 2)

A minimum at (0, 1/2) and horizontal asymptote y = 1.   Example 4.1: y = (x² + 1)/(x² + 2) -5-4-3-2-1123451xyy = 1(0, ½)


A minimum at (0, 1/2) and horizontal asymptote y = 1.



 Completed


Example 4.2 · Pages 103–104
The graph of \(y=f(x)\) has stationary points
\[
P(-1,-10),\qquad Q(3,5).
\]
Sketch:

\(y=|f(x)|\);
\(y=f(|x|)\).




Example 4.2: given curve y = f(x)

The given curve, redrawn from its stated stationary points.   Example 4.2: given curve y = f(x) -5-4-3-2-112345-12-11-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-112345678xyP(−1, −10)Q(3, 5)


The given curve, redrawn from its stated stationary points.




Show solution

For \(y=|f(x)|\), retain every part of the original curve above the \(x\)-axis and reflect every part below the \(x\)-axis in the \(x\)-axis. In particular, \(P(-1,-10)\) is mapped to \((-1,10)\), while \(Q(3,5)\) is unchanged.
For \(y=f(|x|)\), retain only the original curve for \(x\ge0\) and reflect this part in the \(y\)-axis. Thus \(Q(3,5)\) is accompanied by the reflected stationary point \((-3,5)\); the original left-hand part, including \(P\), is not used.



Example 4.2: transformations

Exercise 4B, Question 4
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{2x^2+x-1}{x-1}.
\]
Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). Show that there is no point on \(C\) for which \(1<y<9\).


Show solution

Since
\[
\frac{2x^2+x-1}{x-1}=2x+3+\frac2{x-1},
\]
the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=1},\qquad\boxed{y=2x+3}.
\]
Rearranging as a quadratic in \(x\) gives
\[
2x^2+(1-y)x+(y-1)=0.
\]
Real \(x\) requires
\[
(1-y)^2-8(y-1)\ge0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(y-1)(y-9)\ge0.
\]
Thus \(y\le1\) or \(y\ge9\), so no point has \(1<y<9\).

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2014.



Exercise 4B, Question 5
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2+px+1}{x-2},
\]
where \(p\) is a constant.

Given that \(C\) has two asymptotes, find the equation of each asymptote.
Find the set of values of \(p\) for which \(C\) has two distinct turning points.
Sketch \(C\) in the case \(p=-1\), indicating the coordinates of any intersections with the axes.



Show solution

Polynomial division gives
\[
y=x+p+2+\frac{2p+5}{x-2}.
\]
Hence the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=2},\qquad\boxed{y=x+p+2}.
\]
Also
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=1-\frac{2p+5}{(x-2)^2}.
\]
There are two distinct turning points precisely when \(2p+5>0\), so
\[
\boxed{p>-\frac52}.
\]
For \(p=-1\),
\[
y=x+1+\frac3{x-2}.
\]
The asymptotes are \(x=2\) and \(y=x+1\). The curve has no \(x\)-intercepts because \(x^2-x+1=0\) has negative discriminant, and its \(y\)-intercept is \(\left(0,-\frac12\right)\).

Show solution

Differentiation gives a stationary-point equation whose discriminant is proportional to \(2-k\). Hence there are no stationary points when
\[
\boxed{k\ge2}.
\]
For \(k=4\),
\[
y=2x+2-\frac2{x+1}.
\]
Therefore the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=-1},\qquad\boxed{y=2x+2},
\]
and the intersections with the axes are
\[
(-2,0),\qquad(0,0).
\]

Exercise 4B, Question 7
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{px^2+4x+1}{x+1},
\]
where \(p\) is a positive constant and \(p\ne3\).

Obtain the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\).
Find the value of \(p\) for which the \(x\)-axis is tangent to \(C\), and sketch \(C\) in this case.
For \(p=1\), show that \(C\) has no turning points, and sketch \(C\), giving the exact coordinates of its intersections with the \(x\)-axis.



Show solution

Division gives
\[
y=px+4-p+\frac{p-3}{x+1},
\]
so the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=-1},\qquad\boxed{y=px+4-p}.
\]
Tangency to the \(x\)-axis requires \(px^2+4x+1=0\) to have a repeated root. Hence
\[
16-4p=0,
\]
so \(\boxed{p=4}\) and the tangent point is \(\left(-\frac12,0\right)\).
For \(p=1\),
\[
y=\frac{x^2+4x+1}{x+1}=x+3-\frac2{x+1}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=1+\frac2{(x+1)^2}>0,
\]
so there are no turning points. The \(x\)-intercepts are
\[
\boxed{\left(-2-\sqrt3,0\right),\quad\left(-2+\sqrt3,0\right)}.
\]

2019 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 10 · 12 marks
Two curvesAsymptotesStationary points
The curves \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) have equations
\[
C_1:\ y=\frac{ax}{x+5},
\qquad
C_2:\ y=\frac{x^2+(a+10)x+5a+26}{x+5},
\]
respectively, where \(a>2\).
(i) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C_1\). [2]
(ii) Find the equation of the oblique asymptote of \(C_2\). [2]
(iii) Show that \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) do not intersect. [2]
(iv) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \(C_2\). [3]
(v) Sketch \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) on a single diagram. You do not need to calculate the coordinates of any points where \(C_2\) crosses the axes. [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Since
\[
\frac{ax}{x+5}=a-\frac{5a}{x+5},
\]
the asymptotes of \(C_1\) are
\[
\boxed{x=-5},\qquad\boxed{y=a}.
\]
(ii) For \(C_2\),
\[
x^2+(a+10)x+5a+26=(x+5)(x+a+5)+1,
\]
so its oblique asymptote is
\[
\boxed{y=x+a+5}.
\]
(iii) Equating the two functions and multiplying by \(x+5\) gives
\[
x^2+10x+5a+26=0.
\]
Its discriminant is
\[
100-4(5a+26)=-4-20a<0,
\]
so the curves do not intersect.
(iv) Since \(C_2\) is \(y=x+a+5+1/(x+5)\),
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=1-\frac1{(x+5)^2}.
\]
Thus the stationary-point equation
\[
x^2+10x+24=0,
\]
hence the stationary points are
\[
\boxed{(-4,a+2),\quad(-6,a-2)}.
\]
The sketch must show the common vertical asymptote \(x=-5\), the stated horizontal/oblique asymptotes, the two stationary points of \(C_2\), and no intersection between the curves.

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2019, Q10; 9231/12/M/J/2019, Q10.





2019 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 6 · 9 marks
Oblique asymptoteStationary points
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2}{kx-1},
\]
where \(k\) is a positive constant.
(i) Obtain the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). [3]
(ii) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \(C\). [3]
(iii) Sketch \(C\). [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Long division gives
\[
\frac{x^2}{kx-1}=\frac{x}{k}+\frac1{k^2}+\frac{1/k^2}{kx-1}.
\]
Hence the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=\frac1k},
\qquad
\boxed{y=\frac{x}{k}+\frac1{k^2}}.
\]
Also
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x(kx-2)}{(kx-1)^2},
\]
so the stationary points are
\[
\boxed{(0,0)},
\qquad
\boxed{\left(\frac2k,\frac4{k^2}\right)}.
\]
The branch containing the origin touches the \(x\)-axis at \((0,0)\); the other branch has its minimum at \(\left(2/k,4/k^2\right)\). Both branches approach the stated asymptotes.

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2019, Q6.

Given asymptoteUnknown constants
The line \(y=2x+1\) is an asymptote of the curve \(C\) with equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2+1}{ax+b}.
\]
(i) Find the values of \(a\) and \(b\). [3]
(ii) State the equation of the other asymptote of \(C\). [1]
(iii) Sketch \(C\), indicating the coordinates of any point of intersection with the \(y\)-axis. You do not need to find the stationary points. [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Write \(x^2+1=(ax+b)(2x+1)+R\). Comparing the coefficients of \(x^2\) and \(x\) gives \(2a=1\) and \(a+2b=0\). Hence
\[
\boxed{a=\frac12},\qquad\boxed{b=-\frac14}.
\]
The other asymptote is
\[
\boxed{x=\frac12}.
\]
The \(y\)-intercept is
\[
\boxed{(0,-4)}.
\]
The two branches approach \(x=\frac12\) and \(y=2x+1\) with the correct signs; the numerator has no real zero, so the curve does not cross the \(x\)-axis.

 Completed

ModulusInequality
Let \(a\) be a positive constant.
(a) Sketch
\[
y=\frac{ax}{x+7}.
\]
[2]
(b) Sketch
\[
y=\left|\frac{ax}{x+7}\right|
\]
and find the set of values of \(x\) for which
\[
\left|\frac{ax}{x+7}\right|>\frac a2.
\]
[4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(ax/(x+7)=a-7a/(x+7)\), the original curve has asymptotes \(x=-7\) and \(y=a\), and passes through \((0,0)\).
(b) The function is negative on \(-7<x<0\), so reflect precisely this part in the \(x\)-axis to obtain the modulus graph.
The critical equations are
\[
\frac{ax}{x+7}=\pm\frac a2,
\]
giving \(x=7\) and \(x=-\frac73\). A sign chart across \(-7,-7/3,7\) then gives
\[
\boxed{x<-7\quad\text{or}\quad-7<x<-\frac73\quad\text{or}\quad x>7}.
\]

 Completed

2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 3 · 9 marks
Oblique asymptoteStationary points
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2}{2x+1}.
\]
(a) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). [3]
(b) Find the coordinates of the stationary points on \(C\). [3]
(c) Sketch \(C\). [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Long division gives
\[
\frac{x^2}{2x+1}=\frac x2-\frac14+\frac{1/4}{2x+1}.
\]
Hence the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=-\frac12},
\qquad
\boxed{y=\frac x2-\frac14}.
\]
(b)
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}
=\frac{2x(2x+1)-2x^2}{(2x+1)^2}
=\frac{2x(x+1)}{(2x+1)^2}.
\]
Thus \(x=0,-1\), giving the stationary points
\[
\boxed{(0,0)},\qquad\boxed{(-1,-1)}.
\]
The right branch touches the \(x\)-axis at the origin; the left branch has a stationary point at \((-1,-1)\). Both branches approach the stated asymptotes.

=\frac{-4(x+5)(x-1)}{(2x^2-7x-4)^2}.
\]
Therefore the stationary points are
\[
\boxed{\left(-5,\frac{25}{27}\right),\qquad\left(1,\frac13\right)}.
\]
The intersections are
\[
\boxed{(0,0),\qquad\left(\frac52,0\right)}.
\]
The boundary equations are \(9(2x^2-5x)=\pm(2x^2-7x-4)\). Solving both quadratics and using a sign chart gives
\[
\boxed{
\frac{13-3\sqrt{21}}{10}<x<\frac{19-3\sqrt{33}}{16}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\frac{19+3\sqrt{33}}{16}<x<\frac{13+3\sqrt{21}}{10}}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2025, Q7; 9231/12/M/J/2025, Q7.





2025 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 6 · 14 marks
ParameterModulus
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2+a}{x+a},
\]
where \(a\) is a positive constant.
(a) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). [3]
(b) Find, in terms of \(a\), the \(x\)-coordinates of the stationary points on \(C\). [3]
(c) Sketch \(C\), stating the coordinates of any intersections with the axes. [3]
(d) Sketch
\[
y=\left|\frac{x^2+a}{x+a}\right|.
\]
[1]
(e) Find the set of values of \(a\) for which
\[
\left|\frac{x^2+a}{x+a}\right|=a
\]
has two real solutions. [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

Long division gives
\[
\frac{x^2+a}{x+a}=x-a+\frac{a^2+a}{x+a}.
\]
Hence the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=-a},\qquad\boxed{y=x-a}.
\]
Also
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=1-\frac{a^2+a}{(x+a)^2}.
\]
Setting this equal to zero gives the stationary-point \(x\)-coordinates
\[
\boxed{x=-a\pm\sqrt{a^2+a}}.
\]
The numerator has no real zero and the \(y\)-intercept is
\[
\boxed{(0,1)}.
\]
For \(|f(x)|=a\), the equation \(f(x)=-a\) becomes
\[
x^2+ax+a+a^2=0,
\]
whose discriminant is \(-3a^2-4a<0\). The equation \(f(x)=a\) becomes
\[
x^2-ax+a-a^2=0,
\]
and has two distinct real roots when
\[
5a^2-4a>0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{a>\frac45}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2025, Q6.





2025 May/June · 9231/14 · Question 7 · 16 marks
Range\(f(|x|)\)Inequality
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2+x-4}{x^2+x+2}.
\]
(a) State the equation of the asymptote of \(C\). [1]
(b) Show that, for all real \(x\),
\[
-\frac{17}{7}\le y<1.
\]
[4]
(c) Find the coordinates of any stationary points of \(C\). [3]
(d) Sketch \(C\), stating the coordinates of the intersections with the axes. [3]
(e) Sketch
\[
y=\frac{|x|^2+|x|-4}{|x|^2+|x|+2}
\]
and find the set of values of \(x\) for which
\[
\frac{|x|^2+|x|-4}{|x|^2+|x|+2}< -\frac12.
\]
[5]


Show answer and mark scheme

The asymptote is
\[
\boxed{y=1}.
\]
Since
\[
y=1-\frac6{x^2+x+2}
\]
and
\[
x^2+x+2=\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\frac74\ge\frac74,
\]
it follows directly that
\[
\boxed{-\frac{17}{7}\le y<1}.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{6(2x+1)}{(x^2+x+2)^2},
\]
so the stationary point is
\[
\boxed{\left(-\frac12,-\frac{17}{7}\right)}.
\]
The intersections are
\[
\boxed{(0,-2),\quad
\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt{17}}2,0\right),\quad
\left(\frac{-1+\sqrt{17}}2,0\right)}.
\]
For \(f(|x|)\), retain the \(x\ge0\) half of \(C\) and reflect it in the \(y\)-axis. Put \(u=|x|\). Then
\[
1-\frac6{u^2+u+2}< -\frac12
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
u^2+u-2<0.
\]
Since \(u\ge0\), this gives \(0\le u<1\), hence
\[
\boxed{-1<x<1}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/M/J/2025, Q7.





2025 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 7 · 14 marks
No stationary pointsModulusInequality
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x+2}{x^2+3x+1}.
\]
(a) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). [2]
(b) Show that \(C\) has no stationary points. [3]
(c) Sketch \(C\), stating the coordinates of the intersections with the axes. [3]
(d) Sketch
\[
y=\left|\frac{x+2}{x^2+3x+1}\right|.
\]
[2]
(e) Find in exact form the set of values of \(x\) for which
\[
\left|\frac{x+2}{x^2+3x+1}\right|>2.
\]
[4]


Show answer and mark scheme

The asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=\frac{-3-\sqrt5}{2}},\qquad
\boxed{x=\frac{-3+\sqrt5}{2}},\qquad
\boxed{y=0}.
\]
Differentiation gives
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}
=-\frac{x^2+4x+5}{(x^2+3x+1)^2}.
\]
The numerator quadratic has discriminant \(16-20=-4<0\) and is always positive, so the derivative is never zero. Hence there are no stationary points. The intersections are
\[
\boxed{(-2,0),\qquad(0,2)}.
\]
Solving the boundary equations \(f(x)=\pm2\) and reading the intervals from the modulus sketch gives
\[
\boxed{
-\frac74-\frac{\sqrt{17}}4<x<-\frac52
\quad\text{or}\quad
-\frac74+\frac{\sqrt{17}}4<x<0,
\qquad
x\ne\frac{-3\pm\sqrt5}{2}}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2025, Q7; 9231/13/O/N/2025, Q7.





2025 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 7 · 14 marks
Oblique asymptote\(f(|x|)\)Inequality
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{x^2+x+1}{x+1}.
\]
(a) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). [3]
(b) Find the coordinates of any stationary points on \(C\). [3]
(c) Sketch \(C\). [3]
(d) Sketch
\[
y=\frac{|x|^2+|x|+1}{|x|+1}.
\]
[2]
(e) Find, in exact form, the set of values of \(x\) for which
\[
\frac{|x|^2+|x|+1}{|x|+1}<3.
\]
[3]


Show answer and mark scheme

Long division gives
\[
\frac{x^2+x+1}{x+1}=x+\frac1{x+1}.
\]
Hence the asymptotes of \(C\) are
\[
\boxed{x=-1},\qquad\boxed{y=x}.
\]
Also
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=1-\frac1{(x+1)^2}=0
\]
gives \(x=0,-2\), so the stationary points are
\[
\boxed{(0,1),\qquad(-2,-3)}.
\]
For \(f(|x|)\), retain the right-hand branch and reflect it in the \(y\)-axis; the result is smooth at \((0,1)\). Put \(u=|x|\). Then
\[
\frac{u^2+u+1}{u+1}<3
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
u^2-2u-2<0.
\]
Thus \(0\le u<1+\sqrt3\), giving
\[
\boxed{-1-\sqrt3<x<1+\sqrt3}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2025, Q7.





2025 October/November · 9231/14 · Question 7 · 16 marks
No stationary pointsModulusGiven intervals
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{10x^2-11x-18}{10x-18}.
\]
(a) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). [3]
(b) Show that \(C\) has no stationary points. [4]
(c) Sketch \(C\), stating the coordinates of the points of intersection with the axes. [3]
(d) Sketch
\[
y=\left|\frac{10x^2-11x-18}{10x-18}\right|.
\]
[2]
(e) Given that
\[
\left|\frac{10x^2-11x-18}{10x-18}\right|<4
\]
for
\[
\frac{-29-\sqrt{4441}}{20}<x<p
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{-29+\sqrt{4441}}{20}<x<q,
\]
find \(p\) and \(q\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

Long division gives
\[
\frac{10x^2-11x-18}{10x-18}
=x+\frac7{10}-\frac{27/5}{10x-18}.
\]
Hence the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=\frac95},\qquad\boxed{y=x+\frac7{10}}.
\]
Differentiating this form,
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=1+\frac{54}{(10x-18)^2}>0,
\]
so there are no stationary points. The intersections are
\[
\boxed{(0,1),\qquad\left(-\frac9{10},0\right),\qquad(2,0)}.
\]
For \(|f(x)|<4\), the four boundary values come from \(f(x)=4\) and \(f(x)=-4\). The two values represented by \(p,q\) come from \(f(x)=4\), giving
\[
10x^2-51x+54=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{p=\frac32},\qquad\boxed{q=\frac{18}{5}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/O/N/2025, Q7.
