title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

记忆并使用二次、三次及四次多项式方程的根与系数关系；
计算根的对称函数，或利用这些关系求方程中的未知系数；
通过代换建立新方程，新方程的根与原方程的根具有简单关系。

title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
学习路线


能从系数直接写出二次、三次和四次方程的根与系数关系
能把平方和、立方和等对称函数化为基本的根之和与根之积
能利用每个根都满足原方程来求较高次幂和
能用根与系数关系或代换法建立新方程
能根据给定的根之间的关系求未知系数并解方程

title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Quadratic equations
若 \(az^2+bz+c=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta\)，则
\[
\alpha+\beta=-\frac ba,
\qquad
\alpha\beta=\frac ca.
\]
二次方程中所有关于 \(\alpha,\beta\) 的对称函数，都可以用 \(\alpha+\beta\) 与 \(\alpha\beta\) 表示。例如
\[
\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta.
\]


1.2 Cubic equations
若 \(az^3+bz^2+cz+d=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\)，则
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum\alpha
&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\frac ba,\\
\sum\alpha\beta
&=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=\frac ca,\\
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma
&=\alpha\beta\gamma=-\frac da.
\end{aligned}
\]
教材采用以下简写：
\[
\sum\alpha=\alpha+\beta+\gamma,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha.
\]


1.3 Common symmetric identities
对称函数的值不因根的排列次序改变。计算时通常先把所求式化为 \(\sum\alpha\)、\(\sum\alpha\beta\)、\(\alpha\beta\gamma\) 等基本对称函数。
对二次或三次方程的根，有
\[
\sum\alpha^2
=\left(\sum\alpha\right)^2-2\sum\alpha\beta.
\]
对三次方程的根，有
\[
\sum\alpha^3
=\left(\sum\alpha\right)^3
-3\left(\sum\alpha\right)\left(\sum\alpha\beta\right)
+3\alpha\beta\gamma,
\]
以及
\[
\sum\alpha^2\beta^2
=\left(\sum\alpha\beta\right)^2
-2\left(\sum\alpha\right)\alpha\beta\gamma,
\]
其中
\[
\sum\alpha^2\beta^2
=\alpha^2\beta^2+\beta^2\gamma^2+\gamma^2\alpha^2.
\]
展开或因式分解时，应让最终表达式只含原方程系数能够确定的基本对称函数。


1.4 Power sums
设三次方程的根为 \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\)，并定义
\[
S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n.
\]
若先把方程化为首一形式
\[
z^3+pz^2+qz+r=0,
\]
则
\[
S_0=3,
\qquad
S_1=-p,
\qquad
S_2=p^2-2q.
\]
因为每个根都满足原方程，将根的三个等式相加可得
\[
S_n+pS_{n-1}+qS_{n-2}+rS_{n-3}=0
\qquad(n\geqslant3).
\]
特别地，当 \(n=3\) 时，常数项会出现三次：
\[
S_3+pS_2+qS_1+3r=0.
\]
同理，若四次方程写成
\[
z^4+pz^3+qz^2+rz+s=0
\]
且 \(S_n\) 表示四个根的 \(n\) 次幂之和，则
\[
S_0=4
\]
并且
\[
S_n+pS_{n-1}+qS_{n-2}+rS_{n-3}+sS_{n-4}=0
\qquad(n\geqslant4).
\]
这种方法适合连续计算较高次幂和；开始递推前，应先由根与系数关系求出所需的较低次幂和。


1.5 Reciprocal roots and negative powers
若原方程的常数项不为零，则所有根都不为零，可以讨论倒数根。 对三次方程的根，
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma
&=\frac{\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha}{\alpha\beta\gamma},\\
\frac1{\alpha\beta}+\frac1{\beta\gamma}+\frac1{\gamma\alpha}
&=\frac{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}{\alpha\beta\gamma},\\
\frac1\alpha\frac1\beta\frac1\gamma
&=\frac1{\alpha\beta\gamma}.
\end{aligned}
\]
因此，若 \(az^3+bz^2+cz+d=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\)，其中 \(d\ne0\)，则
\[
\sum\frac1\alpha=-\frac cd,
\qquad
\sum\frac1{\alpha\beta}=\frac bd,
\qquad
\frac1{\alpha\beta\gamma}=-\frac ad.
\]
求倒数根方程时，令 \(z=1/w\) 并乘以适当的 \(w\) 的幂。例如，
\[
az^3+bz^2+cz+d=0
\]
对应的倒数根方程为
\[
dw^3+cw^2+bw+a=0.
\]
也就是说，系数的次序反转。相同方法适用于二次及四次方程。
负次幂和可以看作倒数根的正次幂和。例如
\[
\sum\alpha^{-n}
=\left(\frac1\alpha\right)^n
+\left(\frac1\beta\right)^n
+\left(\frac1\gamma\right)^n,
\]
所以可以先建立倒数根方程，再使用上一节的幂和方法。


1.6 Forming new equations
教材使用两种方法建立新方程：

计算新根的和、两两乘积之和及乘积，再由根与系数关系写出方程；
令新变量与旧变量满足题目给出的根的变换，写出旧变量并代入原方程。

例如新根为 \(2\alpha+1,2\beta+1,2\gamma+1\) 时，令
\[
w=2z+1,
\qquad
z=\frac{w-1}{2}.
\]
新根为 \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\) 时，可以令 \(w=z^2\)，再消去 \(z\)。


1.7 Quartic equations
若 \(az^4+bz^3+cz^2+dz+e=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\)，则
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum\alpha
&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=-\frac ba,\\
\sum\alpha\beta
&=\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta
+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta=\frac ca,\\
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma
&=\alpha\beta\gamma+\beta\gamma\delta
+\gamma\delta\alpha+\delta\alpha\beta=-\frac da,\\
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma\delta
&=\alpha\beta\gamma\delta=\frac ea.
\end{aligned}
\]






提示Sign pattern



从最高次项开始，根的基本对称函数对应的符号依次为
\[
-,\quad +,\quad -,\quad +.
\]

title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
2. Textbook examples and examination questions

Textbook Examples


Example 3.1 · Page 72
Find a quadratic equation with roots \(5\) and \(-3\).


Show solution

The sum of the roots is
\[
5+(-3)=2,
\]
and the product of the roots is
\[
5(-3)=-15.
\]
Taking the coefficient of \(z^2\) to be \(1\), a quadratic equation with the required roots is
\[
\boxed{z^2-2z-15=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.2 · Page 73
The roots of the equation
\[
2z^2+3z+5=0
\]
are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

Find the values of \(\alpha+\beta\) and \(\alpha\beta\).
Find the quadratic equation with roots \(2\alpha\) and \(2\beta\).



Show solution

From the original equation,
\[
\alpha+\beta=-\frac32,
\qquad
\alpha\beta=\frac52.
\]
For the new roots,
\[
2\alpha+2\beta=2(\alpha+\beta)=-3,
\]
and
\[
(2\alpha)(2\beta)=4\alpha\beta=10.
\]
Therefore the required equation is
\[
\boxed{z^2+3z+10=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.3 · Pages 73–74
The roots of the equation
\[
3z^2-4z-1=0
\]
are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Find the quadratic equation with roots \(\alpha+1\) and \(\beta+1\).


Show solution

From the original equation,
\[
\alpha+\beta=\frac43,
\qquad
\alpha\beta=-\frac13.
\]
The sum of the new roots is
\[
(\alpha+1)+(\beta+1)=\alpha+\beta+2=\frac{10}{3},
\]
and their product is
\[
(\alpha+1)(\beta+1)
=\alpha\beta+(\alpha+\beta)+1
=2.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{3z^2-10z+6=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.4 · Pages 74–75
The quadratic equation
\[
ax^2+bx+c=0,
\]
where \(a,b,c\) are constants, has roots \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Prove that
\[
\alpha^2+\beta^2=\frac{b^2-2ac}{a^2}.
\]


Show solution

Since
\[
(\alpha+\beta)^2=\alpha^2+2\alpha\beta+\beta^2,
\]
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2
&=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta\\
&=\left(-\frac ba\right)^2-2\left(\frac ca\right)\\
&=\boxed{\frac{b^2-2ac}{a^2}}.
\end{aligned}
\]

 Completed


Example 3.5 · Page 78
The roots of the equation
\[
2z^3-9z^2-27z+54=0
\]
form a geometric progression, so they may be written as \(\dfrac ar,a,ar\). Solve the equation.


Show solution

Using the product of the roots,
\[
\frac ar\times a\times ar=-\frac{54}{2},
\]
so
\[
a^3=-27
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
a=-3.
\]
Using the sum of the roots,
\[
-\frac3r-3-3r=\frac92.
\]
Hence
\[
2r^2+5r+2=0,
\]
so
\[
(2r+1)(r+2)=0
\]
and therefore \(r=-2\) or \(r=-\dfrac12\). Either value gives the same three roots:
\[
\boxed{\frac32,-3,6}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.6 · Pages 78–79
The roots of the cubic equation
\[
x^3-4x^2+x+6=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find the values of

\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\);
\(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3\).



Show solution

From the original equation,
\[
\sum\alpha=4,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2
-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\\
&=4^2-2(1)\\
&=\boxed{14}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since each root satisfies \(x^3-4x^2+x+6=0\),
\[
\alpha^3=4\alpha^2-\alpha-6,
\]
with corresponding equations for \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\). Adding them gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3
&=4(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)
-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)-18\\
&=4(14)-4-18\\
&=\boxed{34}.
\end{aligned}
\]

 Completed


Example 3.7 · Pages 79–80
The roots of the cubic equation
\[
2z^3+5z^2-3z-2=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find the cubic equation with roots \(2\alpha+1,2\beta+1,2\gamma+1\).


Show solution 1: relations between roots and coefficients

For the original equation,
\[
\sum\alpha=-\frac52,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=-\frac32,
\qquad
\alpha\beta\gamma=1.
\]
For the new roots, their sum is
\[
2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3=-2.
\]
The sum of their products in pairs is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(2\alpha+1)(2\beta+1)
+(2\beta+1)(2\gamma+1)
+(2\gamma+1)(2\alpha+1)\\
&=4(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)
+4(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3\\
&=4\left(-\frac32\right)+4\left(-\frac52\right)+3\\
&=-13.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their product is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(2\alpha+1)(2\beta+1)(2\gamma+1)\\
&=8\alpha\beta\gamma
+4(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)
+2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+1\\
&=8+4\left(-\frac32\right)
+2\left(-\frac52\right)+1\\
&=-2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the required equation is
\[
\boxed{z^3+2z^2-13z+2=0}.
\]



Show solution 2: substitution method

Let
\[
w=2z+1,
\qquad
z=\frac{w-1}{2}.
\]
Substituting into the original equation gives
\[
2\left(\frac{w-1}{2}\right)^3
+5\left(\frac{w-1}{2}\right)^2
-3\left(\frac{w-1}{2}\right)-2=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(4\) and simplifying,
\[
(w-1)^3+5(w-1)^2-6(w-1)-8=0,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{w^3+2w^2-13w+2=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.8 · Pages 80–81
The roots of the cubic equation
\[
2z^3-5z^2+z+2=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find the cubic equation with roots \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\).


Show solution

Let \(w=z^2\), so \(z=\sqrt w\). Substitution gives
\[
2w\sqrt w-5w+\sqrt w+2=0.
\]
Collecting the terms containing \(\sqrt w\),
\[
\sqrt w(2w+1)=5w-2.
\]
Squaring both sides,
\[
w(2w+1)^2=(5w-2)^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
4w^3+4w^2+w&=25w^2-20w+4,\\
4w^3-21w^2+21w-4&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the required equation is
\[
\boxed{4w^3-21w^2+21w-4=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.9 · Pages 84–85
The roots of the quartic equation
\[
4z^4+pz^3+qz^2-z+3=0
\]
are \(\alpha,-\alpha,\alpha+\lambda,\alpha-\lambda\), where \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\) are real numbers.

Express \(p\) and \(q\) in terms of \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\).
Show that \(\alpha=-\dfrac12\), and find the values of \(p\) and \(q\).
Give the roots of the quartic equation.



Show solution

The sum of the roots is
\[
\alpha-\alpha+(\alpha+\lambda)+(\alpha-\lambda)
=2\alpha=-\frac p4,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{p=-8\alpha}.
\]
The sum of the products of the roots in pairs simplifies to \(-\lambda^2\). Hence
\[
-\lambda^2=\frac q4
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{q=-4\lambda^2}.
\]
The sum of the products of the roots in threes is
\[
-2\alpha^3.
\]
Since this is equal to \(-\dfrac{-1}{4}=\dfrac14\),
\[
-2\alpha^3=\frac14.
\]
Thus
\[
\alpha^3=-\frac18
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{\alpha=-\frac12},
\]
and therefore
\[
\boxed{p=4}.
\]
Using the product of the four roots,
\[
-\alpha^2(\alpha^2-\lambda^2)=\frac34.
\]
Substituting \(\alpha=-\dfrac12\) gives
\[
-\frac14\left(\frac14-\lambda^2\right)=\frac34,
\]
so
\[
\lambda^2=\frac{13}{4}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\boxed{q=-13}.
\]
The roots are
\[
\boxed{
\frac12,
-\frac12,
-\frac12+\frac{\sqrt{13}}2,
-\frac12-\frac{\sqrt{13}}2
}.
\]

 Completed


Examination questions printed in the textbook exercises


Exercise 3B, Question 16
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q5 October/November 2015
The cubic equation
\[
x^3+px^2+qx+r=0,
\]
where \(p,q,r\) are integers, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) such that
\[
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=15,
\qquad
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=83.
\]
Write down the value of \(p\) and find the value of \(q\).
Given that \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) are all real and that \(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma=36\), find \(\alpha\) and hence find the value of \(r\).


Show solution

Since \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-p\),
\[
\boxed{p=-15}.
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
83
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2
-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\\
&=15^2-2q,
\end{aligned}
\]
so
\[
\boxed{q=71}.
\]
Now
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma
=\alpha(\beta+\gamma)
=\alpha(15-\alpha)=36.
\]
Thus
\[
\alpha^2-15\alpha+36=0,
\]
giving \(\alpha=3\) or \(\alpha=12\).
If \(\alpha=12\), then \(\beta+\gamma=3\) and \(\beta\gamma=35\), which does not give real values of \(\beta,\gamma\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\alpha=3}.
\]
Then \(\beta+\gamma=12\) and \(\beta\gamma=35\), so
\[
r=-\alpha\beta\gamma=-3(35)=\boxed{-105}.
\]

 Completed


Exercise 3B, Question 17
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q2 October/November 2013
The cubic equation
\[
x^3-px-q=0,
\]
where \(p,q\) are constants, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Show that

\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=2p\);
\(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=3q\);
\[
6(\alpha^5+\beta^5+\gamma^5)
=5(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)
(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2).
\]



Show solution

For the original equation,
\[
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0,
\qquad
\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=-p.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2
-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\\
&=0-2(-p)\\
&=\boxed{2p}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each root satisfies \(x^3=px+q\). Adding the three corresponding equations gives
\[
\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3
=p(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3q
=\boxed{3q}.
\]
Multiplying \(x^3=px+q\) by \(x^2\) gives \(x^5=px^3+qx^2\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^5+\beta^5+\gamma^5
&=p(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)
+q(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)\\
&=p(3q)+q(2p)\\
&=5pq.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus both sides of the required identity are equal to \(30pq\).

 Completed


Exercise 3B, Question 18
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q1 October/November 2011
The equation
\[
x^3+px+q=0
\]
has a repeated root. Prove that
\[
4p^3+27q^2=0.
\]


Show solution

Let the repeated root be \(\alpha\) and the third root be \(\beta\). Since the coefficient of \(x^2\) is zero,
\[
2\alpha+\beta=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\beta=-2\alpha.
\]
Using the sum of the products in pairs,
\[
p=\alpha^2+2\alpha\beta
=\alpha^2-4\alpha^2
=-3\alpha^2.
\]
Using the product of the roots,
\[
-q=\alpha^2\beta=-2\alpha^3,
\]
so \(q=2\alpha^3\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
4p^3+27q^2
&=4(-3\alpha^2)^3+27(2\alpha^3)^2\\
&=-108\alpha^6+108\alpha^6\\
&=\boxed{0}.
\end{aligned}
\]

 Completed


Exercise 3C, Question 7
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q11 October/November 2014
The roots of the quartic equation
\[
x^4+4x^3+2x^2-4x+1=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\). Find the values of

\(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta\);
\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2\);
\(\dfrac1\alpha+\dfrac1\beta+\dfrac1\gamma+\dfrac1\delta\);
\[
\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\beta}{\alpha\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta\delta}
+\frac{\delta}{\alpha\beta\gamma}.
\]

Using the substitution \(y=x+1\), find a quartic equation in \(y\). Solve this quartic equation and hence find the roots of
\[
x^4+4x^3+2x^2-4x+1=0.
\]


Show solution

From the coefficients,
\[
\sum\alpha=-4,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=2,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma=4,
\qquad
\alpha\beta\gamma\delta=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=-4},
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)^2-2\sum\alpha\beta\\
&=16-4\\
&=\boxed{12},
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma+\frac1\delta
=\frac{\sum\alpha\beta\gamma}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}
=\boxed{4}.
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\beta}{\alpha\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta\delta}
+\frac{\delta}{\alpha\beta\gamma}\\
&=\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2}
{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}\\
&=\boxed{12}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(y=x+1\), so \(x=y-1\). Substitution gives
\[
y^4-4y^2+4=0,
\]
or
\[
(y^2-2)^2=0.
\]
Thus \(y=\pm\sqrt2\), each repeated, and the roots of the original equation are
\[
\boxed{-1+\sqrt2,\ -1+\sqrt2,\ -1-\sqrt2,\ -1-\sqrt2}.
\]

 Completed


Exercise 3C, Question 8
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q11 October/November 2012
The roots of the equation
\[
x^4-3x^2+5x-2=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\), and
\[
S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n+\delta^n.
\]
Show that
\[
S_{n+4}-3S_{n+2}+5S_{n+1}-2S_n=0.
\]
Find the values of

\(S_2\) and \(S_4\);
\(S_3\) and \(S_5\).

Hence find the value of
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\alpha^2(\beta^3+\gamma^3+\delta^3)
+\beta^2(\gamma^3+\delta^3+\alpha^3)\\
&\quad+\gamma^2(\delta^3+\alpha^3+\beta^3)
+\delta^2(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3).
\end{aligned}
\]


Show solution

Each root satisfies
\[
x^4-3x^2+5x-2=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(x^n\) and then adding the four resulting equations gives
\[
\boxed{S_{n+4}-3S_{n+2}+5S_{n+1}-2S_n=0}.
\]
From the coefficients,
\[
S_1=0,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=-3,
\]
so
\[
S_2=S_1^2-2\sum\alpha\beta=\boxed{6}.
\]
Taking \(n=0\) in the recurrence, with \(S_0=4\), gives
\[
S_4-3S_2+5S_1-2S_0=0,
\]
and hence
\[
S_4=\boxed{26}.
\]
Also, \(\sum\alpha\beta\gamma=-5\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_3
&=\left(\sum\alpha\right)^3
-3\left(\sum\alpha\right)\left(\sum\alpha\beta\right)
+3\sum\alpha\beta\gamma\\
&=0-0+3(-5)\\
&=\boxed{-15}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(n=1\) in the recurrence gives
\[
S_5-3S_3+5S_2-2S_1=0,
\]
so
\[
S_5=\boxed{-75}.
\]
The final expression is
\[
S_2S_3-S_5
=6(-15)-(-75)
=\boxed{-15}.
\]

 Completed

title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
3. Past-paper question bank

2019



2019 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 6 · 9 marks
Power sumsTransformed roots★★★☆☆
The equation
\[x^3-x+1=0\]
has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(i) Use the relation \(x=y^{1/3}\) to show that the equation
\[y^3+3y^2+2y+1=0\]
has roots \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\). Hence write down the value of \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3\). [3]
Let \(S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n\).
(ii) Find the value of \(S_{-3}\). [2]
(iii) Show that \(S_6=5\) and find the value of \(S_9\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Put \(y=x^3\), so \(x=y^{1/3}\). Then
\[
y-y^{1/3}+1=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
y+1=y^{1/3}.
\]
Cubing both sides,
\[y=(y+1)^3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y^3+3y^2+2y+1=0. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
The three roots are \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\), so Vieta’s formula gives \(\boxed{S_3=-3}\). B1
(ii) For the roots \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\), the sum of pairwise products is \(2\) and the product is \(-1\). Hence
\[S_{-3}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(iii)
\[S_6=S_3^2-2(2)=(-3)^2-4=5. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
Summing the transformed equation over its three roots gives
\[S_9+3S_6+2S_3+3=0,\]
so
\[S_9=-3(5)-2(-3)-3=-12. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2019, Q6; 9231/12/M/J/2019, Q6.





2019 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 9 · 11 marks
Unknown coefficientsSymmetric sums★★★★☆
A cubic equation
\[x^3+bx^2+cx+d=0\]
has real roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) such that
\[
\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma=-\frac5{12},
\qquad \alpha\beta\gamma=-12,
\qquad \alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=90.
\]
(i) Find the values of \(c\) and \(d\). [3]
(ii) Express \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\) in terms of \(b\). [2]
(iii) Show that \(b^3-15b+126=0\). [4]
(iv) Given that \(3+i\sqrt{12}\) is a root of \(y^3-15y+126=0\), deduce the value of \(b\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-d=-12\), \(d=12\). B1
Also
\[\frac{\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha}{\alpha\beta\gamma}=-\frac5{12},\]
so \(c=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=5\). M1 A1
(ii)
\[\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2-2c=b^2-10. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(iii) Since \(S_2=b^2-10\) and every root satisfies \(x^3=-bx^2-5x-12\), summing over all three roots gives
\[90=-b(b^2-10)-5(-b)-36.\]
Hence
\[b^3-15b+126=0. \qquad \text{M1 M1 A1 A1}\]
(iv) The polynomial has real coefficients, so \(3-i\sqrt{12}\) is also a root. These two roots have sum \(6\). Since the coefficient of \(y^2\) is zero, the third root is \(-6\). Thus the required real value is \(\boxed{b=-6}\). M1 A1

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2019, Q9.





2019 October/November · 9231/11, 9231/12 & 9231/13 · Question 7 · 9 marks
Transformed rootsPower sums★★★★☆
The equation \(x^3+2x^2+x+7=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(i) Use the relation \(x^2=-7y\) to show that
\[49y^3+14y^2-27y+7=0\]
has roots
\[\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma},\qquad
\frac{\beta}{\gamma\alpha},\qquad
\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta}. \qquad \textbf{[4]}\]
(ii) Show that
\[\frac{\alpha^2}{\beta^2\gamma^2}+
\frac{\beta^2}{\gamma^2\alpha^2}+
\frac{\gamma^2}{\alpha^2\beta^2}=\frac{58}{49}. \qquad \textbf{[3]}\]
(iii) Find the exact value of
\[
\frac{\alpha^3}{\beta^3\gamma^3}+
\frac{\beta^3}{\gamma^3\alpha^3}+
\frac{\gamma^3}{\alpha^3\beta^3}. \qquad \textbf{[2]}
\]


Show answer and mark scheme

Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-7\),
\[\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma}=-\frac{\alpha^2}{7},\]
and similarly for the other two roots. With \(x^2=-7y\), the original equation becomes
\[
x(1-7y)+7(1-2y)=0,
\]
so \(x=7(2y-1)/(1-7y)\). Squaring and using \(x^2=-7y\) gives
\[
49(2y-1)^2=-7y(1-7y)^2,
\]
which simplifies to the stated cubic. M1 M1 A1 A1
For the transformed roots,
\[e_1=-\frac27,\qquad e_2=-\frac{27}{49},\qquad e_3=-\frac17.\]
Therefore
\[p_2=e_1^2-2e_2=\frac4{49}+\frac{54}{49}=\frac{58}{49}. \qquad \text{M1 A1 A1}\]
Also
\[p_3=e_1p_2-e_2p_1+3e_3=-\frac{317}{343}. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2019, Q7; 9231/12/O/N/2019, Q7; 9231/13/O/N/2019, Q7.




2020



2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 2 · 8 marks
Squared rootsUnknown coefficient★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(6x^3+px^2-3x-5=0\), where \(p\) is a constant, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find a cubic equation whose roots are \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\). [3]
(b) It is given that
\[\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma).\]
(i) Find the value of \(p\). [3]
(ii) Find the value of \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=x^2\). Rewriting the original equation gives \(x(6y-3)=5-py\). Squaring and using \(x^2=y\) gives
\[y(6y-3)^2=(5-py)^2,\]
hence
\[36y^3-(p^2+36)y^2+(10p+9)y-25=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(b)(i)
\[\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\frac p6,\qquad
\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=-\frac12.\]
Thus
\[\frac{p^2}{36}+1=-\frac p3,\]
so \((p+6)^2=0\) and \(p=-6\). M1 A1 A1
(b)(ii) With \(p=-6\),
\[e_1=1,\qquad e_2=-\frac12,\qquad e_3=\frac56,\]
and
\[\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=e_1^3-3e_1e_2+3e_3=5. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2020, Q2; 9231/12/M/J/2020, Q2.





2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 1 · 7 marks
Reciprocal rootsNegative powers★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(7x^3+3x^2+5x+1=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find a cubic equation whose roots are \(\alpha^{-1},\beta^{-1},\gamma^{-1}\). [3]
(b) Find \(\alpha^{-2}+\beta^{-2}+\gamma^{-2}\). [2]
(c) Find \(\alpha^{-3}+\beta^{-3}+\gamma^{-3}\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=1/x\). Then
\[
\frac7{y^3}+\frac3{y^2}+\frac5y+1=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(y^3\) gives
\[y^3+5y^2+3y+7=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
For the reciprocal roots, \(e_1=-5\), \(e_2=3\), \(e_3=-7\).
(b)
\[p_2=e_1^2-2e_2=25-6=19. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(c)
\[p_3=e_1p_2-e_2p_1+3e_3=-5(19)-3(-5)-21=-101. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2020, Q1.





2020 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 3 · 11 marks
Cubed rootsSingular matrix★★★★☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+cx+1=0\), where \(c\) is a constant, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find a cubic equation whose roots are \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\). [3]
(b) Show that \(\alpha^6+\beta^6+\gamma^6=3-2c^3\). [3]
(c) Find the real value of \(c\) for which
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&\alpha^3&\beta^3\\
\alpha^3&1&\gamma^3\\
\beta^3&\gamma^3&1
\end{pmatrix}
\]
is singular. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=x^3\). Since \(cx=-(y+1)\), cubing and using \(x^3=y\) gives \(c^3y=-(y+1)^3\), hence
\[y^3+3y^2+(c^3+3)y+1=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(b) For the new roots, \(e_1=-3\) and \(e_2=c^3+3\). Hence

\[1-\alpha^2-\beta^2-\gamma^2+2\alpha\beta\gamma.\]
Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=1\) and the determinant is zero,
\[\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=1+2=3. \qquad \text{M1 A1 M1 A1}\]
(b)
\[3=b^2-2c. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
Summing the original equation over the roots gives
\[3=-3b+bc+3,\]
so \(b(c-3)=0\). Since \(b>0\), \(c=3\). Substitution gives \(b=3\). M1 A1 DM1 A1

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/M/J/2025, Q4.





2025 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 4 · 8 marks
Quartic linear transformationPower sums★★★☆☆
The quartic equation \(x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\).
(a) Show that a quartic equation with roots \(2\alpha+1,2\beta+1,2\gamma+1,2\delta+1\) is
\[y^4-2y^3+4y^2+2y+11=0. \qquad \textbf{[4]}\]
The sum \((2\alpha+1)^n+(2\beta+1)^n+(2\gamma+1)^n+(2\delta+1)^n\) is denoted by \(S_n\).
(b) Find \(S_2\). [2]
(c) Given that \(S_3=-22\), find \(S_4\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=2x+1\), so \(x=(y-1)/2\). Substitution and multiplication by \(16\) give
\[
(y-1)^4+2(y-1)^3+4(y-1)^2+8(y-1)+16=0,
\]
which simplifies to
\[y^4-2y^3+4y^2+2y+11=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1 A1}\]
For the transformed roots, \(e_1=2\) and \(e_2=4\).
(b)
\[S_2=2^2-2(4)=-4. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(c) Summing the transformed quartic over its four roots,
\[S_4-2S_3+4S_2+2S_1+44=0.\]
Thus
\[S_4=-76. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2025, Q4; 9231/13/O/N/2025, Q4.





2025 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 2 · 8 marks
Recovering coefficientsFourth power sum★★★★☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+bx^2+cx+d=0\), where \(b,c,d\) are constants, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). It is given that
\[
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=2,\qquad
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=3,\qquad
\alpha^4+\beta^4+\gamma^4=5.
\]
(a) Find \(b,c\). [3]
(b) Find \(d\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a)
\[b=-2. \qquad \text{B1}\]
Also
\[3=(-2)^2-2c,\]
so \(c=1/2\). M1 A1
(b) Let \(S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n\). Summing the original cubic over its three roots gives
\[S_3+bS_2+cS_1+3d=0,\]
so
\[S_3=5-3d. \qquad \text{M1 A1FT}\]
Multiplying the original cubic by \(x\) and summing over its roots gives
\[S_4+bS_3+cS_2+dS_1=0.\]
Substitution gives
\[5-2(5-3d)+\frac12(3)+2d=0,\]
so
\[d=\frac7{16}. \qquad \text{M1 A1FT A1}\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2025, Q2.





2025 October/November · 9231/14 · Question 2 · 9 marks
Reciprocal relationUnknown coefficients★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+bx^2+cx+d=0\), where \(d\ne0\), has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) such that
\[\gamma=\frac1\beta.\]
(a) Show that
\[\beta+\frac1\beta=d-b. \qquad \textbf{[3]}\]
(b) Show also that
\[\beta+\frac1\beta=\frac{1-c}{d}. \qquad \textbf{[2]}\]
(c) It is given that \(b=3\), \(c=-3\) and \(d>0\).
(i) Find \(d\). [2]
(ii) Find \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-d\) and \(\gamma=1/\beta\), \(\alpha=-d\). B1
(a) Using the sum of roots,
\[-d+\beta+\frac1\beta=-b,\]
so
\[\beta+\frac1\beta=d-b. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(b) Using the sum of pairwise products,
\[-d\beta+1-\frac d\beta=c,\]
which gives
\[\beta+\frac1\beta=\frac{1-c}{d}. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(c)(i)
\[d-3=\frac4d,\]
so \(d^2-3d-4=0\). Since \(d>0\), \(d=4\). M1 A1
(c)(ii)
\[\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=b^2-2c=9+6=15. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/O/N/2025, Q2.

4. 完成本节的判断标准
当你能够在不查看公式表的情况下完成以下任务，本节可以视为基本掌握：

写出二次、三次及四次方程的全部根与系数关系；

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

使用 \(\sum r\)、\(\sum r^2\)、\(\sum r^3\) 的标准结果求相关级数；
使用 method of differences 求有限级数之和，必要时先作部分分式分解；
直接考察前 \(n\) 项和，判断级数是否收敛，并在收敛时求无穷和。

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
学习路线


能从通项写出前几项，并从具体级数识别通项和求和上下限
能正确拆分求和符号并使用三个标准公式
能通过错位相减处理等比型有限和
能将有理式裂项，使中间项成对消去
能保留所有未消去的首项和尾项
能从 \(S_n\) 在 \(n\to\infty\) 时的极限判断收敛并求无穷和

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Sequences, series and sigma notation
数列是按顺序排列的数；级数是数列各项的和。若通项为 \(u_r\)，前 \(n\) 项和写作
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r.
\]
上下限决定所包含的项。若求和式中没有 \(r\)，仍需按上下限重复相加，例如
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}c=nc.
\]
若已知前 \(n\) 项和，则
\[
u_1=S_1,\qquad u_r=S_r-S_{r-1}\quad(r\ge2).
\]


1.2 Standard results
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1),
\]
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^2=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1),
\]
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^3=\frac14n^2(n+1)^2.
\]
使用时先展开通项，再利用求和的线性性质。不要把 \(\sum r^2\) 误写成 \(\left(\sum r\right)^2\)。


1.3 Changing limits
对于连续的一段整数，可用“大和减小和”：
\[
\sum_{r=a}^{b}u_r
=\sum_{r=1}^{b}u_r-\sum_{r=1}^{a-1}u_r.
\]
同理，若 \(S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r\)，则
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r=S_{2n}-S_n.
\]


1.4 Method of differences
核心是把通项写成相邻项之差：
\[
u_r=f(r)-f(r+1).
\]
于是
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r
=[f(1)-f(2)]+[f(2)-f(3)]+\cdots+[f(n)-f(n+1)],
\]
中间项全部消去，只剩
\[
\boxed{S_n=f(1)-f(n+1)}.
\]
若裂项跨度大于 1，通常会留下多于一个首项和尾项，必须将前几项与最后几项完整写出。


1.5 Sum to infinity
先求有限前 \(n\) 项和 \(S_n\)，再直接考察
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n.
\]
若极限存在且有限，则级数收敛，且该极限就是无穷和。若 \(u_n\not\to0\)，级数一定不收敛；但 \(u_n\to0\) 本身不能保证收敛。

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
2. Textbook Examples

Example 2.1 · Pages 43–44
For the series
\[
2+5+8+\cdots+500,
\]
(i) find a formula for the \(r\)th term \(u_r\); (ii) find the number of terms; (iii) find the sum by reversing and adding; (iv) confirm the answer using sigma notation.


Show solution

The sequence has common difference \(3\), so
\[
u_r=3r-1.
\]
Since \(3r-1=500\), there are \(167\) terms. Reversing and adding gives
\[
2S=167(2+500),
\]
so
\[
\boxed{S=41917}.
\]
Also
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{167}(3r-1)
=3\cdot\frac{167\cdot168}{2}-167
=41917.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.2 · Page 44
Calculate the sum of the integers from \(100\) to \(200\) inclusive.


Show solution

\[
\sum_{r=100}^{200}r
=\sum_{r=1}^{200}r-\sum_{r=1}^{99}r
=\frac{200\cdot201}{2}-\frac{99\cdot100}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{15150}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.3 · Page 47
Given \(u_r=r^2+2r-1\):

write down the first three terms;
find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r\);
check the result for \(n=3\).



Show solution

The first three terms are \(2,7,14\). Also
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^2+2r-1)
&=\sum r^2+2\sum r-\sum1\\
&=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)+n(n+1)-n\\
&=\boxed{\frac16n(2n^2+9n+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(n=3\), the formula gives \(23\), and \(2+7+14=23\).

 Completed


Example 2.4 · Page 48
Write
\[
(1\times3)+(2\times4)+(3\times5)+\cdots+n(n+2)
\]
using sigma notation, and hence find its sum.


Show solution

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+2)
=\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^2+2r).
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+2)=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+7)}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.5 · Page 50
Calculate
\[
5+10+20+40+\cdots+2560+5120.
\]


Show solution

Let the sum be \(S\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=5+10+20+\cdots+2560+5120,\\
2S&=10+20+40+\cdots+5120+10240.
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting gives \(S=10240-5\), hence
\[
\boxed{S=10235}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.6 · Pages 50–51
(i) Show that
\[
\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}=\frac1{r(r+1)}.
\]
(ii) Hence find
\[
\frac1{1\times2}+\frac1{2\times3}+\cdots+\frac1{30\times31}.
\]


Show solution

The identity follows by combining the two fractions. Therefore
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{30}\frac1{r(r+1)}
=\sum_{r=1}^{30}\left(\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}\right)
=1-\frac1{31}.
\]
Hence the sum is
\[
\boxed{\frac{30}{31}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.7 · Page 52
(i) Show that \((2r+1)^2-(2r-1)^2=8r\).
(ii) Hence find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r\).
(iii) Deduce the standard result for \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r\).


Show solution

Expanding proves the identity. Summing gives
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r
=(3^2-1^2)+(5^2-3^2)+\cdots+[(2n+1)^2-(2n-1)^2].
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r=(2n+1)^2-1=4n^2+4n,
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1)}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.8 · Pages 52–53
(i) Show that
\[
\frac2r-\frac3{r+1}+\frac1{r+2}
=\frac{r+4}{r(r+1)(r+2)}.
\]
(ii) Hence find
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{r+4}{r(r+1)(r+2)}.
\]
(iii) Deduce the sum to infinity.


Show solution

After using the stated decomposition and writing the first and last terms, all middle terms cancel, leaving
\[
S_n=\frac32-\frac2{n+1}+\frac1{n+2}
=\frac{n(3n+7)}{2(n+1)(n+2)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{S_\infty=\frac32}.
\]

 Completed

title: 1.3 Summation of series
section: 3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
text:
3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook

Exercise 2B, Question 11
It is given that
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r=2n^2+n.
\]
Write down \(S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4\). Express \(u_r\) in terms of \(r\), justifying your answer. Find
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r.
\]


Show solution

\[
S_1=3,\quad S_2=10,\quad S_3=21,\quad S_4=36.
\]
For \(r\ge2\),
\[
u_r=S_r-S_{r-1}=4r-1,
\]
and this also gives \(u_1=3\). Finally,
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r=S_{2n}-S_n
=\boxed{6n^2+n}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 3, October/November 2013.



Exercise 2C, Question 11
Given that
\[
u_k=\frac1{2k-1}-\frac1{2k+1},
\]
express \(\sum_{k=13}^{n}u_k\) in terms of \(n\) and deduce \(\sum_{k=13}^{\infty}u_k\).


Show solution

\[
\sum_{k=13}^{n}u_k
=\left(\frac1{25}-\frac1{27}\right)+\cdots+
\left(\frac1{2n-1}-\frac1{2n+1}\right)
=\boxed{\frac1{25}-\frac1{2n+1}}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{\sum_{k=13}^{\infty}u_k=\frac1{25}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 1, October/November 2014.



Exercise 2C, Question 12
For positive integers \(n\),
\[
a_n=\frac{n+5}{n^2-n+1}-\frac{n+6}{n^2+n+1},
\]
and \(S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n\). Find \(S_{30}\) correct to 3 decimal places and the least \(N\) for which \(S_N>4.9\).


Show solution

Successive terms telescope because the second fraction in \(a_n\) is the first fraction in \(a_{n+1}\). Thus
\[
S_N=6-\frac{N+6}{N^2+N+1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
S_{30}=6-\frac{36}{931}=\boxed{5.961}\quad\text{(3 d.p.)}.
\]
Checking successive values gives \(S_2<4.9\) and \(S_3>4.9\), so
\[
\boxed{N=3}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2015.



Exercise 2C, Question 13
Let \(f(r)=r(r+1)(r+2)\).

Show that \(f(r)-f(r-1)=3r(r+1)\).
Hence show that \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2)\).
Using the standard result for \(\sum r\), deduce the standard result for \(\sum r^2\).
Find the sum

\[
1^2+2(2^2)+3^2+2(4^2)+\cdots+2(n-1)^2+n^2,
\]
where \(n\) is odd.


Show solution

Summing \(f(r)-f(r-1)=3r(r+1)\) gives
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2).
\]
Since \(r(r+1)=r^2+r\),
\[
\sum r^2=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2)-\frac12n(n+1)
=\boxed{\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)}.
\]
For the final series, add one extra copy of every even square to the usual sum of squares. With \(m=(n-1)/2\),
\[
\boxed{\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)+\frac23m(m+1)(2m+1)}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2012.

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
4. Past-paper question bank

2019



2019 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 2 · 5 marks
Let
\[
u_n=\frac{4\sin\left(n-\frac12\right)\sin\frac12}{\cos(2n-1)+\cos1}.
\]
(i) Show that \(u_n=\sec n-\sec(n-1)\). [2]
(ii) Use the method of differences to find \(\sum_{n=1}^{N}u_n\). [2]
(iii) Explain why \(u_1+u_2+u_3+\cdots\) does not converge. [1]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Using the sum-to-product identities,
\[
\cos(2n-1)+\cos1=2\cos n\cos(n-1),
\]
and
\[
2\sin\left(n-\frac12\right)\sin\frac12
=\cos(n-1)-\cos n.
\]
Therefore
\[
u_n
=\frac{2\{\cos(n-1)-\cos n\}}{2\cos n\cos(n-1)}
=\boxed{\sec n-\sec(n-1)}.
\]
(ii) Writing the first few and final terms,
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}u_n
=(\sec1-1)+(\sec2-\sec1)+\cdots+(\sec N-\sec(N-1))
=\boxed{\sec N-1}.
\]
(iii) The sequence \(\sec N\) does not approach a finite limit as \(N\to\infty\); in particular, \(\cos N\) oscillates and can be arbitrarily close to \(0\). Hence the sequence of partial sums \(\sec N-1\) has no limit, so the infinite series diverges.

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2019, Q2; 9231/12/M/J/2019, Q2.





2019 October/November · 9231/11, 9231/12 & 9231/13 · Question 5 · 9 marks
Let
\[
S_N=\sum_{r=1}^{N}(5r+1)(5r+6),
\qquad
T_N=\sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac1{(5r+1)(5r+6)}.
\]
(i) Use standard results to show that
\[
S_N=\frac13N(25N^2+90N+83).
\]
[3]
(ii) Use the method of differences to express \(T_N\) in terms of \(N\). [4]
(iii) Find \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\dfrac{S_NT_N}{N^3}\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Expanding the summand,
\[
S_N=\sum_{r=1}^{N}(25r^2+35r+6)
=25\sum_{r=1}^{N}r^2+35\sum_{r=1}^{N}r+6N.
\]
Substituting the standard results,
\[
S_N
=\frac{25}{6}N(N+1)(2N+1)
+\frac{35}{2}N(N+1)+6N
\]
\[
=\boxed{\frac13N(25N^2+90N+83)}.
\]
(ii) Partial fractions give
\[
\frac1{(5r+1)(5r+6)}
=\frac15\left(\frac1{5r+1}-\frac1{5r+6}\right),
\]
Hence
\[
T_N=\frac15\left[
\left(\frac16-\frac1{11}\right)
+\left(\frac1{11}-\frac1{16}\right)
+\cdots
+\left(\frac1{5N+1}-\frac1{5N+6}\right)
\right].
\]
All intermediate terms cancel, so
\[
\boxed{T_N=\frac1{30}-\frac1{5(5N+6)}}.
\]
(iii) From the leading terms,
\[
\frac{S_N}{N^3}\longrightarrow\frac{25}{3},
\qquad
T_N\longrightarrow\frac1{30}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{S_NT_N}{N^3}=\frac5{18}}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2019, Q5; 9231/12/O/N/2019, Q5; 9231/13/O/N/2019, Q5.




2020



2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 10 marks
(a) By first expressing \(1/(r^2-1)\) in partial fractions, show that
\[
\sum_{r=2}^{n}\frac1{r^2-1}
=\frac34-\frac{2n+1}{2n(n+1)}.
\]
[5]
(b) Deduce \(\sum_{r=2}^{3}\frac1{r^2-1}\). [1]
(c) Find \(\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}\frac1{r^2-1}\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(r^2-1=(r-1)(r+1)\),
\[
\frac1{r^2-1}
=\frac12\left(\frac1{r-1}-\frac1{r+1}\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{r=2}^{n}\frac1{r^2-1}
=\frac12\left[
\left(1-\frac13\right)
+\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)
+\left(\frac13-\frac15\right)
+\cdots
+\left(\frac1{n-1}-\frac1{n+1}\right)
\right]
\]
\[
=\frac12\left(1+\frac12-\frac1n-\frac1{n+1}\right)
=\frac34-\frac{2n+1}{2n(n+1)},
\]
as required.
(b) Put \(n=3\) in part (a):
\[
\sum_{r=2}^{3}\frac1{r^2-1}=\boxed{\frac{11}{24}}.
\]
(c) Let \(F(n)=\sum_{r=2}^{n}1/(r^2-1)\). Then
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}\frac1{r^2-1}=F(2n)-F(n).
\]
Using part (a),
\[
F(2n)-F(n)
=\left(\frac34-\frac{4n+1}{4n(2n+1)}\right)
-\left(\frac34-\frac{2n+1}{2n(n+1)}\right).
\]
Both remaining fractions tend to \(0\), so
\[
\boxed{0}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2020, Q4; 9231/12/M/J/2020, Q4.





2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 3 · 8 marks
Let
\[
S_n=2^2+6^2+10^2+\cdots+(4n-2)^2.
\]
(a) Use standard results to show that
\[
S_n=\frac43n(4n^2-1).
\]
[4]
(b) Express \(n/S_n\) in partial fractions and find \(\sum_{n=1}^{N}n/S_n\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a)
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}(4r-2)^2
=\sum_{r=1}^{n}(16r^2-16r+4).
\]
Hence
\[
S_n
=\frac{16}{6}n(n+1)(2n+1)-8n(n+1)+4n
\]
\[
=\frac43n(4n^2-1),
\]
as required.
(b) Therefore
\[
\frac{n}{S_n}=\frac3{4(2n-1)(2n+1)}
=\frac38\left(\frac1{2n-1}-\frac1{2n+1}\right).
\]
Writing the terms explicitly,
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{n}{S_n}
=\frac38\left[
\left(1-\frac13\right)
+\left(\frac13-\frac15\right)
+\cdots
+\left(\frac1{2N-1}-\frac1{2N+1}\right)
\right].
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{n}{S_n}=\frac38\left(1-\frac1{2N+1}\right)
=\frac{3N}{4(2N+1)}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2020, Q3.





2020 October/November · 9231/13 · Question 2 · 7 marks
(a) Use standard results to find
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(7r+1)(7r+8)
\]
as a cubic polynomial in \(n\). [3]
(b) Use the method of differences to find
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{(7r+1)(7r+8)}.
\]
[4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since
\[
(7r+1)(7r+8)=49r^2+63r+8,
\]
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(7r+1)(7r+8)
=49\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}6
+63\frac{n(n+1)}2+8n
\]
\[
=\boxed{\frac n3(49n^2+168n+143)}.
\]
(b) Partial fractions give
\[
\frac1{(7r+1)(7r+8)}
=\frac17\left(\frac1{7r+1}-\frac1{7r+8}\right),
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{(7r+1)(7r+8)}
=\frac17\left[
\left(\frac18-\frac1{15}\right)
+\left(\frac1{15}-\frac1{22}\right)
+\cdots
+\left(\frac1{7n+1}-\frac1{7n+8}\right)
\right]
\]
\[
=\frac17\left(\frac18-\frac1{7n+8}\right),
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{(7r+1)(7r+8)}
=\frac n{8(7n+8)}}.
\]

2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 3 · 7 marks
(a) By simplifying
\[
(x^n-\sqrt{x^{2n}+1})(x^n+\sqrt{x^{2n}+1}),
\]
show that
\[
\frac1{x^n-\sqrt{x^{2n}+1}}=-x^n-\sqrt{x^{2n}+1}.
\]
[1]
Let
\[
u_n=x^{n+1}+\sqrt{x^{2n+2}+1}
+\frac1{x^n-\sqrt{x^{2n}+1}}.
\]
(b) Use the method of differences to find \(\sum_{n=1}^{N}u_n\). [3]
(c) Deduce the values of \(x\) for which the infinite series converges and give its sum. [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The product is a difference of two squares:
\[
(x^n-\sqrt{x^{2n}+1})(x^n+\sqrt{x^{2n}+1})
=x^{2n}-(x^{2n}+1)=-1.
\]
Dividing by \(x^n-\sqrt{x^{2n}+1}\) gives the stated identity.
(b) Using part (a),
\[
u_n=\left(x^{n+1}+\sqrt{x^{2n+2}+1}\right)
-\left(x^n+\sqrt{x^{2n}+1}\right).
\]
Thus the sum is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{n=1}^{N}u_n
={}&\left(x^2+\sqrt{x^4+1}-x-\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)\\
&+\left(x^3+\sqrt{x^6+1}-x^2-\sqrt{x^4+1}\right)+\cdots\\
&+\left(x^{N+1}+\sqrt{x^{2N+2}+1}-x^N-\sqrt{x^{2N}+1}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
All intermediate terms cancel, giving
\[
\boxed{\sum_{n=1}^{N}u_n
=x^{N+1}+\sqrt{x^{2N+2}+1}-x-\sqrt{x^2+1}}.
\]
(c) A finite limit requires \(x^{N+1}\to0\), which occurs precisely when \(|x|<1\). Then
\[
\sqrt{x^{2N+2}+1}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Therefore the series converges for \(-1<x<1\), and its sum is
\[
\boxed{1-x-\sqrt{x^2+1}}.
\]

 Completed

\frac{(r+1)(r^2+1)-r\{(r+1)^2+1\}}
{\{(r+1)^2+1\}(r^2+1)}
=\frac{1-r-r^2}{(r^2+2r+2)(r^2+1)},

which proves the identity. Therefore

\frac{r+1}{(r+1)^2+1}-\frac r{r^2+1}

\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{1-r-r^2}{(r^2+2r+2)(r^2+1)}

2021 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 1 · 6 marks
Let
\[
u_r=\frac1{\cos(r+1)\cos r}.
\]
(a) Express \(u_r\) as a difference involving tangents. [2]
(b) Use the method of differences to find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r\). [3]
(c) Explain why the infinite series does not converge. [1]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since
\[
\tan(r+1)-\tan r=\frac{\sin1}{\cos(r+1)\cos r},
\]
\[
u_r=\frac{\tan(r+1)-\tan r}{\sin1}.
\]
(b) Therefore
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r
=\frac1{\sin1}\{(\tan2-\tan1)+(\tan3-\tan2)+\cdots
+(\tan(n+1)-\tan n)\}.
\]
After cancellation,
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r=\frac{\tan(n+1)-\tan1}{\sin1}}.
\]
(c) The sequence \(\tan(n+1)\) does not approach a finite limit, so the partial sums have no limit. Hence the infinite series diverges.

2021 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 2 · 8 marks

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)(r+2)
=\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^3+3r^2+2r)
\]
\[
=\left\{\frac{n(n+1)}2\right\}^2
+\frac12n(n+1)(2n+1)+n(n+1)
\]
\[
=\boxed{\frac14n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)}.
\]
(b) Write
\[
\frac1{r(r+1)(r+2)}
=\frac12\left[\frac1{r(r+1)}-\frac1{(r+1)(r+2)}\right],

\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{r(r+1)(r+2)}
=\frac12\left[

+\cdots
+\frac1{n(n+1)}-\frac1{(n+1)(n+2)}
\right]
\]

=\frac12\left(\frac12-\frac1{(n+1)(n+2)}\right),
\]
so

\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{r(r+1)(r+2)}

2021 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 3 · 7 marks
Let
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}\ln\frac{r(r+2)}{(r+1)^2}.
\]
(a) Show that
\[
S_n=\ln\frac{n+2}{2(n+1)}.
\]
[4]
Let \(S\) be the corresponding sum to infinity.
(b) Find the least \(n\) for which \(S_n-S<0.01\). [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Write the summand as
\[
\ln r-2\ln(r+1)+\ln(r+2).
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_n={}&(\ln1-2\ln2+\ln3)
+(\ln2-2\ln3+\ln4)+\cdots\\
&+(\ln n-2\ln(n+1)+\ln(n+2)).
\end{aligned}
\]
After cancellation,
\[
S_n=-\ln2-\ln(n+1)+\ln(n+2)
=\ln\frac{n+2}{2(n+1)}.
\]
(b) Taking \(n\to\infty\) gives
\[
S=\ln\frac12=-\ln2.
\]
Hence
\[
S_n-S=\ln\frac{n+2}{n+1}.
\]
We require
\[
\ln\frac{n+2}{n+1}<0.01
\]
Exponentiating,
\[
\frac{n+2}{n+1}<e^{0.01}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
n>\frac{2-e^{0.01}}{e^{0.01}-1}=98.5008\ldots.
\]
Therefore the least integer value is
\[
\boxed{n=99}.
\]

Let
\[

\]
(a) Find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r\) in terms of \(n\) and \(x\). [3]
(b) Deduce the non-zero values of \(x\) for which the infinite series converges and give its sum. [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(e^{2x}-2e^x+1=(e^x-1)^2\),
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r
=(e^x-1)^2\sum_{r=1}^{n}e^{rx}.
\]
For \(x\ne0\), the geometric sum is
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}e^{rx}
=\frac{e^x(e^{nx}-1)}{e^x-1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r=e^x(e^x-1)(e^{nx}-1)}.
\]
(b) Since \(x\ne0\), the only \(n\)-dependent factor is \(e^{nx}\). A finite limit exists precisely when \(e^{nx}\to0\), i.e. when \(x<0\). Then
\[
e^x(e^x-1)(e^{nx}-1)\longrightarrow-e^x(e^x-1),
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}u_r=e^x(1-e^x)}.
\]

\[
(2^2-1^2)+(3^2-2^2)+\cdots+\{(n+1)^2-n^2\}
=2\sum_{r=1}^{n}r+n.
\]
The left side telescopes to \((n+1)^2-1\), so
\[
2\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=(n+1)^2-1-n=n(n+1).
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1)}.
\]
(b) Using part (a),
\[
\frac12n(n+1)+an=n^2,
\]
As \(n>0\), divide by \(n\):
\[
\frac{n+1}{2}+a=n.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{a=\frac{n-1}{2}}.
\]

2024 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 5 · 9 marks
It is given that
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r,
\qquad
u_r=x^{f(r)}-x^{f(r+1)},
\qquad x>0.
\]
(a) Find \(S_n\) in terms of \(n,x\) and \(f\). [2]
(b) For \(f(r)=\ln r\), determine when the infinite series converges and give its sum. [3]
(c) For \(f(r)=2\log_x r\), \(x\ne1\), find \(\sum_{n=1}^{N}S_n\) in fully factorised form. [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The defining difference telescopes:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_n={}&\{x^{f(1)}-x^{f(2)}\}
+\{x^{f(2)}-x^{f(3)}\}+\cdots\\
&+\{x^{f(n)}-x^{f(n+1)}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{S_n=x^{f(1)}-x^{f(n+1)}}.
\]
(b) For \(f(r)=\ln r\),
\[
x^{f(r)}=x^{\ln r}=r^{\ln x}.
\]
Since \(f(1)=0\),
\[
S_n=1-(n+1)^{\ln x}.
\]
If \(0<x<1\), then \(\ln x<0\) and \((n+1)^{\ln x}\to0\), so the sum is \(1\). If \(x=1\), every term is zero and the sum is \(0\). If \(x>1\), then \(\ln x>0\) and the partial sums have no finite limit. Thus the series converges for \(0<x\le1\), with the two sums stated above.
(c) For \(f(r)=2\log_x r\) and \(x\ne1\),
\[
x^{f(r)}=x^{2\log_x r}=r^2,
\]
so
\[
S_n=1-(n+1)^2=-n(n+2).
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}S_n
=-\sum_{n=1}^{N}(n^2+2n)
=-\frac{N(N+1)(2N+1)}6-N(N+1)
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{\sum_{n=1}^{N}S_n=-\frac16N(N+1)(2N+7)}.
\]

=\frac{2r+1}{(r^2+1)(r^2+2r+2)},
\]
as required.
(c) Therefore the sum is
\[
\left(\frac12-\frac15\right)
+\left(\frac15-\frac1{10}\right)+\cdots
+\left(\frac1{n^2+1}-\frac1{(n+1)^2+1}\right).
\]
The intermediate terms cancel, giving
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{2r+1}{(r^2+1)(r^2+2r+2)}
=\frac12-\frac1{(n+1)^2+1}}.
\]
(d) Since \(1/\{(n+1)^2+1\}\to0\), the sum to infinity is \(\boxed{\frac12}\).

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/M/J/2025, Q1.





2025 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 1 · 9 marks
(a) Find
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(8r^3+12r^2+4r+3).
\]
[3]
(b) Show that
\[
\frac1{r^4}-\frac1{(r+1)^4}
=\frac{4r^3+6r^2+4r+1}{r^4(r+1)^4},
\]
and hence find the corresponding sum to \(n\). [5]
(c) Deduce the sum to infinity. [1]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Using the standard formulae,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(8r^3+12r^2+4r+3)
={}&8\left\{\frac{n(n+1)}2\right\}^2\\
&+2n(n+1)(2n+1)+2n(n+1)+3n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Collecting and factorising gives
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}(8r^3+12r^2+4r+3)
=n(2n^3+8n^2+10n+7)}.
\]
(b) First,
\[
\frac1{r^4}-\frac1{(r+1)^4}
=\frac{(r+1)^4-r^4}{r^4(r+1)^4}
=\frac{4r^3+6r^2+4r+1}{r^4(r+1)^4},
\]
as required. Hence
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{4r^3+6r^2+4r+1}{r^4(r+1)^4}
=\left(1-\frac1{2^4}\right)
+\left(\frac1{2^4}-\frac1{3^4}\right)+\cdots
+\left(\frac1{n^4}-\frac1{(n+1)^4}\right).
\]
The intermediate terms cancel, so
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{4r^3+6r^2+4r+1}{r^4(r+1)^4}
=1-\frac1{(n+1)^4}}.
\]
(c) Since \(1/(n+1)^4\to0\), the sum to infinity is \(\boxed{1}\).

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2025, Q1; 9231/13/O/N/2025, Q1.





2025 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 1 · 9 marks
(a) Find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^3-r)\) in fully factorised form. [3]
(b) Express
\[
\frac{r+3}{r^3-r}
\]
as \(A/(r-1)+B/r+C/(r+1)\), and hence find its sum from \(r=2\) to \(n\). [5]
(c) Deduce the sum to infinity. [1]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a)
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^3-r)
=\left\{\frac{n(n+1)}2\right\}^2-\frac{n(n+1)}2
\]
\[
=\frac14n(n+1)\{n(n+1)-2\}
=\boxed{\frac14n(n-1)(n+1)(n+2)}.
\]
(b) Since \(r^3-r=(r-1)r(r+1)\), set
\[
\frac{r+3}{(r-1)r(r+1)}
=\frac{A}{r-1}+\frac Br+\frac C{r+1}.
\]
Multiplying through by \((r-1)r(r+1)\) gives
\[
r+3=Ar(r+1)+B(r-1)(r+1)+Cr(r-1).
\]
Using \(r=1,0,-1\) gives \(A=2\), \(B=-3\), \(C=1\). Thus
\[
\frac{r+3}{r^3-r}=\frac2{r-1}-\frac3r+\frac1{r+1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=2}^{n}\frac{r+3}{r^3-r}
={}&\left(2-\frac32+\frac13\right)
+\left(1-1+\frac14\right)+\cdots\\
&+\left(\frac2{n-1}-\frac3n+\frac1{n+1}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Collecting the uncancelled terms gives
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=2}^{n}\frac{r+3}{r^3-r}
=\frac32-\frac2n+\frac1{n+1}}.
\]
(c) Letting \(n\to\infty\), the two remaining \(n\)-dependent fractions tend to zero, so the sum to infinity is \(\boxed{\frac32}\).

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2025, Q1.





2025 October/November · 9231/14 · Question 3 · 9 marks
(a) Use standard results to show that
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)
=\frac14n(n^3+bn^2+cn+d),
\]
and determine \(b,c,d\). [3]
(b) Express \(2/[(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)]\) in partial fractions and hence find its sum from \(r=1\) to \(n\). [5]
(c) State the sum to infinity. [1]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Expand the summand:
\[
(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)=r^3+6r^2+11r+6.
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)
=\left\{\frac{n(n+1)}2\right\}^2
+n(n+1)(2n+1)
+\frac{11}{2}n(n+1)+6n
\]
\[
=\frac14n(n^3+10n^2+35n+50).
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{b=10,\quad c=35,\quad d=50}.
\]
(b) Use
\[
\frac2{(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)}
=\frac1{(r+1)(r+2)}-\frac1{(r+2)(r+3)}.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac2{(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)}
={}&\left(\frac1{2\cdot3}-\frac1{3\cdot4}\right)\\
&+\left(\frac1{3\cdot4}-\frac1{4\cdot5}\right)+\cdots\\
&+\left(\frac1{(n+1)(n+2)}-\frac1{(n+2)(n+3)}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
After cancellation,
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac2{(r+1)(r+2)(r+3)}
=\frac16-\frac1{(n+2)(n+3)}}.
\]
(c) The final fraction tends to zero, so the sum to infinity is \(\boxed{\frac16}\).

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/O/N/2025, Q3.

title: 1.5 Polar coordinates
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

理解 Cartesian coordinates 与 polar coordinates 的关系，并在两种形式之间转换点和曲线方程；
按照 \(r\geqslant0\) 的约定，在指定的 \(\theta\) 区间内描绘简单极坐标曲线；
在图中标出对称性、与 initial line 的交点、曲线在 pole 附近的形状，以及 \(r\) 的最大值和最小值；

title: 1.5 Polar coordinates
text:
学习路线


能在 Cartesian coordinates 与 principal polar coordinates 之间转换
能把直线、圆和简单代数曲线的方程转换为极坐标形式或 Cartesian 形式
作图前能确定定义域、\(r=0\)、initial-line intersections、对称性和极值

能准确确定面积积分的角度上下限，并利用对称性简化积分

title: 1.5 Polar coordinates
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Polar coordinates of a point
点 \(P\) 的极坐标写成 \((r,\theta)\)：\(r\) 是 \(P\) 到 pole \(O\) 的距离，\(\theta\) 是从 initial line 逆时针量到 \(OP\) 的角，通常用弧度表示。
同一点有无限多种表示：
\[
(r,\theta)\equiv(r,\theta+2k\pi),\; k\in\mathbb Z.
\]
本教材的 principal polar coordinates 满足
\[
r>0,\; -\pi<\theta\leqslant\pi.
\]
在 pole 处 \(r=0\)，而 \(\theta\) 没有唯一值。


1.2 Converting points and equations
两种坐标之间的基本关系是
\[
x=r\cos\theta,\; y=r\sin\theta,
\; r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2},\; \tan\theta=\frac yx.
\]
由 Cartesian coordinates 求 \(\theta\) 时，必须结合点所在象限选择正确的角，不能只使用计算器给出的 \(\arctan(y/x)\)。
转换曲线方程时常用
\[
r^2=x^2+y^2,\; r\cos\theta=x,\; r\sin\theta=y.
\]
如果极坐标式中仍含 \(\sin\theta\) 或 \(\cos\theta\)，可乘以适当的 \(r\) 的幂，使它们与 \(x\)、\(y\) 配对。平方消去根号时，应保留原极坐标方程所给的 \(r\) 与 \(\theta\) 范围。


1.3 Sketching a polar curve
作图时依次检查：

Range of \(\theta\) and the convention \(r\geqslant0\)：先确定题目要求的角度范围，再排除使 \(r<0\) 的部分；
Pole：解 \(r=0\)，确定曲线从哪些方向到达或离开 pole；
Initial line：检查 \(\theta=0\)，以及区间内与 initial line 同方向的角；
Symmetry：比较 \(r(-\theta)\)、\(r(\pi-\theta)\) 或观察函数的周期；
Least and greatest values of \(r\)：由三角函数范围或微分求极值；
Direction and shape：取少量关键角，按 \(\theta\) 增大的方向连接。







注记Convention used in this course



若公式给出 \(r<0\)，本课程不把点画到相反方向，也不以虚线延伸；只绘制 \(r\geqslant0\) 的部分。




1.4 Symmetry tests
以下代换可帮助判断对称性：
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{test} & \text{possible symmetry}\\ \hline
\theta\mapsto-\theta & \text{initial line}\\
\theta\mapsto\pi-\theta & \theta=\frac\pi2\\
\theta\mapsto\theta+\pi & \text{pole}
\end{array}
\]
即使方程形式在代换后不完全相同，也可根据给定区间、周期和关键点确认实际图形的对称性。


1.5 Distances from lines
点 \((r,\theta)\) 到 initial line 的垂直距离为
\[
|y|=|r\sin\theta|.
\]
在第一象限内可直接使用 \(r\sin\theta\)。点到半直线 \(\theta=\alpha\) 所在直线的垂直距离为
\[
|r\sin(\theta-\alpha)|.
\]
求最远点时，应对相应距离函数微分，并检查端点以及区间内部的 stationary points。


1.6 Intersections of polar curves
在共同的 \(\theta\) 范围内令两个 \(r\) 表达式相等。还必须单独检查 pole，因为不同的 \(\theta\) 值都可能表示 \(r=0\) 的同一点。
若一条曲线是直线 \(r\sin\theta=c\)，它的 Cartesian equation 是 \(y=c\)；这有时能帮助判断交点个数和位置。


1.7 Area enclosed by a polar curve
曲线 \(r=f(\theta)\)、半直线 \(\theta=\alpha\) 与 \(\theta=\beta\) 所围区域的面积为
\[
\boxed{A=\frac12\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,\mathrm d\theta}.
\]
选择上下限前，应先由 \(r=0\)、曲线交点或题目给出的半直线确定边界。若图形关于某条直线对称，可只积一半再乘以 \(2\)。
两条曲线之间的面积通常写成
\[
A=\frac12\int_\alpha^\beta
\left(r_{\text{outer}}^2-r_{\text{inner}}^2\right)\,\mathrm d\theta.
\]

title: 1.5 Polar coordinates
text:
2. Textbook Examples

Example 5.1 · Pages 118–119
(i) Find the Cartesian coordinates of:
\[
\left(4,\frac{2\pi}{3}\right),\;
\left(12,-\frac\pi6\right).
\]
(ii) Find the principal polar coordinates of:
\[
(-\sqrt3,1),\; (4,-4).
\]


Show solution

(i) Using \(x=r\cos\theta\) and \(y=r\sin\theta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
x&=4\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-2,&
y&=4\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}=2\sqrt3,\\
x&=12\cos\left(-\frac\pi6\right)=6\sqrt3,&
y&=12\sin\left(-\frac\pi6\right)=-6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the Cartesian coordinates are
\[
\boxed{(-2,2\sqrt3)},\;
\boxed{(6\sqrt3,-6)}.
\]
(ii) For \((-\sqrt3,1)\),
\[
r=\sqrt{(-\sqrt3)^2+1^2}=2.
\]
The point is in quadrant II and its reference angle is \(\pi/6\), so
\[
\boxed{\left(2,\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)}.
\]
For \((4,-4)\),
\[
r=\sqrt{4^2+(-4)^2}=4\sqrt2.
\]
The point is in quadrant IV, so the principal angle is \(-\pi/4\). Thus
\[
\boxed{\left(4\sqrt2,-\frac\pi4\right)}.
\]



Example 5.1: points in polar and Cartesian form

Each point is located by a radius from the pole and an angle from the initial line.   Example 5.1: points in polar and Cartesian form initial lineyO(4, 2π/3)(12, −π/6)(−√3, 1)(4, −4)


Each point is located by a radius from the pole and an angle from the initial line.



 Completed


Example 5.2 · Pages 120–121
Find polar equations of the curves
\[
\text{(i) }x^2-y^2=9,\;
\text{(ii) }y=x+4.
\]


Show solution

(i) Substitute \(x=r\cos\theta\) and \(y=r\sin\theta\):
\[
r^2(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta)=9.
\]
Since \(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta=\cos2\theta\),
\[
\boxed{r^2=9\sec2\theta}.
\]
(ii) Substitution gives
\[
r\sin\theta=r\cos\theta+4,
\]
so
\[
r(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)=4.
\]
Using
\[
\sin\theta-\cos\theta
=\sqrt2\sin\left(\theta-\frac\pi4\right),
\]
the required equation is
\[
\boxed{r=2\sqrt2\,\operatorname{cosec}\left(\theta-\frac\pi4\right)}.
\]



Example 5.2: Cartesian curves before conversion

The same geometric curves can be described by polar equations.   Example 5.2: Cartesian curves before conversion initial lineyOx² − y² = 9y = x + 4


The same geometric curves can be described by polar equations.



 Completed


Example 5.3 · Page 121
Find Cartesian equations of the curves
\[
\text{(i) }r=5,\;
\text{(ii) }r^2=4\sin\theta.
\]


Show solution

(i) Since \(r^2=x^2+y^2\),
\[
\boxed{x^2+y^2=25}.
\]
(ii) Multiply by \(r\):
\[
r^3=4r\sin\theta=4y.
\]
Squaring and using \(r^2=x^2+y^2\) gives
\[
r^6=16y^2,
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{(x^2+y^2)^3=16y^2}.
\]



Example 5.3: r = 5 and r² = 4 sin θ

The plotted polar curves correspond to the derived Cartesian equations.   Example 5.3: r = 5 and r² = 4 sin θ initial lineyO-55r = 5r² = 4 sin θ


The plotted polar curves correspond to the derived Cartesian equations.



 Completed


Example 5.4 · Page 124
Sketch the graphs of
\[
\text{(i) }r=3,\;
\text{(ii) }\theta=\frac\pi4.
\]


Show solution

For \(r=3\), every point is a distance \(3\) from the pole, so the graph is a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \(3\). It crosses the initial line at \((3,0)\).
For \(\theta=\pi/4\), the angle is fixed while \(r\geqslant0\) varies. The graph is therefore a half-line from the pole at angle \(\pi/4\); it is not the complete Cartesian line \(y=x\).



Example 5.4: a constant radius and a constant angle

A constant r gives a circle; a constant θ gives a half-line.   Example 5.4: a constant radius and a constant angle initial lineyO-33r = 3θ = π/4(3, 0)


A constant r gives a circle; a constant θ gives a half-line.



 Completed


Example 5.5 · Page 125
A curve is defined by
\[
r=5\cos^2\theta.
\]
(i) Create a table of values for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\).
(ii) Plot the curve for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant2\pi\).
(iii) State the least and greatest values of \(r\) and the values of \(\theta\) at which they occur.


Show solution

At intervals of \(\pi/12\) from \(0\) to \(\pi/2\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
\theta&0&\frac\pi{12}&\frac\pi6&\frac\pi4&\frac\pi3&\frac{5\pi}{12}&\frac\pi2\\ \hline
r&5&4.67&3.75&2.50&1.25&0.34&0
\end{array}
\]
The values are reflected between \(\pi/2\) and \(\pi\) and repeat with period \(\pi\). The initial line is an axis of symmetry.
Since \(0\leqslant\cos^2\theta\leqslant1\),
\[
\boxed{r_{\max}=5\text{ at }\theta=0,\pi},
\]
and
\[
\boxed{r_{\min}=0\text{ at }\theta=\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}{2}}.
\]



Example 5.5: r = 5 cos² θ

The curve is symmetric about both coordinate axes and reaches the pole when cos θ = 0.   Example 5.5: r = 5 cos² θ initial lineyO-55r = 5r = 5


The curve is symmetric about both coordinate axes and reaches the pole when cos θ = 0.



 Completed


Example 5.6 · Page 126
Find the least and greatest values of \(r\) for
\[
r=3+2\cos4\theta
\]
and the values of \(\theta\) at which they occur. Hence sketch the graph.


Show solution

The least value is
\[
3-2=1,
\]
which occurs when \(\cos4\theta=-1\). For \(-\pi<\theta\leqslant\pi\), this gives
\[
\theta=\pm\frac\pi4,\ \pm\frac{3\pi}{4}.
\]
The greatest value is
\[
3+2=5,
\]
which occurs when \(\cos4\theta=1\), including
\[
\theta=0,\ \pm\frac\pi2,\ \pi.
\]
The function has period \(\pi/2\), so the graph repeats in each quadrant and has rotational symmetry of order \(4\). It never reaches the pole because \(r\geqslant1\).



Example 5.6: r = 3 + 2 cos 4θ

Fourfold rotational symmetry; 1 ≤ r ≤ 5.   Example 5.6: r = 3 + 2 cos 4θ initial lineyO-11-55


Fourfold rotational symmetry; 1 ≤ r ≤ 5.



 Completed


Example 5.7 · Pages 126–129
A curve is given by
\[
r=\theta(\pi-\theta).
\]
(i) Plot the curve for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\), where \(r\) is non-negative.
(ii) Create tables of values for \(\pi\leqslant\theta\leqslant3\pi/2\) and \(-\pi/2\leqslant\theta\leqslant0\).
(iii) Sketch the curve for \(-\pi/2\leqslant\theta\leqslant3\pi/2\) using the convention for this course.


Show solution

For \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\), \(r\geqslant0\). The curve starts at the pole when \(\theta=0\), reaches its greatest radius at \(\theta=\pi/2\), and returns to the pole at \(\theta=\pi\):
\[
r_{\max}=\frac\pi2\left(\pi-\frac\pi2\right)=\frac{\pi^2}{4}.
\]
Outside this interval, \(\theta(\pi-\theta)<0\). For instance,
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
\theta&\pi&\frac{7\pi}{6}&\frac{4\pi}{3}&\frac{3\pi}{2}\\ \hline
r&0&-\frac{7\pi^2}{36}&-\frac{4\pi^2}{9}&-\frac{3\pi^2}{4}
\end{array}
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
\theta&-\frac\pi2&-\frac\pi3&-\frac\pi6&0\\ \hline
r&-\frac{3\pi^2}{4}&-\frac{4\pi^2}{9}&-\frac{7\pi^2}{36}&0.
\end{array}
\]
Under the convention \(r\geqslant0\), these negative-radius portions are omitted. The required graph therefore consists only of the loop traced for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\).



Example 5.7: r = θ(π − θ), r ≥ 0

Only the interval 0 ≤ θ ≤ π is drawn because the stated course convention excludes negative r.   Example 5.7: r = θ(π − θ), r ≥ 0 initial lineyOr = π²/4


Only the interval 0 ≤ θ ≤ π is drawn because the stated course convention excludes negative r.



 Completed


Example 5.8 · Pages 132–133
The curve has equation
\[
r=1+2\cos\theta.
\]
Find the area enclosed, using the convention \(r\geqslant0\).


Show solution

The curve reaches the pole when
\[
1+2\cos\theta=0
\Longrightarrow
\cos\theta=-\frac12.
\]
The relevant limiting angles are \(\theta=\pm2\pi/3\). By symmetry about the initial line,
\[
A=2\left(\frac12\int_0^{2\pi/3}(1+2\cos\theta)^2\,\mathrm d\theta\right).
\]
Using \(4\cos^2\theta=2+2\cos2\theta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A
&=\int_0^{2\pi/3}(3+4\cos\theta+2\cos2\theta)\,\mathrm d\theta\\
&=\left[3\theta+4\sin\theta+\sin2\theta\right]_0^{2\pi/3}\\
&=2\pi+2\sqrt3-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{A=2\pi+\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}}.
\]



Example 5.8: r = 1 + 2 cos θ

The curve reaches the pole at θ = ±2π/3 and is symmetric about the initial line.   Example 5.8: r = 1 + 2 cos θ initial lineyO-11-33θ = 2π/3θ = −2π/3(3, 0)


The curve reaches the pole at θ = ±2π/3 and is symmetric about the initial line.



 Completed

title: 1.5 Polar coordinates
section: 3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
text:
3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook






注记



本节只收录教材 Exercise 中明确标有 Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics 来源的题目。题目以英文与 LaTeX 重排，图形由方程重新绘制。




Exercise 5B · Question 9 · Page 131
The curves \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) have polar equations
\[
C_1:r=\frac12,\; 0\leqslant\theta\leqslant2\pi,
\]
and
\[
C_2:r=\sin\frac\theta2,\; 0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi.
\]
Find the polar coordinates of the point of intersection of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\). Sketch \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) on the same diagram.


Show solution

At an intersection away from the pole, the two curves have the same \(r\) and \(\theta\):
\[
\sin\frac\theta2=\frac12.
\]
Since \(0\leqslant\theta/2\leqslant\pi/2\),
\[
\frac\theta2=\frac\pi6
\Longrightarrow
\theta=\frac\pi3.
\]
Thus the point of intersection is
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac12,\frac\pi3\right)}.
\]
\(C_1\) is the circle with centre at the pole and radius \(1/2\). The curve \(C_2\) starts at the pole, passes through the stated intersection and reaches \((-1,0)\) when \(\theta=\pi\).



Exercise 5B Q9: two polar curves

The circle and C₂ meet at θ = π/3.   Exercise 5B Q9: two polar curves initial lineyOC₁: r = 1/2C₂: r = sin(θ/2)(1/2, π/3)


The circle and C₂ meet at θ = π/3.



 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2015, Q5 (part question).





Exercise 5C · Question 9 · Page 134
The curve \(C\) has polar equation
\[
r=a(1+\sin\theta),\; 0\leqslant\theta<2\pi,
\]
where \(a\) is a positive constant. Draw a sketch of \(C\).
Find the exact area of the region enclosed by \(C\) and the half-lines \(\theta=\pi/3\) and \(\theta=2\pi/3\).


Show solution

The curve is symmetric about \(\theta=\pi/2\). It has
\[
r=2a\text{ at }\theta=\frac\pi2,\;
r=0\text{ at }\theta=\frac{3\pi}{2},
\]
and meets the initial line at \(r=a\).
The required area is
\[
A=\frac12a^2\int_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}(1+\sin\theta)^2\,\mathrm d\theta.
\]
Since
\[
(1+\sin\theta)^2
=\frac32+2\sin\theta-\frac12\cos2\theta,
\]
we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
A
&=\frac{a^2}{2}
\left[
\frac32\theta-2\cos\theta-\frac14\sin2\theta
\right]_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}\\
&=\frac{a^2}{2}left(\frac\pi2+2+\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{A=\frac{a^2}{8}\left(2\pi+8+\sqrt3\right)}.
\]



Exercise 5C Q9: r = a(1 + sin θ)

The required sector lies between the two coral half-lines; the drawing is scaled with a = 1.   Exercise 5C Q9: r = a(1 + sin θ) initial lineyOθ = π/3θ = 2π/3r = 2a


The required sector lies between the two coral half-lines; the drawing is scaled with a = 1.



 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2014, Q5.





Exercise 5C · Question 10 · Page 134
The curve \(C\) has polar equation
\[
r=2+2\cos\theta,\; 0\leqslant\theta<\pi.
\]
Sketch \(C\). Find the area of the region \(R\) enclosed by \(C\) and the initial line.
The half-line \(\theta=\pi/5\) divides \(R\) into two parts. Find the area of each part, correct to \(3\) decimal places.


Show solution

The curve starts at \((4,0)\) and reaches the pole at \(\theta=\pi\). The required region is the part above the initial line.
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{area}(R)
&=\frac12\int_0^\pi(2+2\cos\theta)^2\,\mathrm d\theta\\
&=\int_0^\pi(3+4\cos\theta+\cos2\theta)\,\mathrm d\theta\\
&=\left[3\theta+4\sin\theta+\frac12\sin2\theta\right]_0^\pi\\
&=\boxed{3\pi}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The area between \(\theta=0\) and \(\theta=\pi/5\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_1
&=\left[3\theta+4\sin\theta+\frac12\sin2\theta\right]_0^{\pi/5}\\
&=4.71163\ldots\\
&=\boxed{4.712}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The remaining area is
\[
A_2=3\pi-A_1=4.71315\ldots=\boxed{4.713}.
\]

The half-line θ = π/5 divides the upper half-cardioid into the two required regions.   Exercise 5C Q10: r = 2 + 2 cos θ initial lineyO-44θ = π/5(4, 0)


The half-line θ = π/5 divides the upper half-cardioid into the two required regions.

title: 1.5 Polar coordinates

4. Past-paper question bank






注记



以下题目按完全相同的地区版本合并，所有图形均由题目中的极坐标方程重新绘制，答案依据对应的 Cambridge mark scheme 展开。



2019



2019 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 11 EITHER · 14 marks
\(C_1\) has equation \(r^2=2\theta\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\). The point \(P\) is furthest from the line \(\theta=\pi/2\).
(i) Show that \(2\theta\tan\theta=1\) at \(P\), and verify a root between \(0.6\) and \(0.7\). [5]
\(C_2\) has equation \(r^2=\theta\sec^2\theta\) for \(0\leqslant\theta<\pi/2\). The curves meet at the pole and at \(Q\).
(ii) Find the exact value of \(\theta\) at \(Q\). [2]
(iii) Sketch \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) together. [2]
(iv) Find exactly the area enclosed by the curves. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Distance from \(\theta=\pi/2\) is \(x=r\cos\theta=(2\theta)^{1/2}\cos\theta\). Hence
\[
\frac{dx}{d\theta}=(2\theta)^{1/2}\left(\frac{\cos\theta}{2\theta}-\sin\theta\right)=0
\Longrightarrow \boxed{2\theta\tan\theta=1}.
\]
For \(f(\theta)=2\theta\tan\theta-1\),
\[f(0.6)=-0.179<0,\; f(0.7)=0.179>0,\]
so a root lies in \((0.6,0.7)\).
(ii) Away from the pole,
\[2\theta=\theta\sec^2\theta\Longrightarrow\cos^2\theta=\frac12,\]
so \(\boxed{\theta=\pi/4}\).
(iv) \(C_1\) is outside \(C_2\) for \(0<\theta<\pi/4\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/4}\left(2\theta-\theta\sec^2\theta\right)d\theta\\
&=\boxed{\frac{\pi^2}{32}-\frac\pi8+\frac14\ln2}.
\end{aligned}
\]



2019 M/J 11–12: C₁ and C₂

The curves meet at θ = π/4; the shaded-area calculation uses 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/4.   2019 M/J 11–12: C₁ and C₂ initial lineyOC₁C₂Q


The curves meet at θ = π/4; the shaded-area calculation uses 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/4.




Sources: 9231/11/M/J/2019 Q11 EITHER; 9231/12/M/J/2019 Q11 EITHER.





2019 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 2 · 7 marks
\(C\) has equation \(r^2=\ln(1+\theta)\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant2\pi\).
(i) Sketch \(C\). [2]
(ii) Find exactly the area bounded by \(C\) and the initial line. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

The curve starts at the pole, spirals anticlockwise with increasing \(r\), and returns to the initial line at \(\theta=2\pi\); it is tangent to the initial line at the pole.
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}\ln(1+\theta)d\theta\\
&=\frac12\int_1^{2\pi+1}\ln u\,du\\
&=\frac12[u\ln u-u]_1^{2\pi+1}\\
&=\boxed{\left(\pi+\frac12\right)\ln(2\pi+1)-\pi}.
\end{aligned}
\]



2019 M/J 13: r² = ln(1 + θ)

An increasing anticlockwise spiral, tangent to the initial line at the pole.   2019 M/J 13: r² = ln(1 + θ) initial lineyO


An increasing anticlockwise spiral, tangent to the initial line at the pole.




Source: 9231/13/M/J/2019 Q2.





2019 October/November · 9231/11, /12 & /13 · Question 11 EITHER · 14 marks
For \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\),
\[C_1:r=2(e^\theta+e^{-\theta}),\; C_2:r=e^{2\theta}-e^{-2\theta}.\]
The curves meet at \(P\) where \(\theta=\alpha\).
(i) Show that \(e^{2\alpha}-2e^\alpha-1=0\), find \(\alpha\) exactly and show that \(r=4\sqrt2\) at \(P\). [6]
(ii) Sketch both curves. [3]
(iii) Find to \(3\) significant figures the area enclosed by the curves and initial line. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

Equating radii and dividing by \(e^\alpha+e^{-\alpha}\) gives \(e^\alpha-e^{-\alpha}=2\), hence
\[e^{2\alpha}-2e^\alpha-1=0,\; e^\alpha=1+\sqrt2,\]
so
\[\boxed{\alpha=\ln(1+\sqrt2)},\; \boxed{r=4\sqrt2}.\]
The required area is
\[
\frac12\int_0^\alpha\left[4(e^\theta+e^{-\theta})^2-(e^{2\theta}-e^{-2\theta})^2\right]d\theta.
\]
After expansion this equals
\[
\left[5\theta+e^{2\theta}-e^{-2\theta}-\frac18e^{4\theta}+\frac18e^{-4\theta}\right]_0^\alpha
=5\alpha+\sqrt2.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{A=5.82}\) to \(3\) significant figures.



2019 O/N: exponential polar curves

The curves and the initial line enclose the required region before P.   2019 O/N: exponential polar curves initial lineyOC₁C₂P


The curves and the initial line enclose the required region before P.




Sources: 9231/11/O/N/2019 Q11 EITHER; 9231/12/O/N/2019 Q11 EITHER; 9231/13/O/N/2019 Q11 EITHER.




2020



2020 May/June · 9231/11 & /12 · Question 7 · 12 marks
\(C_1:r=\theta\cos\theta\) and \(C_2:r=\theta\sin\theta\), for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\).
(a) Show that the point of \(C_1\) furthest from \(\theta=\pi/2\) satisfies \(2\theta\tan\theta-1=0\), and verify a root in \((0.6,0.7)\). [5]
(b) Find the non-pole intersection. [2] (c) Sketch both curves. [3] (d) Find the enclosed area exactly. [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(x=r\cos\theta=\theta\cos^2\theta\), so
\[\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\cos^2\theta-2\theta\sin\theta\cos\theta=0
\Longrightarrow 2\theta\tan\theta-1=0.\]
The values at \(0.6\) and \(0.7\) are \(-0.179\) and \(0.179\), establishing the root. At the other intersection,
\[\theta\cos\theta=\theta\sin\theta\Longrightarrow\boxed{(r,\theta)=\left(\frac\pi{4\sqrt2},\frac\pi4\right)}.\]
Finally,
\[
A=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/4}\theta^2(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta)d\theta
=\boxed{\frac{\pi^2}{64}-\frac18}.
\]



2020 M/J 11–12: C₁ and C₂

The curves meet away from the pole at θ = π/4.   2020 M/J 11–12: C₁ and C₂ initial lineyOC₁C₂Q


The curves meet away from the pole at θ = π/4.




Sources: 9231/11/M/J/2020 Q7; 9231/12/M/J/2020 Q7.





2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 5 · 6 marks
\(C:r=a\tan\theta\), where \(a>0\) and \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/4\).
(a) Sketch \(C\) and state the greatest distance from the pole. [2]
(b) Find exactly the area bounded by \(C\) and \(\theta=\pi/4\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(r\) increases from \(0\) to \(a\), so the greatest distance is \(\boxed{a}\).
\[
A=\frac{a^2}{2}\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^2\theta\,d\theta
=\frac{a^2}{2}[\tan\theta-\theta]_0^{\pi/4}
=\boxed{\frac{a^2}{2}\left(1-\frac\pi4\right)}.
\]



2020 M/J 13: r = a tan θ

Scaled with a = 1; the greatest radius is a.   2020 M/J 13: r = a tan θ initial lineyOθ = π/4
