2020 October/November · 9231/11 & /13 · Question 7 · 11 marks
(a) Show that \((x^2+y^2)^{5/2}=4xy(x^2-y^2)\) has polar equation \(r=\sin4\theta\). [4]
For \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/4\), (b) sketch the curve and state its symmetry line; [3] (c) find its enclosed area exactly. [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

Substitution gives
\[r^5=4r^4\cos\theta\sin\theta(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta),\]
so \(r=2\sin2\theta\cos2\theta=\boxed{\sin4\theta}\). The single loop is symmetric about \(\boxed{\theta=\pi/8}\).
\[A=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/4}\sin^24\theta\,d\theta
=\frac14\left[\theta-\frac18\sin8\theta\right]_0^{\pi/4}
=\boxed{\frac\pi{16}}.\]



2020 O/N 11–13: r = sin 4θ

A single loop symmetric about θ = π/8.   2020 O/N 11–13: r = sin 4θ initial lineyOθ = π/8


A single loop symmetric about θ = π/8.




Sources: 9231/11/O/N/2020 Q7; 9231/13/O/N/2020 Q7.





2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 5 · 8 marks
\(C:r=\ln(1+\pi-\theta)\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\).
(a) Sketch \(C\) and state the point furthest from the pole. [3]
(b) Find exactly the area bounded by \(C\) and the initial line. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(r\) decreases from \(\ln(1+\pi)\) to \(0\), so the furthest point is \(\boxed{(\ln(1+\pi),0)}\).
With \(u=1+\pi-\theta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_1^{1+\pi}\ln^2u\,du\\
&=\frac12[u(\ln^2u-2\ln u+2)]_1^{1+\pi}\\
&=\boxed{\frac12(1+\pi)\{\ln^2(1+\pi)-2\ln(1+\pi)+2\}-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]



2020 O/N 12: r = ln(1 + π − θ)

The radius decreases from ln(1 + π) to zero.   2020 O/N 12: r = ln(1 + π − θ) initial lineyO


The radius decreases from ln(1 + π) to zero.




Source: 9231/12/O/N/2020 Q5.




2021



2021 May/June · 9231/11 & /12 · Question 5 · 7 marks
\(C:r=a\cot(\pi/3-\theta)\), where \(a>0\), \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/6\), and the greatest radius is \(2\sqrt3\).
(a) Sketch \(C\) and show that \(a=2\). [3] (b) Find the bounded area exactly. [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

At \(\theta=\pi/6\), \(r=a\cot(\pi/6)=a\sqrt3=2\sqrt3\), hence \(\boxed{a=2}\).
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=2\int_0^{\pi/6}\cot^2(\pi/3-\theta)d\theta\\
&=2[-\cot u-u]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}
=\boxed{\frac{4\sqrt3-\pi}{3}}.
\end{aligned}
\]



2021 M/J 11–12: r = 2 cot(π/3 − θ)

The radius increases to 2√3.   2021 M/J 11–12: r = 2 cot(π/3 − θ) initial lineyOθ = π/6


The radius increases to 2√3.




Sources: 9231/11/M/J/2021 Q5; 9231/12/M/J/2021 Q5.





2021 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 5 · 9 marks
For \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\),
\[r=\frac1{\pi-\theta}-\frac1\pi.\]
(a) Sketch \(C\). [3] (b) Show that the area bounded by \(C\) and \(\theta=\pi/2\) is \((3-4\ln2)/(4\pi)\). [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(r\) increases from \(0\) and the curve is tangent to the initial line at the pole.
\[
A=\frac1{2\pi^2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\theta^2}{(\pi-\theta)^2}d\theta.
\]
Let \(u=\pi-\theta\). Then
\[A=\frac1{2\pi^2}\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\left(\frac{\pi^2}{u^2}-\frac{2\pi}{u}+1\right)du
=\boxed{\frac{3-4\ln2}{4\pi}}.\]



2021 M/J 13: reciprocal-difference curve

The curve leaves the pole tangentially and has increasing radius.   2021 M/J 13: reciprocal-difference curve initial lineyO


The curve leaves the pole tangentially and has increasing radius.




Source: 9231/13/M/J/2021 Q5.





2021 October/November · 9231/11 & /13 · Question 6 · 7 marks
\(C:r=2\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\).
(a) Find the point furthest from the pole. [5] (b) Sketch \(C\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

Differentiating gives
\[\frac{dr}{d\theta}=2\{\cos^2\theta-(1+\sin\theta)\sin\theta\}=0.\]
Thus \(1-sin\theta-2\sin^2\theta=0\), so \(\sin\theta=1/2\) in the interval. Hence
\[\boxed{(r,\theta)=\left(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2},\frac\pi6\right)}.\]
The curve begins at \((2,0)\), reaches this maximum, then is tangent to \(\theta=\pi/2\) at the pole.



2021 O/N 11–13

The maximum radius occurs at θ = π/6.   2021 O/N 11–13 initial lineyOmaximum


The maximum radius occurs at θ = π/6.




Sources: 9231/11/O/N/2021 Q6; 9231/13/O/N/2021 Q6.





2021 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 5 · 12 marks
\(C:r=3+2\sin\theta\) for \(-\pi<\theta\leqslant\pi\), and \(l:r\sin\theta=2\).
(a) Complete the sketch. [1] (b) Add \(l\) and find both intersections. [5] (c) Find exactly the area enclosed by \(C\) and \(l\) that contains the pole. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(l\) is \(y=2\). At an intersection,
\[2=(3+2\sin\theta)\sin\theta,\]
giving \(\sin\theta=1/2\). Therefore the intersections are
\[\boxed{(4,\pi/6)},\;\boxed{(4,5\pi/6)}.\]
Using symmetry, the curved part with two radii has area
\[2\cdot\frac12\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/6}(3+2\sin\theta)^2d\theta
=\frac{22\pi}{3}-\frac{13\sqrt3}{2}.\]
Adding the two congruent triangles gives \(4\cos(\pi/6)\times2=4\sqrt3\). Hence
\[\boxed{A=\frac{22\pi}{3}-\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}}.\]



2021 O/N 12: curve and y = 2

The horizontal line y = 2 cuts the symmetric closed curve at two points.   2021 O/N 12: curve and y = 2 initial lineyOC(4, π/6)(4, 5π/6)


The horizontal line y = 2 cuts the symmetric closed curve at two points.




Source: 9231/12/O/N/2021 Q5.




2022



2022 May/June · 9231/11 & /12 · Question 6 · 13 marks
\(C:r^2=\tan^{-1}(\theta/2)\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant2\).
(a) Sketch \(C\) and state exactly its greatest radius. [3]
(b) Find exactly the area bounded by \(C\) and \(\theta=2\). [5]
For \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\), (c) show that the point furthest from \(\theta=\pi/2\) satisfies
\[
(\theta^2+4)\tan^{-1}(\theta/2)\sin\theta-\cos\theta=0,
\]
and verify a root in \((0.6,0.7)\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(r\) increases throughout the interval, so
\[r_{\max}=\sqrt{\tan^{-1}1}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2}}.\]
For the area, integration by parts gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^2\tan^{-1}(\theta/2)d\theta\\
&=\frac12\left[\theta\tan^{-1}(\theta/2)-\ln(\theta^2+4)\right]_0^2\\
&=\boxed{\frac\pi4-\frac12\ln2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For part (c), the perpendicular distance is
\[x=r\cos\theta=\{  an^{-1}(\theta/2)\}^{1/2}\cos\theta.\]
Setting \(dx/d\theta=0\) and clearing the positive factors gives the required equation. Its left side is
\[-0.108\text{ at }\theta=0.6,\; 0.209\text{ at }\theta=0.7,\]
so the root is verified.



2022 M/J 11–12

The radius increases to √π/2.   2022 M/J 11–12 initial lineyOθ = 2


The radius increases to √π/2.




Sources: 9231/11/M/J/2022 Q6; 9231/12/M/J/2022 Q6.





2022 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 6 · 13 marks
\(C\) has Cartesian equation \(x^2+xy+y^2=a\), where \(a>0\).
(a) Show that
\[r^2=\frac{2a}{2+\sin2\theta}.\]
[3] (b) Sketch the part for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/4\). [2]
(c) Find exactly the area enclosed by this part, the initial line and \(\theta=\pi/4\). [8]


Show answer and mark scheme

Substituting \(x=r\cos\theta\) and \(y=r\sin\theta\) gives
\[r^2(1+\sin\theta\cos\theta)=a,\]
hence
\[\boxed{r^2=\frac{2a}{2+\sin2\theta}}.\]
The radius decreases smoothly from \(\sqrt a\) at \(\theta=0\) to \(\sqrt{2a/3}\) at \(\theta=\pi/4\).
Using \(t=\tan\theta\) and \(dt=(1+t^2)d\theta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/4}r^2d\theta
=\frac a2\int_0^1\frac{dt}{t^2+t+1}\\
&=\frac a2\int_0^1\frac{dt}{(t+1/2)^2+3/4}\\
&=\frac a{\sqrt3}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{2t+1}{\sqrt3}\right]_0^1\\
&=\boxed{\frac{\pi a}{6\sqrt3}}.
\end{aligned}
\]



2022 M/J 13

Scaled with a = 1; the radius decreases on 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/4.   2022 M/J 13 initial lineyOθ = π/4


Scaled with a = 1; the radius decreases on 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/4.




Source: 9231/13/M/J/2022 Q6.




2023



2023 October/November · 9231/11 & /13 · Question 6 · 15 marks
(a) Show that \((x-1/2)^2+y^2=1/4\) has polar equation \(r=\cos\theta\). [3]
\(C_1:r=\cos\theta\) and \(C_2:r=\sin2\theta\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\) meet at the pole and \(P\).
(b) Find \(P\). [3] (c) Sketch both curves and mark \(P\). [3] (d) Find exactly the enclosed area containing \(OP\). [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

Expanding the Cartesian equation gives \(x^2-x+y^2=0\), hence
\[r^2-r\cos\theta=0\Longrightarrow\boxed{r=\cos\theta}.\]
At the non-pole intersection,
\[\sin2\theta=\cos\theta\Longrightarrow 2\sin\theta=1,\]
so
\[\boxed{P\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\frac\pi6\right)}.\]
\(C_2\) bounds the region for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/6\), and \(C_1\) for \(\pi/6\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/6}\sin^22\theta\,d\theta
+\frac12\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/2}\cos^2\theta\,d\theta\\
&=\boxed{\frac\pi8-\frac{3\sqrt3}{32}}.
\end{aligned}
\]



2023 O/N 11–13: C₁ and C₂

The required region is bounded by different curves on either side of P.   2023 O/N 11–13: C₁ and C₂ initial lineyOC₁C₂P


The required region is bounded by different curves on either side of P.




Sources: 9231/11/O/N/2023 Q6; 9231/13/O/N/2023 Q6.





2023 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 6 · 13 marks
\[C:r=e^{-\theta}-e^{-\pi/2},\;0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2.\]
(a) Sketch \(C\) and state exactly its greatest radius. [3] (b) Find exactly the area bounded by \(C\) and the initial line. [5]
(c) Show that the point furthest from the initial line satisfies
\[1-e^{\theta-\pi/2}-\tan\theta=0,\]
and verify a root in \((0.56,0.57)\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(r\) decreases from \(1-e^{-\pi/2}\) to \(0\), so the greatest radius is
\[\boxed{1-e^{-\pi/2}}.\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/2}(e^{-\theta}-e^{-\pi/2})^2d\theta\\
&=\boxed{\frac14-e^{-\pi/2}+\frac{\pi+3}{4}e^{-\pi}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The distance from the initial line is
\[y=(e^{-\theta}-e^{-\pi/2})\sin\theta.\]
Setting \(dy/d\theta=0\) and dividing by \(e^{-\theta}\cos\theta\) gives the stated equation. Its values at \(0.56\) and \(0.57\) have opposite signs, so the root is verified.



2023 O/N 12

The radius decreases from 1 − e^(−π/2) to the pole.   2023 O/N 12 initial lineyO


The radius decreases from 1 − e^(−π/2) to the pole.




Source: 9231/12/O/N/2023 Q6.




2024



2024 May/June · 9231/11 & /12 · Question 7 · 15 marks
\(C:r^2=(\pi-\theta)\tan^{-1}(\pi-\theta)\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\).
(a) Sketch \(C\) and state the point furthest from the pole. [3]
(b) Find the area enclosed by \(C\) and the initial line. [7]
(c) Show that the point furthest from the initial line satisfies
\[2(\pi-\theta)\tan^{-1}(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta-
\frac{\pi-\theta}{1+(\pi-\theta)^2}-\tan^{-1}(\pi-\theta)=0,\]
and verify a root in \((1.2,1.3)\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

\(r\) decreases to the pole, so the furthest point is
\[\boxed{\left(\sqrt{\pi\tan^{-1}\pi},0\right)}.\]
With \(u=\pi-\theta\) and integration by parts,
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\frac12\int_0^\pi u\tan^{-1}u\,du\\
&=\frac14(\pi^2+1)\tan^{-1}\pi-\frac\pi4.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\boxed{A=\frac14\{(\pi^2+1)\tan^{-1}\pi-\pi\}}\).
For part (c), use \(y=r\sin\theta\) and differentiate \(y^2=r^2\sin^2\theta\). Clearing non-zero factors yields the stated equation; its two endpoint values have opposite signs.



2024 M/J 11–12

A decreasing-radius arc from the initial line to the pole.   2024 M/J 11–12 initial lineyO


A decreasing-radius arc from the initial line to the pole.




Sources: 9231/11/M/J/2024 Q7; 9231/12/M/J/2024 Q7.





2024 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 7 · 10 marks
\(C:r^2=\sin2\theta\cos\theta\) for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi\).

Since \(r^2\geqslant0\), the two loops occur for \(0\leqslant\theta\leqslant\pi/2\) and meet at the pole. They are symmetric about \(\boxed{\theta=\pi/2}\).
\[r^2=2\sin\theta\cos^2\theta.\]

title: 1.7 Proof by induction
text:
重要本节考纲要求



Use the method of mathematical induction to establish a given result.
题目可以涉及有限和、递推数列、不等式、导数或矩阵幂；证明结构相同，但 inductive step 的运算对象不同。




设命题为 \(P(n)\)，起始整数为 \(n=n_0\)。完整证明必须包含：

Base case: 验证 \(P(n_0)\)；
Inductive hypothesis: 假设 \(P(k)\) 对某个 \(k\ge n_0\) 成立；
Target: 明确 \(P(k+1)\) 应是什么；
Inductive step: 只使用 \(P(k)\) 与已知事实推出 \(P(k+1)\)；
Conclusion: 写出由 mathematical induction，\(P(n)\) 对所有 \(n\ge n_0\) 成立。

\[
P(n_0),\; P(k)\Longrightarrow P(k+1)
\;\Longrightarrow\;
P(n)\text{ for every integer }n\ge n_0.
\]









提示Proof template



Base case. When \(n=n_0\), show that LHS = RHS (or that the stated inequality is true).
Hypothesis. Assume the result is true for \(n=k\), where \(k\ge n_0\):
\[
P(k).
\]
Step. For \(n=k+1\), begin from the side that contains the \(k\)-case, apply the hypothesis, and simplify until the target \(P(k+1)\) is obtained.
Conclusion. Therefore \(P(k)\Rightarrow P(k+1)\). Since \(P(n_0)\) is true, the result follows by mathematical induction for all integers \(n\ge n_0\).





If
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}f(r)=F(n),
\]
then the \((k+1)\) case begins with
\[
S_{k+1}=S_k+f(k+1).
\]
Use the hypothesis \(S_k=F(k)\), then show
\[
F(k)+f(k+1)=F(k+1).
\]
Do not assume the target \(F(k+1)\) at the beginning of the inductive step.



For \(u_{n+1}=g(u_n)\) and a proposed formula \(u_n=F(n)\), assume \(u_k=F(k)\) and write
\[
u_{k+1}=g(u_k)=g(F(k)).
\]
The target is \(F(k+1)\). The recurrence, not the proposed answer, must be the starting point.



For an inequality, the hypothesis supplies a bound rather than an equality. Every multiplication or division must respect signs. A typical step is
\[
A_{k+1}=c_kA_k>c_kB_k\ge B_{k+1},
\]
where the proof must explain why \(c_k>0\) and why the second comparison holds.
The base case must use the first value for which the statement is claimed, which need not be \(1\).



If a formula is proposed for \(D^n[f(x)]\), then
\[
D^{k+1}[f(x)]=\frac{d}{dx}\left(D^k[f(x)]\right).
\]
Differentiate the expression supplied by the hypothesis and simplify to the target with \(k\) replaced by \(k+1\).



For a proposed expression \(A^n=M_n\), use
\[
A^{k+1}=A^kA=M_kA.
\]
Carry out the matrix multiplication explicitly and transform every entry into the corresponding entry of \(M_{k+1}\). Do not treat matrix multiplication as elementwise multiplication.




Checking several numerical cases gives evidence, not proof.
Proving only \(P(k)\Rightarrow P(k+1)\) is insufficient without a valid base case.
A correct base case alone does not establish later cases.
The conclusion must state the domain, such as all positive integers or all integers \(n\ge4\).

title: 1.7 Proof by induction
text:
2. Textbook Examples
本节保留教材 Sections 2.4–2.5 的全部编号 Example 2.9–2.13。

Prove, for every positive integer \(n\), that
\[
1^2+2^2+\cdots+n^2=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1).
\]






提示Solution





For \(n=1\),
\[
\text{LHS}=1,
\;
\text{RHS}=\frac16(1)(2)(3)=1.
\]
Assume the result is true for \(n=k\):
\[
1^2+2^2+\cdots+k^2=\frac16k(k+1)(2k+1).
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
1^2+\cdots+k^2+(k+1)^2
&=\frac16k(k+1)(2k+1)+(k+1)^2\\
&=\frac16(k+1)\{k(2k+1)+6(k+1)\}\\
&=\frac16(k+1)(2k^2+7k+6)\\
&=\frac16(k+1)(k+2)(2k+3).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the required formula with \(n=k+1\). Therefore the implication from \(k\) to \(k+1\) holds. Since the result is true for \(n=1\), it is true for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





The sequence is defined by
\[
u_{n+1}=4u_n-3,
\;
u_1=2.
\]
Prove that \(u_n=4^{n-1}+1\).






提示Solution





For \(n=1\), the formula gives \(u_1=4^0+1=2\), so the base case is true.
Assume that for \(n=k\),
\[
u_k=4^{k-1}+1.
\]
Using the recurrence,
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_{k+1}&=4u_k-3\\
&=4(4^{k-1}+1)-3\\
&=4^k+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the proposed formula for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result is true for all positive integers \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Prove that \(n!>2^n\) for every integer \(n\ge4\).






提示Solution





For \(n=4\),
\[
4!=24>16=2^4.
\]
Assume that \(k!>2^k\) for some integer \(k\ge4\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
(k+1)!&=(k+1)k!\\
&>(k+1)2^k\\
&>2\cdot2^k\\
&=2^{k+1},
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(k+1>2\). Thus the result for \(k\) implies the result for \(k+1\). Since it is true for \(n=4\), it follows by mathematical induction that \(n!>2^n\) for every integer \(n\ge4\).





Prove that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(xe^{ax})=na^{n-1}e^{ax}+a^nxe^{ax},
\]
where \(a\) is constant.






提示Solution





For \(n=1\), the product rule gives
\[
\frac d{dx}(xe^{ax})=e^{ax}+axe^{ax},
\]
which agrees with the formula.
Assume that
\[
\frac{d^k}{dx^k}(xe^{ax})=ka^{k-1}e^{ax}+a^kxe^{ax}.
\]
Differentiate once more:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}}{dx^{k+1}}(xe^{ax})
&=\frac d{dx}\left(ka^{k-1}e^{ax}+a^kxe^{ax}\right)\\
&=ka^ke^{ax}+a^ke^{ax}+a^{k+1}xe^{ax}\\
&=(k+1)a^ke^{ax}+a^{k+1}xe^{ax}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the required expression for \(n=k+1\). The formula therefore holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Given
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\3&2\end{pmatrix},
\]
prove that
\[
A^n=\frac14
\begin{pmatrix}
3\cdot5^n+1&5^n-1\\
3\cdot5^n-3&5^n+3
\end{pmatrix}.
\]






提示Solution





For \(n=1\), the right-hand side is
\[
\frac14\begin{pmatrix}16&4\\12&8\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\3&2\end{pmatrix}=A.
\]
Assume the formula holds for \(n=k\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
A^{k+1}
&=A^kA\\
&=\frac14
\begin{pmatrix}
3\cdot5^k+1&5^k-1\\
3\cdot5^k-3&5^k+3
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\3&2\end{pmatrix}\\
&=\frac14
\begin{pmatrix}
15\cdot5^k+1&5\cdot5^k-1\\
15\cdot5^k-3&5\cdot5^k+3
\end{pmatrix}\\
&=\frac14
\begin{pmatrix}
3\cdot5^{k+1}+1&5^{k+1}-1\\
3\cdot5^{k+1}-3&5^{k+1}+3
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Hence the formula holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.

title: 1.7 Proof by induction
section: 3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
text:
3. Cambridge examination questions in the textbook
这里只收录教材 Exercise 中明确标注 Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics 9231 来源的题目。

It is given that \(u_r=r\cdot r!\) for \(r=1,2,3,\ldots\) and
\[
S_n=u_1+u_2+\cdots+u_n.
\]

Write down the values of \(2!-S_1\), \(3!-S_2\), \(4!-S_3\) and \(5!-S_4\).
Conjecture a formula for \(S_n\).
Prove the formula by mathematical induction for every positive integer \(n\).

Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 3, October/November 2014.






提示Answer








\[
S_1=1,
\; S_2=1+4=5,
\; S_3=5+18=23,
\; S_4=23+96=119.
\]
Hence
\[
2!-S_1=3!-S_2=4!-S_3=5!-S_4=1.
\]

The conjecture is

\[
\boxed{S_n=(n+1)!-1}.
\]

For \(n=1\), \(S_1=1\) and \(2!-1=1\), so the formula is true.

Assume that for \(n=k\),
\[
S_k=(k+1)!-1.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{k+1}
&=S_k+(k+1)(k+1)!\\
&=(k+1)!-1+(k+1)(k+1)!\\
&=(k+1)![1+(k+1)]-1\\
&=(k+2)!-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the formula for \(n=k+1\). Therefore \(S_n=(n+1)!-1\) for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





It is given that
\[
y=(1+x)^2\ln(1+x).
\]

Find \(d^3y/dx^3\).
Prove by mathematical induction that, for every integer \(n\ge3\),

\[
\frac{d^ny}{dx^n}
=(-1)^{n-1}\frac{2(n-3)!}{(1+x)^{n-2}}.
\]
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 5, October/November 2015.






提示Answer






Put \(v=1+x\). Then

\[
y'=2v\ln v+v,
\]
\[
y''=2\ln v+3,
\]
and therefore
\[
\boxed{y'''=\frac2{1+x}}.
\]

The result for \(n=3\) gives

\[
(-1)^2\frac{2(0)!}{1+x}=\frac2{1+x},
\]
which agrees with part (i).
Assume that for some \(k\ge3\),
\[
\frac{d^ky}{dx^k}=(-1)^{k-1}2(k-3)!(1+x)^{-(k-2)}.
\]
Differentiate once:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}y}{dx^{k+1}}
&=(-1)^{k-1}2(k-3)![-(k-2)](1+x)^{-(k-1)}\\
&=(-1)^k\frac{2(k-2)!}{(1+x)^{k-1}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the proposed result with \(n=k+1\). Hence the formula holds for every integer \(n\ge3\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(e^x\sin x)
=2^{n/2}e^x\sin\left(x+\frac{n\pi}{4}\right).
\]
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Question 3, October/November 2011.






提示Answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
\frac d{dx}(e^x\sin x)=e^x(\sin x+\cos x)
=\sqrt2e^x\sin\left(x+\frac\pi4\right),
\]
so the formula is true.
Assume that for \(n=k\),
\[
\frac{d^k}{dx^k}(e^x\sin x)
=2^{k/2}e^x\sin\left(x+\frac{k\pi}{4}\right).
\]
Let \(\theta=x+k\pi/4\). Differentiating gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}}{dx^{k+1}}(e^x\sin x)
&=2^{k/2}e^x(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)\\
&=2^{k/2}\sqrt2e^x\sin\left(\theta+\frac\pi4\right)\\
&=2^{(k+1)/2}e^x\sin\left(x+\frac{(k+1)\pi}{4}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Therefore the formula holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.

title: 1.7 Proof by induction
text:
4. Past-paper question bank
完全相同的地区版本合并为一题，并列出全部来源。答案保留 base case、hypothesis、inductive step 与 conclusion。

2019


Prove by mathematical induction that, for \(z\ne1\) and every positive integer \(n\),

\[
1+z+z^2+\cdots+z^{n-1}=\frac{z^n-1}{z-1}.
\]
[5]

By taking

\[
z=\frac12(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta),
\]
use de Moivre’s theorem to deduce that
\[
\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}2^{-m}\sin(m\theta)
=\frac{2\sin\theta}{5-4\cos\theta}.
\]
[5]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/19 Q8; 9231/12/M/J/19 Q8.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






For \(n=1\),

\[
1=\frac{z-1}{z-1}.
\]
Assume that
\[
1+z+\cdots+z^{k-1}=\frac{z^k-1}{z-1}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
1+z+\cdots+z^{k-1}+z^k
&=\frac{z^k-1}{z-1}+z^k\\
&=\frac{z^k-1+z^k(z-1)}{z-1}\\
&=\frac{z^{k+1}-1}{z-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Hence the identity holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.

Here \(|z|=1/2<1\), so the infinite geometric series gives

\[
\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}z^m=\frac1{1-z}.
\]
Taking imaginary parts and applying de Moivre’s theorem,
\[
\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}2^{-m}\sin(m\theta)
=\operatorname{Im}\left(\frac1{1-\frac12(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)}\right).
\]
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate. The denominator is
\[
1-\cos\theta+\frac14
=\frac14(5-4\cos\theta),
\]
and the imaginary part of the numerator is \(\frac12\sin\theta\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}2^{-m}\sin(m\theta)
=\frac{2\sin\theta}{5-4\cos\theta}}.
\]





Prove by mathematical induction that \(3^{3n}-1\) is divisible by \(13\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Source: 9231/13/M/J/19 Q1.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
3^3-1=26=2\cdot13.
\]
Assume that \(3^{3k}-1=13m\) for some integer \(m\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
3^{3(k+1)}-1
&=27\cdot3^{3k}-1\\
&=26\cdot3^{3k}+(3^{3k}-1)\\
&=13(2\cdot3^{3k}+m).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the result holds for \(k+1\), and hence for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





It is given that \(y=\ln(ax+1)\), where \(a>0\). Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^ny}{dx^n}
=(-1)^{n-1}\frac{(n-1)!a^n}{(ax+1)^n}.
\]
[6]
Sources: 9231/11/O/N/19 Q2; 9231/12/O/N/19 Q2; 9231/13/O/N/19 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
y'=\frac{a}{ax+1},
\]
which agrees with the formula.
Assume that
\[
\frac{d^ky}{dx^k}
=(-1)^{k-1}(k-1)!a^k(ax+1)^{-k}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}y}{dx^{k+1}}
&=(-1)^{k-1}(k-1)!a^k(-k)a(ax+1)^{-k-1}\\
&=(-1)^k\frac{k!a^{k+1}}{(ax+1)^{k+1}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the formula for \(n=k+1\). Hence it holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






2020

Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The transformation represented by \(A^{-1}\) maps a triangle of area \(30\text{ cm}^2\) onto one of area \(d\text{ cm}^2\). Find \(d\). [3]
Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),

\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[5]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/20 Q6; 9231/12/M/J/20 Q6.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






Since \(\det A=2\),

\[
|\det A^{-1}|=\frac12.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{d=15}\).

For \(n=1\), the proposed expression is \(A\).

Assume that
\[
A^k=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
A^{k+1}
&=A^kA\\
&=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\\
&=\begin{pmatrix}2^{k+1}&0\\2(2^k-1)+1&1\end{pmatrix}\\
&=\begin{pmatrix}2^{k+1}&0\\2^{k+1}-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the formula for \(n=k+1\). Hence it holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





The sequence satisfies \(u_1=1\) and
\[
u_{n+1}=2u_n+1.
\]

Prove by induction that \(u_n=2^n-1\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Deduce that \(u_{2n}\) is divisible by \(u_n\) for \(n\ge1\). [2]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/20 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






For \(n=1\), \(2^1-1=1=u_1\).

Assume that \(u_k=2^k-1\). Then
\[
u_{k+1}=2u_k+1=2(2^k-1)+1=2^{k+1}-1.
\]
Thus the result holds for \(k+1\), and hence for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.



\[
u_{2n}=2^{2n}-1=(2^n-1)(2^n+1)=u_n(2^n+1).
\]
Since \(2^n+1\) is an integer, \(\boxed{u_n\mid u_{2n}}\).





Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^{2n-1}}{dx^{2n-1}}(x\sin x)
=(-1)^{n-1}\{x\cos x+(2n-1)\sin x\}.
\]
[7]
Sources: 9231/11/O/N/20 Q5; 9231/13/O/N/20 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
\frac d{dx}(x\sin x)=x\cos x+\sin x,
\]
which is the proposed expression.
Assume that
\[
\frac{d^{2k-1}}{dx^{2k-1}}(x\sin x)
=(-1)^{k-1}\{x\cos x+(2k-1)\sin x\}.
\]
Differentiate twice. First,
\[
\frac{d^{2k}}{dx^{2k}}(x\sin x)
=(-1)^{k-1}\{-x\sin x+2k\cos x\}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{2k+1}}{dx^{2k+1}}(x\sin x)
&=(-1)^{k-1}\{-x\cos x-(2k+1)\sin x\}\\
&=(-1)^k\{x\cos x+(2k+1)\sin x\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Hence the formula holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that \(7^{2n}-1\) is divisible by \(12\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/20 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
7^2-1=48=4\cdot12.
\]
Assume that \(7^{2k}-1=12m\) for some integer \(m\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
7^{2(k+1)}-1
&=49\cdot7^{2k}-1\\
&=49(7^{2k}-1)+48\\
&=12(49m+4).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the expression is divisible by \(12\) for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result follows for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






2021

Prove by mathematical induction that \(2^{4n}+31^n-2\) is divisible by \(15\) for every positive integer \(n\). [6]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/21 Q1; 9231/12/M/J/21 Q1.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
2^4+31-2=45=3\cdot15.
\]
Assume that \(2^{4k}+31^k-2=15m\) for some integer \(m\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
2^{4(k+1)}+31^{k+1}-2
&=(15+1)2^{4k}+(30+1)31^k-2\\
&=(2^{4k}+31^k-2)+15\cdot2^{4k}+30\cdot31^k\\
&=15\{m+2^{4k}+2\cdot31^k\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The bracket is an integer. Hence the expression is divisible by \(15\) for \(n=k+1\), and therefore for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(5r^4+r^2)
=\frac12n^2(n+1)^2(2n+1).
\]
[6]

Hence, using the standard formula for \(\sum r^2\), find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^4\) in fully factorised form. [3]

Source: 9231/13/M/J/21 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






For \(n=1\), the left side is \(6\) and the right side is

\[
\frac12(1)^2(2)^2(3)=6.
\]
Assume that
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{k}(5r^4+r^2)
=\frac12k^2(k+1)^2(2k+1).
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{k+1}(5r^4+r^2)
&=\frac12k^2(k+1)^2(2k+1)+5(k+1)^4+(k+1)^2\\
&=\frac12(k+1)^2\{2k^3+11k^2+20k+12\}\\
&=\frac12(k+1)^2(k+2)^2(2k+3).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the result for \(n=k+1\). Hence part (a) follows by mathematical induction.



\[
5\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^4+\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)
=\frac12n^2(n+1)^2(2n+1).
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^4
=\frac1{30}n(n+1)(2n+1)(3n^2+3n-1)}.
\]





The sequence satisfies \(a_1=1\) and
\[
a_{n+1}=\left(a_n+\frac1{a_n}\right)^3.
\]

Prove by mathematical induction that

\[
\ln a_n\ge3^{n-1}\ln2
\]
for every integer \(n\ge2\). [6]

Show that

\[
\ln a_{n+1}-\ln a_n>3^{n-1}\ln4
\]
for \(n\ge2\). [2]
Sources: 9231/11/O/N/21 Q3; 9231/13/O/N/21 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






Since \(a_2=(1+1)^3=8\),

\[
\ln a_2=3\ln2=3^{2-1}\ln2.
\]
Assume that \(\ln a_k\ge3^{k-1}\ln2\) for some \(k\ge2\). Since \(a_k>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ln a_{k+1}
&=3\ln\left(a_k+\frac1{a_k}\right)\\
&>3\ln a_k\\
&\ge3^k\ln2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the result holds for \(k+1\), and hence for every integer \(n\ge2\) by mathematical induction.



\[
\begin{aligned}
\ln a_{n+1}-\ln a_n
&=3\ln\left(a_n+\frac1{a_n}\right)-\ln a_n\\
&>2\ln a_n\\
&\ge2\cdot3^{n-1}\ln2\\
&=3^{n-1}\ln4.
\end{aligned}
\]





It is given that \(y=xe^{ax}\), where \(a\) is constant. Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^ny}{dx^n}=(a^nx+na^{n-1})e^{ax}.
\]
[6]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/21 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
y'=(ax+1)e^{ax},
\]
which agrees with the formula.
Assume
\[
\frac{d^ky}{dx^k}=(a^kx+ka^{k-1})e^{ax}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}y}{dx^{k+1}}
&=a(a^kx+ka^{k-1})e^{ax}+a^ke^{ax}\\
&=\{a^{k+1}x+(k+1)a^k\}e^{ax}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






2022

The sequence of positive numbers satisfies \(u_1>4\) and
\[
u_{n+1}=\frac{u_n^2+u_n+12}{2u_n}.
\]

By considering \(u_{n+1}-4\), prove by mathematical induction that \(u_n>4\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Show that \(u_{n+1}<u_n\) for \(n\ge1\). [3]

Sources: 9231/11/M/J/22 Q3; 9231/12/M/J/22 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






The base case \(u_1>4\) is given.

Assume that \(u_k>4\). Since \(u_k\) is positive,
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_{k+1}-4
&=\frac{u_k^2+u_k+12}{2u_k}-4\\
&=\frac{u_k^2-7u_k+12}{2u_k}\\
&=\frac{(u_k-3)(u_k-4)}{2u_k}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(u_{k+1}>4\). Since the base case is true, \(u_n>4\) for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.



\[
\begin{aligned}
u_{n+1}-u_n
&=\frac{-u_n^2+u_n+12}{2u_n}\\
&=-\frac{(u_n-4)(u_n+3)}{2u_n}<0,
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(u_n>4\). Hence \(\boxed{u_{n+1}<u_n}\).





Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(a>0\).

State the geometrical transformation represented by \(A\). [1]
Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),

\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}1&na\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[5]
Source: 9231/13/M/J/22 Q5.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






\(A\) represents a shear in the \(x\)-direction, with shear factor \(a\).
For \(n=1\), the proposed matrix is \(A\).

Assume that
\[
A^k=\begin{pmatrix}1&ka\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
A^{k+1}
&=A^kA\\
&=\begin{pmatrix}1&ka\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\\
&=\begin{pmatrix}1&(k+1)a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Hence the formula holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






2023

For \(x\ne1\), prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
1+2x+3x^2+\cdots+nx^{n-1}
=\frac{1-(n+1)x^n+nx^{n+1}}{(1-x)^2}.
\]
[6]
Sources: 9231/11/O/N/23 Q2; 9231/13/O/N/23 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
\text{LHS}=1,
\;
\text{RHS}=\frac{1-2x+x^2}{(1-x)^2}=1.
\]
Assume that
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{k}rx^{r-1}
=\frac{1-(k+1)x^k+kx^{k+1}}{(1-x)^2}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{k+1}rx^{r-1}
&=\frac{1-(k+1)x^k+kx^{k+1}}{(1-x)^2}+(k+1)x^k\\
&=\frac{1-(k+1)x^k+kx^{k+1}+(k+1)x^k(1-x)^2}{(1-x)^2}\\
&=\frac{1-(k+2)x^{k+1}+(k+1)x^{k+2}}{(1-x)^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the target for \(n=k+1\). Hence the identity holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(x^2e^x)
=\{x^2+2nx+n(n-1)\}e^x.
\]
[6]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/23 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
\frac d{dx}(x^2e^x)=(x^2+2x)e^x,
\]
which agrees with the formula.
Assume that
\[
\frac{d^k}{dx^k}(x^2e^x)
=\{x^2+2kx+k(k-1)\}e^x.
\]
Differentiate once:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}}{dx^{k+1}}(x^2e^x)
&=\{x^2+2kx+k(k-1)+2x+2k\}e^x\\
&=\{x^2+2(k+1)x+k(k+1)\}e^x.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the proposed formula for \(n=k+1\). Hence it holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






2024

Prove by mathematical induction that
\[
6^{4n}+38^n-2
\]
is divisible by \(74\) for every positive integer \(n\). [6]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/24 Q2; 9231/12/M/J/24 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
6^4+38-2=1332=18\cdot74.
\]
Assume that
\[
6^{4k}+38^k-2=74m
\]
for some integer \(m\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
6^{4(k+1)}+38^{k+1}-2
&=1296\cdot6^{4k}+38\cdot38^k-2\\
&=1296(6^{4k}+38^k-2)-1258\cdot38^k+2590\\
&=74\{1296m-17\cdot38^k+35\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The bracket is an integer, so the expression is divisible by \(74\) for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result follows for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^2=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1).
\]
[5]
The sum \(S_n\) is defined by \(S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^4\).

Using

\[
(2r+1)^5-(2r-1)^5=160r^4+80r^2+2,
\]
show that
\[
S_n=\frac1{30}n(n+1)(2n+1)(3n^2+3n-1).
\]
[6]
Source: 9231/13/M/J/24 Q4.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer






For \(n=1\), both sides equal \(1\).

Assume
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{k}r^2=\frac16k(k+1)(2k+1).
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{k+1}r^2
&=\frac16k(k+1)(2k+1)+(k+1)^2\\
&=\frac16(k+1)(2k^2+7k+6)\\
&=\frac16(k+1)(k+2)(2k+3).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the result for \(n=k+1\). Therefore the formula holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.

Sum the given identity from \(r=1\) to \(r=n\). The left side telescopes:

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\{(2r+1)^5-(2r-1)^5\}=(2n+1)^5-1.
\]
Hence
\[
(2n+1)^5-1=160S_n+80\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^2+2n.
\]
Using part (a),
\[
160S_n=(2n+1)^5-1-\frac{40}{3}n(n+1)(2n+1)-2n.
\]
Factorising and dividing by \(160\) gives
\[
\boxed{S_n=\frac1{30}n(n+1)(2n+1)(3n^2+3n-1)}.
\]





Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(\tan^{-1}x)=P_n(x)(1+x^2)^{-n},
\]
where \(P_n(x)\) is a polynomial of degree \(n-1\). [6]
Sources: 9231/11/O/N/24 Q2; 9231/13/O/N/24 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
\frac d{dx}(\tan^{-1}x)=(1+x^2)^{-1}.
\]
Thus \(P_1(x)=1\), which has degree \(0=1-1\).
Assume that
\[
\frac{d^k}{dx^k}(\tan^{-1}x)=P_k(x)(1+x^2)^{-k},
\]
where \(P_k\) has degree \(k-1\). Differentiating,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}}{dx^{k+1}}(\tan^{-1}x)
&=P_k'(x)(1+x^2)^{-k}-2kxP_k(x)(1+x^2)^{-k-1}\\
&=\{(1+x^2)P_k'(x)-2kxP_k(x)\}(1+x^2)^{-k-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[
P_{k+1}(x)=(1+x^2)P_k'(x)-2kxP_k(x).
\]
Both terms have degree at most \(k\), and the leading coefficient is non-zero, so \(P_{k+1}\) has degree \(k\). This is the required form for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result follows for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





The sequence satisfies \(u_1=4\) and
\[
u_{n+1}=3u_n-2.
\]
Prove by induction that \(u_n=3^n+1\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/24 Q1.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\), \(3^1+1=4=u_1\).
Assume \(u_k=3^k+1\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_{k+1}&=3u_k-2\\
&=3(3^k+1)-2\\
&=3^{k+1}+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the result for \(k\) implies the result for \(k+1\). Since the base case is true, \(u_n=3^n+1\) for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.






2025

The sequence satisfies \(u_1=5\) and
\[
u_{n+1}=6u_n+5.
\]
Prove by induction that \(u_n=6^n-1\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Sources: 9231/11/M/J/25 Q3(a); 9231/12/M/J/25 Q3(a).






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\), \(6^1-1=5=u_1\).
Assume that \(u_k=6^k-1\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_{k+1}&=6u_k+5\\
&=6(6^k-1)+5\\
&=6^{k+1}-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the result for \(k\) implies the result for \(k+1\). Since the base case is true, \(u_n=6^n-1\) for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that \(2025^n+47^n-2\) is divisible by \(46\) for every positive integer \(n\). [6]
Source: 9231/13/M/J/25 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
2025+47-2=2070=45\cdot46.
\]
Assume that for \(n=k\),
\[
2025^k+47^k-2=46m
\]
for some integer \(m\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
2025^{k+1}+47^{k+1}-2
&=47(2025^k+47^k-2)+(2025-47)2025^k+92\\
&=47(46m)+1978\cdot2025^k+92\\
&=46\left(47m+43\cdot2025^k+2\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The bracket is an integer, so the expression is divisible by \(46\) for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that, for every integer \(n\ge2\),
\[
\frac{d^n}{dx^n}(x\ln x)=(-1)^n(n-2)!x^{1-n}.
\]
[6]
Source: 9231/14/M/J/25 Q2.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=2\),
\[
\frac{d}{dx}(x\ln x)=\ln x+1,
\;
\frac{d^2}{dx^2}(x\ln x)=\frac1x.
\]
The proposed expression gives \((-1)^2(0)!x^{-1}=1/x\), so the base case holds.
Assume that for some \(k\ge2\),
\[
\frac{d^k}{dx^k}(x\ln x)=(-1)^k(k-2)!x^{1-k}.
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d^{k+1}}{dx^{k+1}}(x\ln x)
&=(-1)^k(k-2)!(1-k)x^{-k}\\
&=(-1)^{k+1}(k-1)!x^{-k}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the result with \(n=k+1\). Therefore it holds for every integer \(n\ge2\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\frac{d^{2n-1}}{dx^{2n-1}}(x\cos x)
=(-1)^n\{x\sin x-(2n-1)\cos x\}.
\]
[7]
Sources: 9231/11/O/N/25 Q3; 9231/13/O/N/25 Q3.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\),
\[
\frac d{dx}(x\cos x)=\cos x-x\sin x
=(-1)\{x\sin x-\cos x\}.
\]
Assume that for \(n=k\),
\[
\frac{d^{2k-1}}{dx^{2k-1}}(x\cos x)
=(-1)^k\{x\sin x-(2k-1)\cos x\}.
\]
The next required order is \(2(k+1)-1=2k+1\), so differentiate twice. The first derivative is
\[
(-1)^k\{x\cos x+2k\sin x\}.
\]
The second is
\[
\begin{aligned}
(-1)^k\{(2k+1)\cos x-x\sin x\}
&=(-1)^{k+1}\{x\sin x-(2k+1)\cos x\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the formula for \(n=k+1\). Hence the result holds for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





The sequence of positive numbers satisfies \(u_1<5\) and
\[
u_{n+1}=\frac{6u_n+5}{u_n+2}.
\]
By considering \(5-u_{n+1}\), prove by mathematical induction that \(u_n<5\) for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Source: 9231/12/O/N/25 Q3(a).






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





The base case \(u_1<5\) is given.
Assume that \(u_k<5\). Since the terms are positive, \(u_k+2>0\). Now
\[
\begin{aligned}
5-u_{k+1}
&=5-\frac{6u_k+5}{u_k+2}\\
&=\frac{5u_k+10-6u_k-5}{u_k+2}\\
&=\frac{5-u_k}{u_k+2}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence \(u_{k+1}<5\). Since the base case is true, \(u_n<5\) for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.





Prove by mathematical induction that
\[
\left(\frac65\right)^n\ge1+\frac n5
\]
for every positive integer \(n\). [5]
Source: 9231/14/O/N/25 Q1.






提示Mark-scheme-style answer





For \(n=1\), both sides equal \(6/5\).
Assume that
\[
\left(\frac65\right)^k\ge1+\frac k5.
\]
Since \(6/5>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(\frac65\right)^{k+1}
&\ge\frac65\left(1+\frac k5\right)\\
&=1+\frac{k+1}{5}+\frac{k}{25}\\
&\ge1+\frac{k+1}{5},
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(k/25\ge0\). Therefore the inequality holds for \(k+1\), and hence for every positive integer \(n\) by mathematical induction.

title: 1.7 Proof by induction
text:
5. 完成本节的判断标准

能清楚写出 base case、hypothesis、step 和 conclusion；
能先写出 \(P(k+1)\) 的 target，而不循环论证；
级数题会加入第 \((k+1)\) 项；
递推、导数和矩阵题会从定义或 recurrence 开始；
不等式题会说明每次比较的方向和适用条件。

title: 2.2 Matrices
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

把三个未知数、三个线性方程组的求解问题写成矩阵方程，或反过来把矩阵方程写成方程组；
理解方程组一致与不一致的各种情形，联系系数矩阵的 singular/non-singular 性质，解一致方程组，并从直线和平面的角度作出几何解释；
理解 square matrix 的 characteristic equation、eigenvalue 与 eigenvector 的含义，并用定义 \(A\mathbf e=\lambda\mathbf e\) 证明简单性质（例如 \(\lambda^n\) 是 \(A^n\) 的特征值）；
求 \(2\times2\) 与 \(3\times3\) 矩阵的特征值和特征向量（只要求实且互异的特征值）；
把方阵写成 \(QDQ^{-1}\)，其中 \(D\) 是以特征值为对角元的对角矩阵，\(Q\) 的列是对应特征向量，并利用该形式计算矩阵幂；
使用方阵满足自身特征方程这一事实（仅限 \(2\times2\)、\(3\times3\) 矩阵）。

title: 2.2 Matrices
text:
学习路线


能把三元一次方程组写成 \(M\mathbf x=\mathbf b\)，并先检查 \(\det M\) 是否为零
能区分三平面交于一点、交于一条直线（sheaf）、重合以及无公共点（含 parallel planes 与 triangular prism）
能从 \(A\mathbf e=\lambda\mathbf e\) 出发解释 eigenvalue 与 eigenvector 的几何意义
能写出 characteristic equation \(\det(A-\lambda I)=0\) 并求实特征值
能对每个特征值解 \((A-\lambda I)\mathbf e=0\) 求特征向量
能构造 \(Q\)、\(D\) 使 \(A=QDQ^{-1}\)，并计算 \(A^n\)
会用 \(A\) 满足自身特征方程来化简矩阵多项式或求 \(A^{-1}\)

title: 2.2 Matrices
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Solving simultaneous linear equations: with unique solutions
三个未知数、三个方程的线性方程组
\[
a_1x+b_1y+c_1z=d_1,\quad
a_2x+b_2y+c_2z=d_2,\quad
a_3x+b_3y+c_3z=d_3
\]
可以写成矩阵方程
\[
M\mathbf x=\mathbf b,
\]
其中 \(M\) 是系数矩阵，\(\mathbf x=(x,y,z)^{\mathsf T}\)。若 \(\det M\ne0\)，则 \(M\) non-singular，存在唯一解
\[
\mathbf x=M^{-1}\mathbf b.
\]
求 \(3\times3\) 逆矩阵时，先求余子式（co-factors）、代数余子式矩阵及其转置（adjugate matrix），再除以 \(\det M\)。


1.2 Geometrical interpretation: three planes
三个方程对应三个平面，解的几何情形由 \(\det M\) 与平面之间的位置关系决定：

\(\det M\ne0\)：三平面交于唯一一点；
\(\det M=0\) 且有解：三平面共线交于一条直线（sheaf of planes），或三平面重合；
\(\det M=0\) 且无解：如三平面构成 triangular prism，或存在平行平面。

判别方法：先看 \(\det M\)；再看有无平面平行（法向量成比例）；若平行则检查是否相同；最后检查能否由两个平面的线性组合得到第三个（左右两边同时成立则为 sheaf，仅系数成立则为 prism）。


1.3 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
若 \(M\mathbf e=\lambda\mathbf e\) 且 \(\mathbf e\ne\mathbf0\)，则 \(\lambda\) 是 \(M\) 的 eigenvalue，\(\mathbf e\) 是对应的 eigenvector。几何上，\(M\) 把方向 \(\mathbf e\) 上的向量放大 \(\lambda\) 倍（invariant line 上的缩放）。
特征方程为
\[
\boxed{\det(M-\lambda I)=0}.
\]
特征值 \(\lambda\) 的全体非零特征向量（连同零向量）构成对应特征子空间。若 \(M\mathbf e=\lambda\mathbf e\)，则
\[
M^2\mathbf e=\lambda^2\mathbf e,\qquad
M^n\mathbf e=\lambda^n\mathbf e.
\]


1.4 Diagonalisation and powers of matrices
若 \(3\times3\) 矩阵 \(M\) 有互异的实特征值 \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\) 与对应特征向量 \(\mathbf e_1,\mathbf e_2,\mathbf e_3\)，令
\[
Q=\bigl(\mathbf e_1\ \mathbf e_2\ \mathbf e_3\bigr),
\qquad
D=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3),
\]
则 \(Q\) non-singular 且
\[
\boxed{M=QDQ^{-1}}.
\]
于是
\[
\boxed{M^n=QD^nQ^{-1}}.
\]
计算矩阵幂时，只需把每个特征值取 \(n\) 次幂，再乘回 \(Q\) 与 \(Q^{-1}\)。


1.5 The characteristic equation
Cayley–Hamilton 定理（本课程范围内）：每个方阵满足自己的特征方程。若特征方程为
\[
\lambda^3+p\lambda^2+q\lambda+r=0,
\]
则
\[
M^3+pM^2+qM+rI=O.
\]
这一结果可用来化简 \(M\) 的高次幂；若 \(r\ne0\)，两边左乘 \(M^{-1}\) 还可以把 \(M^{-1}\) 表示成 \(M^2\)、\(M\) 与 \(I\) 的线性组合。

title: 2.2 Matrices
text:
2. Textbook Examples

Example 1 · Page 21
You invest a total of \(\$22000\) in three different funds:

Fund \(x\) offers \(4\%\) interest per year with low risk.
Fund \(y\) offers \(5\%\) interest per year with medium risk.
Fund \(z\) offers \(10\%\) interest per year with high risk.
Fund \(z\) appears more promising than fund \(y\), so you invest three times more with \(z\) than with \(y\).

In the first year you earn a total of \(\$1450\) in interest, but you forget how much you invested in \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\). Work out what your initial investments were.


Show solution

The information can be written as
\[
x+y+z=22000,\qquad 0.04x+0.05y+0.1z=1450,\qquad 3y=z,
\]
or
\[
4x+5y+10z=145000,\qquad 3y-z=0.
\]
In matrix form,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\4&5&10\\0&3&-1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}22000\\145000\\0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The inverse of the coefficient matrix is
\[
M^{-1}=-\frac1{19}
\begin{pmatrix}-35&4&5\\4&-1&-6\\12&-3&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}
=-\frac1{19}
\begin{pmatrix}-35&4&5\\4&-1&-6\\12&-3&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}22000\\145000\\0\end{pmatrix}
=\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}8000\\3000\\9000\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
So the initial investments were \(\$8000\) in \(x\), \(\$3000\) in \(y\) and \(\$9000\) in \(z\).

 Completed


Example 2 · Page 27
Determine the nature of the intersection of the following planes. If they have a solution, state clearly the solution as a single point or the equation of the line or the equation of the plane of intersection.
\[
\Pi_1:-x+2y=8,\qquad
\Pi_2:2x+3y-z=23,\qquad
\Pi_3:-x+4y-2z=26.
\]


Show solution

Write the left-hand side as a matrix:
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2&0\\2&3&-1\\-1&4&-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Calculating the determinant using the first row,
\[
\det M=-1\bigl(3(-2)-(-1)(4)\bigr)-2\bigl(2(-2)-(-1)(-1)\bigr)+0=12.
\]
As \(\det M\ne0\), the planes meet at a unique point. Solving
\[
M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}8\\23\\26\end{pmatrix}
\]
gives
\[
\boxed{x=2,\quad y=5,\quad z=-4}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3 · Page 28
Determine whether or not the following planes have any solution, and state the configuration of the planes.
\[
\Pi_1:3x+3y+4z=6,\qquad
\Pi_2:x+z=1,\qquad
\Pi_3:-6x+3y-5z=-3.
\]


Show solution

This can be written as
\[
\begin{pmatrix}3&3&4\\1&0&1\\-6&3&-5\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}6\\1\\-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is
\[
\det M=3\bigl(0(-5)-1(3)\bigr)-0+3\bigl(1(3)-1(4)\bigr)=0.
\]
So there is not a unique solution. None of the planes is parallel (no left-hand sides are scalar multiples), so the configuration is either a triangular prism or a sheaf.
By inspecting the equations, \(7\Pi_1+\Pi_3=\Pi_2\) for both the left-hand sides and the right-hand sides:
\[
7(3x+3y+4z)+(-6x+3y-5z)=15x+24y+23z,
\]
and
\[
7(6)+(-3)=39.
\]
This confirms the planes form a sheaf. Let \(z=\lambda\). From \(\Pi_2\), \(x=1-\lambda\). Substituting into \(\Pi_1\),
\[
3(1-\lambda)+3y+4\lambda=6
\;\Longrightarrow\;
y=1-\frac{\lambda}3.
\]
Hence the line of intersection is
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-\frac13\\1\end{pmatrix}}
\]
or, equivalently,
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}
+\mu\begin{pmatrix}-3\\-1\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]

 Completed


Example 4 · Page 35
A village has a population of 700. Every person belongs to one of two competing fitness clubs. Each month, Hardrock Gym keeps \(50\%\) of its members but loses the other \(50\%\) to its rival; Pure Gym keeps \(80\%\) of its members but loses the other \(20\%\) to its rival. At the start of January the clubs have 350 members each.
(a) Show that the matrix calculation for finding the following month’s membership is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.2\\0.5&0.8\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}350\\350\end{pmatrix},
\]
and explain what the numbers represent.
(b) How many members does each gym have at the start of February?
(c) Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors for \(\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.2\\0.5&0.8\end{pmatrix}\).
(d) Which eigenvector represents the long-term membership? What is the stable number of members for Hardrock Gym and Pure Gym?


Show solution

(a) The first row gives Hardrock’s members: they keep \(0.5\times350\) of their own and gain \(0.2\times350\) from Pure. The second row gives Pure’s members: they gain \(0.5\times350\) and keep \(0.8\times350\).
(b)
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0.5&0.2\\0.5&0.8\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}350\\350\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}245\\455\end{pmatrix}.
\]
So Hardrock has \(\boxed{245}\) members and Pure has \(\boxed{455}\).
(c) The characteristic equation is
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}0.5-\lambda&0.2\\0.5&0.8-\lambda\end{pmatrix}=0,
\]
giving
\[
\lambda^2-1.3\lambda+0.3=0
\;\Longrightarrow\;
(\lambda-0.3)(\lambda-1)=0,
\]
so
\[
\lambda=0.3\ \text{or}\ 1.
\]
For \(\lambda=0.3\), \((M-0.3I)\mathbf e=0\) gives \(y=-x\), so an eigenvector is
\[
\mathbf e_1=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(\lambda=1\), \((M-I)\mathbf e=0\) gives \(y=\frac52x\), so an eigenvector is
\[
\mathbf e_2=\begin{pmatrix}2\\5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(d) The eigenvector \(\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}\) does not make sense in terms of members, so the long-term membership is described by \(\begin{pmatrix}2\\5\end{pmatrix}\) with eigenvalue \(1\). Since the total is 700,
\[
2k+5k=700\;\Longrightarrow\;k=100.
\]
So the stable membership is
\[
\boxed{200\ \text{members for Hardrock Gym and}\ 500\ \text{for Pure Gym}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 5 · Page 38
Find the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the matrix
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}-2&6&-6\\-11&13&2\\-17&6&9\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

The characteristic equation is \(\det(M-\lambda I)=0\):
\[
\begin{vmatrix}-2-\lambda&6&-6\\-11&13-\lambda&2\\-17&6&9-\lambda\end{vmatrix}=0.
\]
Expanding gives
\[
\lambda^3-20\lambda^2+25\lambda+750=0
\;\Longrightarrow\;
(\lambda+5)(\lambda-10)(\lambda-15)=0.
\]
So the eigenvalues are
\[
\boxed{\lambda=-5,\ 10,\ 15}.
\]
For \(\lambda=-5\), solving \((M+5I)\mathbf e=0\) gives
\[
\mathbf e=\begin{pmatrix}1\\\frac12\\1\end{pmatrix}
\sim\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(\lambda=10\), solving \((M-10I)\mathbf e=0\) gives
\[
\mathbf e=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(\lambda=15\), solving \((M-15I)\mathbf e=0\) gives
\[
\mathbf e=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

 Completed


Example 6 · Page 40
Show that if \(M\) has an eigenvector \(\mathbf e\) with an eigenvalue \(\lambda\), then \(M^2\) has an eigenvalue \(\lambda^2\).


Show solution

The properties of eigenvalues and eigenvectors give
\[
M\mathbf e=\lambda\mathbf e.
\]
Then
\[
M^2\mathbf e=M(M\mathbf e)=M(\lambda\mathbf e)=\lambda(M\mathbf e)=\lambda^2\mathbf e.
\]
So \(\lambda^2\) is an eigenvalue of \(M^2\), with the same eigenvector \(\mathbf e\).

 Completed


Example 7 · Page 45
Given the matrix
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}-3&2&-2\\-3&2&-15\\1&-1&15\end{pmatrix},
\]
(a) find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of \(A\);
(b) find a non-singular matrix \(Q\) and a diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(A=QDQ^{-1}\).


Show solution

(a) The characteristic equation is
\[
\begin{vmatrix}-3-\lambda&2&-2\\-3&2-\lambda&-15\\1&-1&15-\lambda\end{vmatrix}=0,
\]
which expands to
\[
2\lambda^3-\lambda^2-2\lambda+1=0
\;\Longrightarrow\;
(\lambda-1)(\lambda+1)(2\lambda-1)=0.
\]
So
\[
\boxed{\lambda=-1,\ \tfrac12,\ 1}.
\]
For \(\lambda=-1\), \((A+I)\mathbf e=0\) gives \(x=y\), so
\[
\mathbf e_1=\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(\lambda=\frac12\), \((A-\frac12 I)\mathbf e=0\) gives \(y=z\), so
\[
\mathbf e_2=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(\lambda=1\), \((A-I)\mathbf e=0\) gives \(z=-2x\), so
\[
\mathbf e_3=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Taking the eigenvectors as columns,
\[
Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&-2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Q^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&1\\-2&2&-1\\-1&1&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
and
\[
D=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0&0\\0&\frac12&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{A=QDQ^{-1}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 8 · Page 47
Given
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}-2&2&0\\1&1&-2\\0&2&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
(a) show that the characteristic equation for \(M\) is
\[
\lambda^3+2\lambda^2+\lambda+4=0;
\]
(b) verify that \(M\) satisfies its own characteristic equation;
(c) use the result to find \(M^{-1}\).


Show solution

(a) The characteristic equation is \(\det(M-\lambda I)=0\):
\[
\begin{vmatrix}-2-\lambda&2&0\\1&1-\lambda&-2\\0&2&-1-\lambda\end{vmatrix}=0.
\]
Expanding,
\[
(-2-\lambda)\bigl((1-\lambda)(-1-\lambda)-(-2)(2)\bigr)-2\bigl(1(-1-\lambda)-0\bigr)=0,
\]
which simplifies to
\[
\boxed{\lambda^3+2\lambda^2+\lambda+4=0}.
\]
(b) Directly computing
\[
M^2=\begin{pmatrix}6&-2&-4\\-1&-1&0\\2&0&-3\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
M^3=\begin{pmatrix}-14&2&8\\1&-3&2\\4&-2&3\end{pmatrix},
\]
gives
\[
M^3+2M^2+M+4I
=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
So \(M\) satisfies its own characteristic equation.
(c) From
\[
M^3+2M^2+M+4I=0,
\]
multiplying through by \(M^{-1}\) gives
\[
M^2+2M+I+4M^{-1}=0,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=-\frac14\left(M^2+2M+I\right)}.
\]

 Completed

title: 2.2 Matrices
text:
3. Past-paper question bank

2020


2020 May/June · 9231/21 & 9231/22 · Question 8 · 14 marks
(a) Find the values of \(a\) for which the system of equations
\[
3x+y+z=0,\qquad ax+6y-z=0,\qquad ay-2z=0
\]
does not have a unique solution. [3]
The matrix \(A\) is given by
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}3&1&1\\0&6&-1\\0&0&-2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Use the characteristic equation of \(A\) to find the inverse of \(A^2\). [4]
(c) Find a matrix \(P\) and a diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(A^5=PDP^{-1}\). [7]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The system fails to have a unique solution exactly when \(\det M=0\):
\[
\begin{vmatrix}3&1&1\\a&6&-1\\0&a&-2\end{vmatrix}
=3(-12+a)-(-2a)+a^2
=a^2+5a-36=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{a=4\ \text{or}\ a=-9}.
\]
(b) The eigenvalues of \(A\) are \(3\), \(6\), \(-2\), so the characteristic equation is
\[
(\lambda-3)(\lambda-6)(\lambda+2)=\lambda^3-7\lambda^2+36=0.
\]

A=\begin{pmatrix}-2&0&0\\0&7&9\\4&1&7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Show that the characteristic equation of \(A\) is
\[
m^3-12m^2+12m+80=0
\]
and find the eigenvalues of \(A\). [4]
(b) Use the characteristic equation of \(A\) to show that
\[
A^4=pA^2+qA+rI,
\]
where \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\) are integers to be determined. [4]
(c) Find a matrix \(P\) and a diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \((A-3I)^4=PDP^{-1}\). [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Expanding \(\det(A-mI)=0\),
\[
(-2-m)\bigl((7-m)^2-9\bigr)=0,
\]
so
\[
m^3-12m^2+12m+80=0
\;\Longrightarrow\;
(m+2)(m-4)(m-10)=0.
\]
The eigenvalues are
\[
\boxed{m=-2,\ 4,\ 10}.
\]
(b) Since \(A^3-12A^2+12A+80I=0\),
\[
A^4-12A^3+12A^2+80A=0.
\]
Substituting \(A^3=12A^2-12A-80I\),
\[
A^4=12(12A^2-12A-80I)-12A^2-80A
=\boxed{132A^2-224A-960I}.
\]
So \(p=132\), \(q=-224\), \(r=-960\).
(c) Corresponding eigenvectors are
\[
m=-2:\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
m=4:\begin{pmatrix}0\\3\\-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
m=10:\begin{pmatrix}0\\3\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{P=\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\1&3&3\\-1&-1&1\end{pmatrix}},
\qquad
\boxed{D=\begin{pmatrix}(-5)^4&0&0\\0&1^4&0\\0&0&7^4\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}625&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&2401\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/22/O/N/2024, Q8.



2025


2025 May/June · 9231/21 & 9231/22 · Question 8 · 13 marks
(a) It is given that \(m\) is an eigenvalue of the non-singular square matrix \(A\), with corresponding eigenvector \(\mathbf e\). Show that \(\mathbf e\) is an eigenvector of \(A^3\) with corresponding eigenvalue \(m^3\). [2]
The matrix \(A\) is given by
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}-1&3&4\\0&1&0\\0&-2&5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Show that the eigenvalues of \(A\) are \(-1\), \(1\) and \(5\). [2]
(c) Find a matrix \(P\) and a diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(A-2I=PDP^{-1}\). [6]
(d) Use the characteristic equation of \(A\) to show that
\[
(A-2I)^3=aA^2+bA+cI,
\]
where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are constants to be determined. [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(A\mathbf e=m\mathbf e\),
\[
A^3\mathbf e=A^2(A\mathbf e)=A^2(m\mathbf e)=mA(A\mathbf e)=m^2A\mathbf e=m^3\mathbf e.
\]
So \(\mathbf e\) is an eigenvector of \(A^3\) with eigenvalue \(m^3\).
(b) The characteristic equation is
\[
\begin{vmatrix}-1-\lambda&3&4\\0&1-\lambda&0\\0&-2&5-\lambda\end{vmatrix}
=(-1-\lambda)(1-\lambda)(5-\lambda)=0,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\lambda=-1,\ 1,\ 5}.
\]
(c) Corresponding eigenvectors are
\[
\lambda=-1:\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\lambda=1:\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\\1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\lambda=5:\begin{pmatrix}2\\0\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{P=\begin{pmatrix}1&5&2\\0&2&0\\0&1&3\end{pmatrix}},
\qquad
\boxed{D=\begin{pmatrix}-3&0&0\\0&-1&0\\0&0&3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) The characteristic equation of \(A\) is
\[
(\lambda+1)(\lambda-1)(\lambda-5)=\lambda^3-5\lambda^2-\lambda+5=0,
\]
so
\[
A^3=5A^2+A-5I.
\]
Expanding \((A-2I)^3=A^3-6A^2+12A-8I\) and substituting,
\[
(A-2I)^3=-A^2+13A-13I.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{a=-1,\ b=13,\ c=-13}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/21/M/J/2025, Q8; 9231/22/M/J/2025, Q8.



2025 October/November · 9231/21 & 9231/23 · Question 6 · 10 marks
The matrix \(P\) has non-zero eigenvalues and is given by
\[
P=\begin{pmatrix}a&1&1\\0&2a&-1\\0&0&-3a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) State, in terms of \(a\), the eigenvalues of \(P\). [1]
(b) (i) Find \(P^2\) in terms of \(a\). [1]
(ii) Use the characteristic equation of \(P\) to find \(P^{-1}\) in terms of \(a\). [3]
The \(3\times3\) matrix \(A\) has eigenvalues \(1\), \(2\), \(3\) with corresponding eigenvectors
\[
\begin{pmatrix}a\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}1\\2a\\0\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\\-3a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(c) Find \(A\) in terms of \(a\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) For an upper triangular matrix,
\[
\boxed{a,\ 2a,\ -3a}.
\]
(b)(i)
\[
\boxed{P^2=\begin{pmatrix}a^2&3a&-2a-1\\0&4a^2&a\\0&0&9a^2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(ii) The characteristic equation is
\[
(\lambda-a)(\lambda-2a)(\lambda+3a)=\lambda^3-7a^2\lambda+6a^3=0,
\]
so \(P^3-7a^2P+6a^3I=0\). Multiplying through by \(P^{-1}\),
\[
6a^3P^{-1}=7a^2I-P^2.
\]
Using part (b)(i),
\[
\boxed{P^{-1}=\frac1{6a^3}
\begin{pmatrix}6a^2&-3a&2a+1\\0&3a^2&-a\\0&0&-2a^2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(c) With the eigenvectors as columns,
\[
P=\begin{pmatrix}a&1&1\\0&2a&-1\\0&0&-3a\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
A=P\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&3\end{pmatrix}P^{-1}
=\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}1&\frac1{2a}&\frac{1-4a}{6a^2}\\0&2&\frac1{3a}\\0&0&3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/21/O/N/2025, Q6; 9231/23/O/N/2025, Q6.



2025 October/November · 9231/22 · Question 8 · 15 marks
(a) Find the values of \(k\) for which the system of equations
\[
x-y+2kz=1,\qquad kx+y+2z=2,\qquad 2x-y+z=3
\]
does not have a unique solution. [3]
(b) Given that \(k=-\frac12\), show that the system of equations in part (a) is inconsistent. Interpret this situation geometrically. [3]
(c) Given instead that \(k=-1\), show that the system of equations in part (a) is also inconsistent. Interpret this situation geometrically. [4]
The matrix \(A\) is given by
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&-2\\-1&1&2\\2&-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(d) Use the characteristic equation of \(A\) to show that
\[
A^4=pA^2+qA
\]
where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers to be determined. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The determinant of the coefficient matrix is
\[
\begin{vmatrix}1&-1&2k\\k&1&2\\2&-1&1\end{vmatrix}=2k^2+3k+1=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{k=-1\ \text{or}\ k=-\frac12}.
\]
(b) When \(k=-\frac12\), the equations become
\[
x-y-z=1,\qquad -\frac12x+y+2z=2,\qquad 2x-y+z=3.
\]
Adding the first two equations gives \(\frac12x+z=3\), while the third equation gives \(2x-y+z=3\); eliminating variables leads to the contradiction \(1=-2\). Therefore the system is inconsistent. Geometrically, the planes form a triangular prism (no common point).
(c) When \(k=-1\), the equations become
\[
x-y-2z=1,\qquad -x+y+2z=2,\qquad 2x-y+z=3.
\]
The first two equations give \(1=-2\), a contradiction. So the system is inconsistent. Geometrically, two planes are parallel (and not identical), with the third plane not parallel to them.
(d) The characteristic equation of \(A\) is
\[
\begin{vmatrix}1-\lambda&-1&-2\\-1&1-\lambda&2\\2&-1&1-\lambda\end{vmatrix}
=-\lambda^3+3\lambda^2-8\lambda=0.
\]
So \(A^3=3A^2-8A\). Multiplying by \(A\),
\[
A^4=3A^3-8A^2=3(3A^2-8A)-8A^2=A^2-24A.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{p=1,\ q=-24}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/22/O/N/2025, Q8.
